evidence.readmeExcerpt:
dsh-connect-workbuddy

把本机登录的 WorkBuddy 模型接入 DeepSeek Harness，并提供账号池与模型管理。

English · 安装 · 工作原理 · 账号池 · 更新日志 · 问题反馈

一个独立的 [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) bundle 插件。它把本机已登录的 WorkBuddy 账号（**国内版与国际版 WorkBuddy AI 均支持**）接到 DSH 的模型选择器，同时提供账号池与可勾选的模型管理界面。**国内版与国际版是两个并行的供应商（`workbuddy` / `workbuddy-global`），可同时使用**；插件设置卡片以 tab 区分两者，方便统一管理。 ## 功能特性 - **双供应商并行接入（国内版 + 国际版）** —— 国内版注册为 `workbuddy` provider（`GLM-5.3`、`DeepSeek-V4-Pro`、`Kimi-K3`、`MiniMax-M3`、`Hy3` 等），国际版注册为 `workbuddy-global` provider（`GPT-5.6`、`Gemini-3.5-Flash`、`GLM-5.3`、`Kimi-K3` 等）。**有账号的区域其模型会出现在 DSH 模型选择器里**：两边都有账号时两组同时可选，不同会话可以各选一边，互不干扰。**本机没有账号的区域不列出任何模型**（该区域一个请求也发不出去，列出来只会点到就失败）；只要在该区域登录一次，「重新检测账号」或重启后模型就会自动出现——provider 本身始终注册着，因为它的设置卡片正是登录的入口（重新检测在账号池区块里）。模型名内嵌上游积分倍率（如 `GLM-5.3 · x0.79`），与 WorkBuddy 自身模型菜单一致。 - **插件卡片 tab 切换** —— 设置卡片顶部为「国内版 / 国际版」两个 tab，各含独立的账号池与模型管理；每个 tab 的账号、目录、勾选与未保存草稿完全隔离——在一个 tab 里切账号或刷新模型，不会触碰另一边的运行时目录与会话。 - **可单独关闭任一版本供应商** —— 每个 tab 右侧有一个勾选框（默认都勾选）。**取消勾选即把该供应商从 DSH 模型选择器里彻底撤掉**（不是只藏起 tab）：它的路由与「设置 → 模型」页的目录条目一并摘除，启动时也不再为它发无用请求。账号、积分、目录与勾选**全部保留**，重新勾选即完整恢复。典型用法是「我根本用不到国际版」——关掉它，让选择器干净。注意：若某会话此前选中的正是被关闭供应商的模型，该会话再调用会报 `NO_ADAPTER`，卡片会在关闭态的 tab 上明确提示这一点，不会静默失败。 - **模型管理** —— 从上游刷新完整模型目录，逐项勾选启用或禁用；刷新是草稿操作，点保存才生效。上游同时给出积分倍率、上下文/输出上限与推理档位；**图片输入按厂商核验表判定**：刷新时只有厂商文档明确写为原生多模态的模型才自动勾选，文档写明纯文本的不勾，**没有厂商资料的一律按「未核实」不猜**（上游的 `supportsImages` 是平台侧声明，不等于模型能看图，不参与判定）。用户仍可随时手动勾选，勾选状态保存在本地。**每个模型行还有「可关闭思考」（`off`）勾选框**：决定要不要为该模型提供「完全关闭思考」这一档位。默认由内置复核名单给出（上游声称可关闭、实测却对它返回 HTTP 400 的 9 个模型默认不勾），你可以按模型改勾/取消——**取消**用于上游新出现的拒绝模型，**勾上**用于名单误伤、或你已确认可用的模型；首次保存即写入你的勾选，之后不再重算。 - **模型可用性测试（含冷却恢复时间）** —— 限量模型的冷却时间过去只能靠反复试错去猜。现在每个模型行有一个「测试」按钮，直接告诉你它此刻能否使用、不能用时何时恢复。**它发的是一条真实体积的请求（约 25k 输入 token）**，而不是「发个 ping 看通不通」——因为上游的限流**按请求体积触发**（实测约 20k 能过、约 30k 被拒），小请求看着正常、长对话里却可能每次都被拒，那正是「测试通过、实际被限」的来源。**恢复时间的来源**：上游的 429 **不带** `Retry-After` 响应头（也没有 `X-RateLimit-*`），但它把重置时间写在**响应体**里——`{"code":6004,"msg":"…将在 2026-09-30 02:30:30 UTC+8 重置…"}`。插件从响应体解析该时间（并按其声明的 UTC 偏移换算，不受你本机时区影响），因此卡片能直接显示「✗ 被限流 · 2026/9/30 02:30:30 之后可再用」。三处来源都没说时，插件**不编造倒计时**，如实显示「上游未给出何时恢复」。限流**不会**去借月周期包的刷新时间（那会让人为几秒的限流去等几周）。探测在后台发起，**凭据不会传到页面**；结果不写入设置，也不改变你已保存的勾选。 **两点需要知道**：① **它真的花钱**——实测一次报 `credit` 0.02（被限流时直接 429，几乎不花）。因此**只能按单个模型手工点**，没有「测试已勾选」这类批量按钮：一次覆盖整个列表就是一次不可控支出（服务端也据此**只接受单个模型**，多模型请求会被拒）。② 上游虽宣称 1M 上下文，但节流线远低于此；插件按模型的**原生窗口**向 DSH 宣称（3.5.0 起不再默认压到 200K），所以 DSH 很晚才压缩对话——长会话撞限流是这条机制的直接结果。想让 DSH 更早压缩，就在模型行上手动设一个「DSH 上下文预算」上限（可选 200K / 500K / 模型原生窗口）。 - **本机账号切换** —— 自动发现 WorkBuddy 桌面端留下的多个登录凭据，可按区域切换账号；Token 不写入 DSH 设置。 - **对话输入框积分读数（国内版 / 国际版自动切换）** —— 对话输入框左侧工具栏常驻一行可点击的读数（如 `WB CN · 1,072`），**按本会话当前选中的模型自动切换区域**：选中 WB CN 的模型就显示国内版余额，选中 WB AI 的模型就显示国际版余额；用其它 provider 的模型时该读数完全不出现。每 5 分钟自动刷新，也可点开手动刷新。点击读数弹出面板：**按账号列出的余额表格**，点某一行即可切换到该账号（与卡片上的账号选择是同一个设置）；**当前不能用的账号会在行内标出原因**（如「被限流」「积分耗尽」），标注口径与账号池表格一致。面板里的余额只在打开时才去查，因此不会让 5 分钟的后台刷新按账号数翻倍。要关掉某一边，就在卡片对应区域的 tab 下取消勾选「在输入框工具栏显示积分读数」；该区域的供应商被关闭时，读数不显示、开关也置灰。同一个开关下面还有「显示位置」这一行：默认在输入框工具栏（与模型选择同一行），改成「输入框下方」后读数落到轮次/步数/token 统计那一行——装了别的插件把工具栏座位占掉时用得上。 - **账号池：多账号批量操作与自动换号** —— 把要用的账号勾进池子，即可**一键签到所有账号**、**一键测试所有账号 × 你指定的模型**（默认挑该区域倍率为 0 的免费模型）；开启**启用账号池**即同时打开**自动换号**——某个请求在上游失败时，插件会依次用池内其他可用账号重试，直到有一个接手、或全部不可用为止，然后才把错误报给你。成员**默认一个都不含**、必须显式勾选（「本机有登录」不等于「要拿它去签到和花积分」）；**开启后由池子的排序决定每一次请求用谁**（可用优先，其次快过期先花、积分高、凭据更新的）；失败时依次用池内其他可用账号重试。排序**从不写回你保存的选择**——关掉开关，你选定的账号立刻完全生效。只有请求本身不合法（HTTP 400）不换号：同一个请求体换谁都是 400，重试只会白等。**这个开关只管「插件要不要自己决定」**：关掉它，插件不再替你选账号、也不再替你换号，但**签到与测试仍然可用**（它们是手动动作）。测试走的是与模型行同一套真实体积探测，因此**有真实成本**；**不提供自动签到**——签到会真实领取奖励，只在你点按钮时执行。详见[账号池](#账号池)。 - **凭据失效时给出可执行的建议** —— 上游拒绝当前账号的 token 时，插件会**实际探测**本机其他账号：若有账号仍然可用，就直接告诉你「切换到它即可」（并附一键切换），而不是笼统地让你重新登录——被钉在一个作废的旧备份上时，重新登录并不能解决问题。只有本机确实没有别的账号可切换时，才会提示重新登录。 - **扫码添加账号、批量导入导出、逐账号测试/删除** —— 不必先装 WorkBuddy 桌面 App：卡片里的「扫码添加账号」（国际版为「网页登录」——那边是浏览器登录页，没有二维码）点开即弹出对话框，并在浏览器里**自动打开**授权页；被浏览器拦截时对话框内提供链接、复制与「重新打开页面」兜底。所有凭据统一落到插件自己的凭据库（`$DSH_HOME/workbuddy-vault//.json`，一账号一文件），**桌面 App 的认证文件始终只读、永不被改动**。账号表格每一行右侧有「测试」与「删除」：测试与批量测试走同一套探测，结果可比；删除只删插件自己存的那份，并把这个账号**暂时隐藏**：删掉后立刻消失，也不会被自动轮询带回来；点「重新检测账号」即可找回（重新登录或导入同一账号也会清除隐藏记录）。**桌面 App 的登录始终不动**——删除是「本插件不再列出它」，不是退出 App 登录。「导出 / 导入账号」可把凭据搬到另一台机器：多选导出 JSON → 选文件后先看**脱敏预览**（只显示字段与是否有 token，明文不进预览）→ 勾选导入。导入按账号去重覆盖，**只有确认属于该区域**的记录才入库，认不出的域名会被跳过并如实计入「已跳过」。详见[账号池](#账号池)。 - **积分信息在账号池里** —— 成员表逐账号显示剩余积分与最近到期时间，排序的第二键就是积分（谁多谁优先）。查询是**只读**的、不消耗积分。 - **凭据路径多候选** —— macOS / Windows / Linux 逐一探测默认位置，也支持环境变量与卡片内直接指定。**未登录时卡片会列出「探测过哪些路径、各自为什么没成」**：五档原因（不存在 / 读不了 / 没有可用 token / 字段已加密且拿不到密钥 / 属于另一个地区）分开呈现，因此「已经登录了、但桌面 App 不在场」这种最容易误判的情况会明说需要 App 在场，而不是叫你重新登录一次。**属于另一个地区**那一档尤其不同：登录信息是真实可用的，只是挂在另一个标签页下，卡片会直接给出结论「切换标签页即可，不用重新登录」。列表只讲一次——提示段落说结论，折叠列表给路径细节，两处不重复同一件事。 - **安全 loopback shim** —— 每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret，真实 WorkBuddy token 不交给 pi-ai。 - **命令行诊断** —— `status` / `doctor` / `logout`，按区域报告登录与积分，无需浏览器即可确认宿主状态。 ## 工作原理 ```text DSH PiAiAdapter（每个 provider 一套） -> 安全 loopback shim（每区域一个随机端口 + 进程内随机 secret） -> WorkBuddyUpstreamClient -> 国内版 https://copilot.tencent.com/v2/chat/completions -> 国际版 https://www.workbuddy.ai/v2/chat/completions -> WorkBuddy SSE -> DSH 本地执行工具并回传结果 ``` 国内版与国际版各持一套完整的运行时栈——凭据 store、模型 catalog、回环 shim、adapter——按凭据域名（`workbuddy.ai` / `codebuddy.ai` → 国际版，其余 → 国内版）隔离可见账号，所以**两个区域的账号可以同时在线、同时被不同会话使用**。国际版有两个品牌域名：桌面端登录在 `workbuddy.ai`，CodeBuddy CLI 登录在 `codebuddy.ai`，两者都是国际版。 模型目录按区域取自各自的正确来源，两者都是 **App 自己读的那份** `/v3/config`，区别只在用哪个客户端身份去取：国内版用 CodeBuddy CLI 的 User-Agent，国际版用桌面端 User-Agent（配置服务按客户端渠道返回不同清单；国内版只有 CLI 渠道的清单里带免费的 `hy4-preview-f`，国际版则必须用桌面端才能取到账号真实的 20 个模型，含免费的 `deepseek-v4.1-flash`）。国内版若 `/v3/config` 取不到，会退回旧的 `/v2/enterprises/personal/models` 并记一条日志——那份旧名册是 CLI 渠道的，同名槽位挂着付费的 `hy4-preview`（`x0.29`）而不是 App 显示的免费 `hy4-preview-f`（`x0.00`），所以只在降级时使用。积分概览走 `https://www.codebuddy.cn/v2/billing/meter/get-user-resource`（国际版账号自动路由到其凭据所属的国际网关，`workbuddy.ai` 或 `codebuddy.ai`——两个品牌域名的凭据互不通用），均为只读接口。 凭据读取自 WorkBuddy 桌面 App 自身的 auth 文件（只读）；刷新得到的 token 按区域存放在 `$DSH_HOME/.workbuddy-auth.cn.json` 与 `$DSH_HOME/.workbuddy-auth.global.json`（双账号同时在线互不覆盖；旧的单文件 `.workbuddy-auth.json` 作为迁移来源保留读取），桌面端文件永不被写入。 **加密凭据字段**：新版桌面端（Windows 先行）把 auth 文件里的 `accessToken` / `refreshToken` 从纯字符串改为 `{"$wbEncrypted":1,"envelope":"…"}` 的 AES-256-GCM 信封，**账号昵称 `nickname` 同样被加密**（不解密就会退回成一串 uin 数字）。信封用的是 App **自身构建期内置**的字段密钥，并非用户密钥，因此插件不内置任何密钥副本，而是在需要时用 `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE` 调用已安装 App 的原生绑定（`electron_browser_workbuddy_storage.loggerGet()`）取回同一份载荷并就地派生密钥——也就是「向写下这个文件的那个构建本身询问」。密钥只在本进程内存中缓存，不落盘、不进日志；纯字符串文件（macOS 与旧版 Windows）走原路径，一次子进程都不会启动。其中的 `account.phoneNumber` 虽同样加密，插件**不读取也不显示**。若 App 安装在非常规位置，用 `WORKBUDDY_APP_EXECUTABLE` 指定其可执行文件。 ## 账号池

一台机器上往往登录过多个 WorkBuddy 账号。**账号池**把这件事收成一次点击：把要用的账号勾进池子，然后「一键签到所有账号」或「一键测试所有账号」；再打开**启用账号池**，插件就会在请求失败时自动换号接着跑。 **每个区域（国内版 / 国际版）各有独立的一池**：成员与目标模型互不影响——两边的账号本来就属于不同的上游栈。**签到只有国内版有**：海外区域不显示签到按钮，也没有那一列。 ### 自动换号（开启账号池即生效） - **谁来服务由排序决定**：开启账号池后，**每一次请求**都发给池子里排序最靠前的可用账号——所以「当前使用」显示的是排序的结果，不一定是你手动选的那个。排序规则见下一节。 - **失败时继续往下试**：某个请求在上游失败时，插件会**依次**用池内其他可用账号重试，直到有一个接手、或全部不可用为止；全部失败才把错误报出来（并在错误里注明尝试过几个账号）。 - **哪些失败会换号**：429 限流、402 无积分、401 凭据失效、502 网关/网络——这些都是**某个账号**的状态，换一个账号很可能就过了。 - **哪些不会**：请求本身不合法（HTTP 400）。同一个请求体换哪个账号都是同样的 400，重试只是让用户多等几轮才看到同一个错误。**流中途断开也不会重试**——字节已经发出去了，重放会让客户端看到两段拼接的回答。 - **已知不可用的账号会被跳过**：正在限流冷却期内、或凭据已被上游拒绝的成员不会参与（这也是「一键测试」的意义：测试结果直接决定谁能被选中）。**从没测试过的账号按「默认可用」参与**——刚发现的登录不该因为「还没测」就被排除。 - **手动选择不会被改写**：池子通过运行时覆盖决定「谁服务」，**从不写回你保存的选择**；关闭账号池，你选定的账号立刻完全恢复生效。这也是为什么卡片要显示「当前使用」——它可能不是你在上面选的那个，而你应该看得出来。 - **失败会被记下来**：某个请求撞上失败时，插件把这次失败写成该账号的测量（含上游报文里给出的重置时间），所以**下一个请求直接从可用账号开始**，不会每次都先撞一遍同一个限流账号。只有需要你手动「一键测试」时才不写测量这件事，从此不成立了。HTTP 400 例外——那是**请求**不合法，与账号无关，记下来会白白闲置一个好账号；未勾选进池的账号也不记（勾选才是「可以花它的积分」的同意）。 - 每次换号都会在宿主日志里留一行 `warn`，写明因何失败、换到了下一个账号。 ### 这个开关到底控制什么 **它只控制「插件要不要自己决定」，不控制「你能不能操作」。** | | 账号池 **开启** | 账号池 **关闭** | |---|---|---| | 谁服务 | 由排序**自动**选出（可用优先 → 快过期先花 → 积分高 → 凭据新） | **你在账号池里手动选**「使用哪个账号」 | | 请求失败 | **自动**换下一个可用账号重试 | 不换号，如实报错 | | 一键签到 / 一键测试 | 可用 | **仍然可用** | | 目标测试模型 | 可改 | **仍然可改** | 最后两行是刻意的：签到与测试是**手动动作**，它们作用于你勾选的成员，与「插件是否自动路由」是两件事。之前把按钮也挂在开关上，导致关掉账号池就**再也没法签到或测试**——而「关闭」本该是「我手动来」，不是「什么都不许做」。 **手动选择账号在哪里**：账号池区块里。**关闭账号池时**，该区块会显示一行「使用哪个账号」的下拉，选定即生效（写回本区域的账号槽，与凭据失效时的「切换到可用账号」走同一条已验证的写入路径）；**开启账号池时这一行不显示**——那时由排序决定，一个改了不生效的下拉比没有更糟。账号的发现（「重新检测账号」）、勾选、签到与测试全部集中在这个区块里，所以账号管理只有一处。 **唯一的硬约束**：池里一个成员都没勾选时，批量动作一律拒绝。空的池**绝不**退化成「那就对全部账号执行」——那是唯一会花掉你没授权过的积分的解读。 ### 排序规则（开启账号池后决定谁服务） 1. **可用优先** —— 被测量判定为不可用（限流未到恢复时间、凭据被拒、连通性失败等）的排到最后，不参与选择； 2. **快过期的积分先花** —— 3 天内到期的积分用不掉就作废，所以**有临期积分的账号排在前面**，**先到期的先排**；两个都在临期时，**临期积分多的优先**； 3. **积分高者优先** —— 在没有临期积分的账号里，选积分最多的。**积分只在有新鲜读数时参与**（卡片轮询、批量测试或保存时读到的那份，10 分钟内有效）：请求路径**不会**为了排序去打上游，否则一页对话就会变成 N 个额外请求； 4. **凭据更晚过期的优先**； 5. 最后按账号 id 收尾，保证顺序是**全序**、可复现，不会因为账号表顺序变化而抖动。 > **第 2 条为什么排到第 3 条前面**（issue #70）：这两条此前是**严格字典序**——先比积分总量，只有总量**完全相等**才比到期时间。而总量几乎从不恰好相等，于是「快过期优先」**实际上从未生效过**：一条「不花就作废」的规则被另一条完全遮蔽，等于死代码。真实病例里，某账号有 **196.4 分当天作废**，只因为比另两个账号少约 1,200 分就永远排在最后，那 196 分必然烂掉。 > > 代价也要说清：这条规则会让**临期 1 分**的账号排到**余额 5 万**的账号前面。这不是缺陷——积分是通用的，不花那 1 分它**确定**会损失；而余额 5 万的账号下一轮还在。唯一的真实代价是临期账号可能不够跑完一个请求，这时由既有的换号逻辑接手。 ### 两个批量动作 - **一键签到所有账号** —— 逐个账号签到。**签到前先查当天状态**，已签到的直接标记为「已签到」而**不发写入请求**（幂等，不重复领取）；任何单个账号失败只标记该行，**不中断整批**。 - **一键测试所有账号** —— 对每个成员发一次**真实体积**的探测请求（约 25k 输入 token；与模型行的「测试」是同一套 `probeModel`，因而同样继承两个实测结论：限流**按请求体积**触发、恢复时间写在**响应体**里而不是响应头），得出该账号此刻能否用这个模型。 **测试目标是哪个模型**：默认是**该区域目录里倍率为 0 的免费模型**（实测国内版当前只有 `hy3` 一个；**不写死名字**，因为上游会改倍率——`deepseek-v4.1-flash` 就已从 0 变成 0.11），也可以在下拉里指定一个具体模型。指定的模型若已离开目录，**手动动作会明确拒绝**（`target-model-stale`），而不是偷偷换一个——你点的是「测这个模型」，换掉就是答非所问。 **成本与边界**：测试是真实请求，指向免费模型时（倍率 0）几乎不花钱，但它**不是零成本的空转**；签到则会真实领取当日奖励。两个动作都**只在你点按钮时执行**——插件**不提供自动签到**，卡片上也不放一个永远点不动的开关。 ### 池成员是显式勾选，默认一个都不含 「本机有登录」不等于「要拿它去签到和花积分」。成员默认**空**，必须逐个勾选（或点「全选」）；**空池不会退化成「全部账号」**——没勾选时两个批量动作直接拒绝，而不是替你把所有账号跑一遍。 勾选是一次**草稿编辑**：点「保存」才落盘，未保存时保存按钮带 dirty 指示；切走或关掉卡片，草稿仍在。 ### 手动选择：卡片上没有账号下拉了 账号**一律在账号池里管**：成员勾选就是现在的账号选择面，「重新检测账号」也在那一块。原先那个「账号选择」下拉在有账号池之后是自相矛盾的——池开启时由排序决定谁服务，它改什么都不生效，却看起来像权威；顶部状态行还可能显示成 A、下拉显示成 B。 所以区域状态行也跟着改：**池开启时不再报出某一个账号名**（多个账号同时登录是常态，用单数说「已登录：A」本身就是错的），只陈述本区域可用、由池决定用谁；**池关闭时才报出那个账号**——那时它确实是唯一答案。状态行旁边的圆点与 token 过期时间讲的是「这个区域能不能用」，和「谁在计费」是两件事，后者由账号池区块负责显示。 ### 账号为什么出池，以及什么时候回来 | 探测结果 | 对轮换的意义 | | --- | --- | | 可用 | 可入选 | | 被限流 | **暂时**出池，按上游给出的重置时间自动回池（上游没说时间就按 30 分钟兜底，**不编造倒计时**） | | 积分耗尽 | 出池，按月周期包的刷新时间回池 | | 连不上上游 / 失败 | **暂时**出池，30 分钟后自动回池——这类结果说的往往不是账号，而是一次网络抖动或上游 5xx | | 凭据被拒 / 模型不存在 | 出池，**只能靠手动「测试」回池**：一个需要重新登录，一个是本区域不再提供该模型，等待都修不好 | 关键一条：**「被限流」「连不上上游」都不等于不可用**。它们恰恰是最值得等的那两类状态——当成永久失效剔除，正好丢掉池子里本来最能用的账号，而且**当池内每个成员都被这样剔除时，池子就没有任何候选，自动换号会无处可去**，你只会看到上游原始报错。 **为什么只有限流/欠费/瞬时故障会自己回池**：这三类要么由上游写明了恢复时间，要么由插件按 30 分钟兜底；而「凭据被拒」「模型不存在」等待都无意义，只能由你手动重测或重新登录来刷新。插件**不再有自动复测定时器**（见下），所以后两类的唯一出路就是手动动作。 ### 保存与草稿：为什么卡片上有两个「保存」 模型管理一个、账号池一个，这是**刻意保留**而非漏合并：两者的草稿域不同，合并后一次写入失败会连累另一边（模型目录写不进去，就连池偏好也存不了）；一个共享的「放弃」还会在一次误点里同时丢掉两份草稿。两边都是**验证写入**——**写不成功不丢弃草稿**，否则用户的编辑就永久丢了。 池里还有一类状态**不走草稿**：探测结果、冷却时间、当前轮换到的账号。它们是**观测事实**，由插件自己高频写入。原因很实际——草稿是覆盖式的，若观测结果也进草稿，你手工点一次「保存」就可能把插件刚写进去的结果**回退成几分钟前的旧值**。 ## 安装 > ⚠️ **版本要求：DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 及以上（当前窗口：`0.1.7-rc.1` ~ `0.2.x` 正式版）。** 自 v2.1.0 起本插件只支持 DSH 0.1.7-rc.1 及以上的宿主（旧版宿主无法通过依赖解析安装本版）；0.1.5 及更早的宿主请停留在 v2.0.15。自 v2.1.2 起上界放宽为 **`<0.3.0-0`**，0.3.0 线被明确拒绝。详见下方[受支持的宿主范围](#受支持的宿主范围)。 ### 受支持的宿主范围 DSH 的随包门禁（`packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts` 的 `evaluatePluginCompatibility`）会逐条核对本插件声明的 `dsh-*` peer 范围；**只要有一条不满足，整个组合包会被跳过**（进入 `skippedBundles`，仅打印到 stderr）——provider 命令行 ```sh dsh plugin --profile exec dsh-connect-workbuddy status # 登录状态与剩余积分 dsh plugin --profile exec dsh-connect-workbuddy doctor # 凭据路径与宿主诊断 dsh plugin --profile exec dsh-connect-workbuddy logout # 清理插件持有的凭据副本 ``` `status` 与 `doctor` 支持 `--json` 输出机器可读格式。 > **为什么这三条命令能在「什么都没装」的机器上跑（issue #47）** > > 该插件把 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write`、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-home-paths` 等一整套 DSH 包声明为 **peer**：由宿主提供，插件不自己带一份。这在**已启动的 DSH 进程内**工作正常（宿主有运行期拦截层负责按宿主安装位置解析这些名字），但 `dsh plugin … exec` 不是那种环境——它就是在 profile 目录里跑一次 `pnpm exec`，子进程用**普通 Node 解析规则**，而 profile 是按 `autoInstallPeers: false` 建的，peer 根本不会装进去。于是这两个包解析不到。 > > 4.3.1 及更早版本会因此在**加载期**直接崩溃（`ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`），且报错文件看起来和命令无关： > > ``` > Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write' > imported from …/profiles/dsh-tui/node_modules/dsh-connect-workbuddy/lib/host-heartbeat-*.js > ``` > > 原因是打包把 `auth` / `host-heartbeat` / `at-rest` / `pi-ai-runtime` 合并进了**同一个 chunk**，`lib/bin.js` 一 import 它，`auth.ts` 里那句顶层 import 就被求值了——连只读的 `status` 也一样。**4.3.2 起**这两个包改为「宿主优先、按需加载」：宿主在场时仍用宿主的那份（保持与宿主共享同一套跨进程写协议），不在场时回落到插件自带的小实现。所以现在 `exec` 在干净机器上可用，`doctor` 也会把当前用的是哪一份打印出来： > > ``` > Atomic writes: built-in copy (host peer not resolvable here; normal outside a booted DSH) > ``` > > 在仓库里跑（peer 齐全）则显示 `host-provided (@deepseek-ai/dsh-atomic-write)`。这条守卫写在 `tests/host-peers.spec.ts`：它直接扫描**构建产物**，一旦 `lib/bin.js` 的依赖图里再出现裸包名就变红。 ## 开发 ```sh pnpm install pnpm run check # typecheck + test + build ``` 本地开发用 `link:` 安装到 desktop profile（改码后重启 DSH Desktop 生效）： ```sh dsh plugin --profile desktop add /Users/dmh2002/DshProject/dsh-connect-workbuddy ``` ### 写脚本调用 `chatStream()` 时注意：它返回的是**信封**，不是可迭代流 ```ts const envelope = await client.chatStream(credential, bodyJson) if (!envelope.ok) { /* 失败：envelope.status / .kind / .message / .detail */ } else { await envelope.response.text() /* 或者按 SSE 消费 */ } ``` **先查 `envelope.ok` 再消费** —— 它返回 `{ ok: true, response }` 或 `{ ok: false, status, kind, message, detail }`，而不是一个可以直接 `for await` 的流。跳过这一步的典型后果是**把失败全报成成功**（`response` 是 `undefined`，读它会抛错或被吞掉，于是「每个模型都成功」）。这条来自 issue #56 报告者的实测提醒，写在这里是为了让下一个人少踩一次同样的坑。 失败信封里的 `kind` 就是本文提到的失败分类（`soft_rate` / `model_busy` / `hard_credit` / `session_dead` / `policy_reject` / `not_found` / `server` / `client`），`detail` 携带上游的 `upstreamCode` / `requestId` / `displayMsg`。 WorkBuddy 客户端接口（非官方开放 API），WorkBuddy 更新后插件可能需要随之调整。 - **账号切换**基于 WorkBuddy 桌面端留下的历史 auth 文件（App 自身的备份产物），并非官方多账号 API。默认行为仍是跟随 App 当前登录；切换账号是显式选项，且历史凭据可能因 App 清理或退出登录而失效。 - 显式选择的账号若在本机消失（App 更换登录或清理备份文件），插件**不会**静默改选其他账号——那样会让账单落到另一个账号上。卡片会明确说明「保存的账号已不存在」，此时重新选择一个账号，或点「跟随 App 当前登录」清除该选择即可恢复。**重新登录桌面端 App 无法修复这种状态**：凭据本身是好的，失效的只是保存下来的账号标识。 - 从 2.0.0 之前的版本升级而来的用户，设置里可能仍留有旧版的顶层 `accountId`（迁移来源）。它只作用于其所属区域，且**该区域被显式清除（`accounts.<区域> = ""`）后即不再生效**——否则清除掉的账号会在下次启动时被静默恢复。卡片会显示每个区域当前是「使用保存的账号」还是「跟随 App 当前登录」：清除后回到的默认账号往往与刚清掉的账号是同一个，没有这行提示就无法分辨清除是否生效。 - **Windows：profile 的配置文件 `cordis.patch.yml` 被占用时，账号改动可能无法保存**。DSH 用「写临时文件 + 覆盖替换」的方式更新该文件，而杀毒软件、OneDrive 等同步盘或正在打开该文件的编辑器会短暂锁住它；重试耗尽后，写入失败**不会**让 `set()` 报错。插件因此会在写入后回读校验：**确认落盘才显示「已清除」**，失败则给出明确错误并保留原来的选择（不会显示一个旧选择默默反驳的假确认）。遇到该提示时，关闭占用该文件的程序后重试即可。 - Windows / Linux 的凭据默认路径按平台约定推导。已在真实 Windows 11 上确认 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\CodeBuddyExtension\Data\Public\auth` 与 `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\WorkBuddy\WorkBuddy.exe` 命中，**其余候选与 Linux 路径仍未经真机验证**；必要时可通过环境变量 `WORKBUDDY_AUTH_FILE` 指定实际位置。 - **独立 CLI（`dsh plugin … exec`）不带宿主提供的 peer 包**，因此插件在**宿主之外**运行时会回落到自带的原子写实现（`src/host-peers.ts`）。它转写了宿主的行为契约（锁文件命名 `.lock`、Windows 的 `EACCES`/`EBUSY`/`EPERM` 重试与节奏），并且只在这两个包解析不到时才启用——宿主内、以及仓库检出里都仍用宿主/依赖里的那份。`doctor` 会报告当前用的是哪一份。详见[命令行](#命令行)一节的 issue #47 说明。 - **加密凭据依赖桌面 App 在场**：新版桌面端（**5.6.0 起，macOS 与 Windows 同样如此**）加密了 auth 文件里的 token 字段，插件需要调用该 App 自身的原生绑定才能取回字段密钥。因此 App 若未安装、被卸载，或安装在探测路径之外（**Windows 上会自动回退查安装注册表**，仍找不到时用 `WORKBUDDY_APP_EXECUTABLE` 指定），加密文件就读不出来——此时账号会显示为未登录，而**不会**退化成读出一个残缺的 token。`doctor` 会报告这项能力是否可用。该密钥是构建期常量，随 App 版本可能轮换；插件每次向本机 App 现取，不缓存到磁盘，所以 App 升级后无需升级插件。 - **App 可执行文件按 bundle 自身声明定位，不按 App 名猜**：WorkBuddy 的 macOS bundle 里 `CFBundleExecutable` 是 `Electron`（不是 `WorkBuddy`），因此插件读取 bundle 的 `Info.plist` 来决定二进制名。国内版 `WorkBuddy.app` 与国际版 `WorkBuddy AI.app` 都在候选内；App 被归入 `/Applications` 子目录（如 `/Applications/IDE/WorkBuddy.app`）时，插件还会向下扫一层并用 bundle id 确认身份后才使用——**不会**因为同名的其他 Electron 应用而误启动它。 - **「未登录」与「登录信息读不出来」是两件事**：加密文件读不出时，插件给出的建议是「安装桌面 App / 用 `WORKBUDDY_APP_EXECUTABLE` 指定其位置」，而**不是**「重新登录一次」——后者对这种情况无效（凭据本身是好的，缺的是密钥）。 - **403「request illegal」（code 11140）是服务端策略拒绝，不是登录问题**：聊天网关有时会按内容策略直接拒绝一次请求，响应体形如 `{"code":11140,"msg":"request illegal","requestId":"…","displayMsg":{"zh":"内容未通过安全审核，请调整后重试。"}}`。此前插件把它归为通用 `client` 错误返回 400，DSH 侧又显示成 AUTH 异常——看起来像「登录坏了」，但**重新登录解决不了它**：凭据本身是好的，被拒的是这一次请求。现在这类拒绝按 403 原样透传，消息里带官方文案、`code 11140` 和 `requestId`（联系官方支持时提供）。写回宿主的 `error.code` 是 `policy_reject` 这个稳定类别（而非数值 `11140`）：宿主按类别决定要不要原地重试，而策略拒绝是确定性的——重试只会白烧预算，`11140` 也不是宿主认得的词；模型行的「测试」也显示「服务端按内容策略拒绝」而非「token 被拒」。遇到时的两个出口：在 WorkBuddy 桌面端用同一账号发同样的内容验证（桌面端同样被拒，说明限制在账号/内容侧）；或切换区域/账号后重试。 - **切换区域会让上下文「变大」，甚至一换区就 `code 11115` 超限——不是网关多算你的钱**：同一份历史在两个区域的计费口径不同，根子在宿主内置的 `@earendil-works/pi-ai` 重放历史的方式。它给每条 assistant 消息算一次 `isSameModel`（`transform-messages.js:68`，判据是 provider **且** api **且** model id 三者全等）：不等的消息，其 thinking 会被**降级成普通正文**（`:88–96`，并不是丢弃），而正文是网关会数的，thinking 走的是另一个字段（字段名两边都是 `reasoning_content`）。**这一点已由 issue #59 报告者的同区增量实测证实**：`reasoning` 不计费，且同一侧自己的工具结果块按本插件实测的 455.5 tok/1k 就吃掉了它全部计费量的 97.7%。本插件把国内版与国际版注册成**两条 provider 路由**（`workbuddy` / `workbuddy-global`，见[工作原理](#工作原理)），而它们是同一个 model id——于是**换一次区，另一侧产生的全部 thinking 就整批从 thinking 桶挪进正文桶**。这就是 issue #59 里「同一份对话历史，国际网关算 1.374M、国内网关算 708K（1.94×）」的成因；反方向切回来则是同一公式的 0.696×。 - 由此带来三个用户可见的后果：换区后 token 计数可能跳 ±30%~94%，**跳多少只取决于另一侧 thinking 的字符数，与历史总长无关**；在**同一个区域内换模型**也会触发同样的降级（`isSameModel` 的 model 那条腿），所以不换区也可能看到计数变化；跳变叠加在宿主当前的压缩阈值（`min(0.8×窗口, 窗口−128000−65536)`）上，就会让本来不超限的会话一换区立刻撞上 `code 11115 prompt is too long`。 - **这是宿主与 pi-ai 之间的一处错配，不是本插件的 bug**：不跨 provider/模型重放 thinking 这件事本身是对的（别家模型的思考过程对当前模型没有上下文价值），错在把 `provider` 当作「是不是同一个模型」的必要条件，而这里两个 provider 字符串指的是**同一个模型的两个接入区域**。 - **本插件已在 4.9.0 起从插件侧绕开它**：两条路由注册的 **model 身份统一为 `workbuddy`**（`src/adapter.ts` 的 `WORKBUDDY_MODEL_IDENTITY`），也就是模型自己声明的 `provider` 字段两边相同，于是 `isSameModel` 成立、换区不再把 thinking 降级成正文。**路由 id 没有合并**——它仍是 `workbuddy` / `workbuddy-global`，各自指向自己的 shim、目录与凭据，所以一侧故障不会带走另一侧，模型选择器也仍是两组。**4.9.0/4.9.1 的这版修复漏了一半，国际版整区不可用（issue #75）**：上面的说法只对 `getModel(provider, id)` 这一条按**参数**查表的路径成立；真正跑聊天的 `models.streamSimple(model, …)` 第一步是 `requireProvider(model)` = `providers.get(model.provider)`（`models.js:351–355`），查的是**模型上盖的那个字段**。于是国内版（路由 `workbuddy`、盖 `workbuddy`）自洽，国际版（路由 `workbuddy-global`、盖 `workbuddy`）在只注册了 `workbuddy-global` 的注册表里查不到，**每一个请求都在发出前就抛 `Unknown provider: workbuddy`**——一次也会失败，且报错里不带任何 WorkBuddy 字样，看起来像宿主坏了。**4.9.2 起改为：每条路由把自己的注册表同时登记上「路由 id」和「共享身份」两个键**（`src/adapter.ts` 的 `modelIdentityKeysOf`），模型上盖的身份仍然两边相同（#59 不回退），而 `requireProvider` 在国际版自己的注册表里也能查到、并拿到**国际版自己的** provider 对象（含它自己的 shim 地址与凭据）。pi-ai 的注册表本来就是 `Map`（`models.js:37` 的 `providers.set(provider.id, provider)`，键取的是 **provider 对象的 `id`**，不是 profiles 映射的键），所以这是注册表原生支持的事；**路由集合、模型选择器、目录与凭据都没有变化**，多出来的那个键不出现在任何 UI 里。回归测试 `tests/issue75-global-provider-dispatch.spec.ts` 走的是宿主的真实构造（`createModels` + `setProvider` + `streamSimple`），并保留一个反证用例固定住旧的失败文案。详见 `docs/audit/ISSUE59-OPTIONS.md` 的「#75 CORRECTION」一节。 - 升级后仍可能看到计数变化的部分：**在同一区域内换模型**仍会降级（`model` 那条腿是真的换了模型，thinking 签名未必对新模型有效，保留才是错的）；**升级之前就录在历史里的消息**带着旧的按区域 id，重放时仍按旧规则降级——这种历史只会越聊越少，不会反过来影响新录的消息。 - 真正的修法仍在上游（让 `isSameModel` 认「provider 等价组」声明，而不是让插件去伪装自己的身份）；插件侧的兜底是 4.8.0 起的 `src/context-rescue.ts`——**一旦上游确认超限，就按块折叠历史后重发**，而不是把宿主要压缩的整段历史原样重放一遍（原样重放正是「压缩请求自己超限 → 压缩死锁」的成因）。想亲眼看到这件事发生在哪条消息上：设 `WORKBUDDY_BODY_REPORT` 抓一次 body 组成报告，它只记计数、不记正文。 ## 免责声明 - # `third-party-backend` — the D-5 dogfood bundle A third-party backend bundle **as it would be published**: written against the frozen `tui.dsh/v1alpha1` `Backend` contribution family and nothing else — no `@deepseek-ai/*` dependency, no `src/` import, no host service. It is never published; `scripts/verify-backend-assembly.ts` installs it into a throwaway profile and drives the real assembly chain over it. What a bundle must get right, and where each piece lives here: | Piece | Why | File | |---|---|---| | `dsh.bundle.patch` | Only an installed package whose `package.json` declares it becomes a profile *layer* (`dsh.profile.bundles`), and that list is what the D-1 assembly reads | `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml` | | package-root `dsh-plugin.json` | The declaration the host admits; it counts only beside the `package.json` that establishes the entry's package root (#1568) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | `contributes['x-dsh-tui']` with `kind: 'Backend'` | The writing surface: `apiVersion` + `kind` + contribution `id` + `name` + `spec` (`spec.id` is the backend id) | `dsh-plugin.json` | | handler export named `backend` | The registry's documented default (`backendExport` is in-tree only, so a declaration cannot name another export) | `backend.js` | | `spec.unloadExport` | Module-level/process-wide pools only; session-scoped resources belong to `session.dispose()` | `dsh-plugin.json` → `backend.js` | | `exports: { ".": "./backend.js" }` | Resolution goes through the entry the Loader's own resolver picks — an `exports` map that hides `./package.json` is fine on purpose | `package.json` | A bundle currently declares one backend: the fixed `backend` export must pass the handler assertion and carry the same id as `spec.id`. Multiple declarations are refused, as are manifests whose canonical projection rejects duplicate contribution identities. Entries awaiting authorization are not probed or loaded. The full field semantics are in [`notes/0009-backend-contribution.md`](../../../tui-profile/notes/0009-backend-contribution.md) and the seam write-up in [`docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md`](../../../tui-profile/docs/plugin-admission-and-development.md) (接缝十四). The published type face is exported from this package's entry (`BackendSpec`, `validateBackendSpec`, `backendAdmission`, …). This fixture stops at the picker: `detect()` says honestly that it ships no runtime, and `open()` refuses. Everything past the assembly chain — detection, sessions, catalogs, the install wizard — is a real backend's own work. `closeEchoPool()` is inert (there is no runtime to close) but counts its calls, and `echoPoolCloseCount()` exposes that count read-only. The regression reads it through the Loader's own module instance, so it observes that the host closes the declared pool exactly once, only for a backend it actually loaded.

# dsh-TUI > An interactive terminal UI for DeepSeek Harness. It ships a pixel-whale > header, live work status, streaming thinking, double-Esc time rewind, a > context progress bar, and a TPS gauge. Zero core changes: it consumes only > DSH's public exports, and is moving from a mounted plugin to an app with its > own entry and composition root, where DSH loads in process as the first-party > backend. Install to enable; uninstall leaves no patches behind. ## Highlights - **Pixel whale pet** — three startup intros, click to wake; freezes after the first task. - **Launchpad and first-run guide** — every ordinary launch lands on a landing page with a **real input box** (big text + whale + quick actions, dropping whole blocks on short/narrow terminals; whale-girl images use a compact native-canvas footprint instead of leaving a large gap before the title; on by default — /settings `launchpad` off boots straight into chat); command completion matches chat: `Tab` fills the input, `Enter` runs the command and clears it. The first run walks a four-step wizard (API key / language+theme / model+workspace / shortcuts), re-runnable with `/setup`. - **Terminal-native UI** — streaming Markdown, tool cards, `/` and `@` completion, `#L12-14` ranges, history search, zh/en UI. - **Task completion notifications** — DSH, Claude and Codex notify after successful live work settles, with no queued follow-up or active goal. The title is “dsh-TUI · Task complete”; the body shows the latest settled reply as a single-line plain-text preview (Markdown formatting removed, up to 200 characters). OSC 777/9 apply an additional 2048-byte sequence budget, including title and protocol bytes, preserving whole graphemes. No reply shows only the title; BEL only rings. `/settings` → Conversation: `taskNotifications` = `unfocused` (default), `always`, or `off`; `notificationMethod` = `auto` (default), `osc9`, `bel`, or `windows`. Auto uses separate title/body fields on Ghostty/WezTerm (OSC 777) and Kitty (OSC 99); iTerm2/Warp and explicit `osc9` use a title prefix; other terminals ring the bell; delivery follows your terminal's notification/bell settings. On local Windows, `auto` resolves to `windows`, the system's native notifications: a task-completion toast. The first toast registers that user's AppUserModelID under HKCU, the toast appears about 3 seconds after the task ends (the PowerShell cold start that buys the no-extra-install route), and for DSH sessions an enabled, active external DSH notification plugin in the running profile makes dsh-TUI yield to it (no toast, no bell); an installed but disabled plugin does not suppress notifications; if that AppUserModelID cannot be written, the notification falls back to the bell instead of going silent. SSH sessions keep the attached terminal's notification protocol in `auto` mode; explicit `windows` still selects the host's native transport. tmux requires `set -g allow-passthrough on` for OSC notifications and `set -g focus-events on` for focus reporting. Terminals without focus reporting need `always`. Replay, cancellation and failures do not notify. Works in inline and fullscreen modes. - **Native cursor** — focused text inputs inherit your terminal's cursor shape, color, blinking, and enabled animation or trail effects in both inline and fullscreen modes. The `/model` picker shows the same cursor during movement between provider tabs, model rows, and effort levels, then hides it after **0.5 seconds at rest**; clipped regions fall back to the model row. The session manager also moves this cursor between the workspace rail, session rows, and search box; typing claims the search caret, and navigation returns it to the focused row. Configure animation and trail effects in your terminal. - **Images** — Kitty/Sixel thumbnails, centered preview with zoom and pan, paste-time fitting, text fallback. Kitty images scale to the reserved cells' physical pixels, including on HiDPI terminals. - **Mermaid diagrams** — ````mermaid ```` fences drawn as Unicode diagrams. - **LaTeX math** — `$…$` and `$$…$$` formulas as Unicode text, fractions and limits stacked in display blocks; `mathRendering: image` typesets block and one-row inline formulas as terminal images on graphics terminals. - **Timeline rail** — every turn clickable; timeline / scrollbar / hidden gutter. - **Side panel** — `Ctrl+B` splits the chat with a panel column once the terminal is wide enough; drag the divider to resize it. All eight built-in panels are enabled by default. The header shows each inactive panel's symbol; hover to see its name. Narrow terminals and inline mode keep full-screen panels. - **Live state** — activity animation, context bar, TPS, cache hit rate, effort, tokens, session cost estimate (main + subagents), Git and session metadata. Context-bar fill follows backend occupancy; colors estimate content composition. Compaction clears obsolete estimates, and missing composition displays a single used block with a measured used count in both hover details. - **One session manager** — `/resume` `/home` `/agentview` `/bg` `⌸`. - **Session workflow** — `/new` `/compact` `/export` `/btw`, model hot-switch, fork, rewind, vim, fullscreen draft editor. - **IDE selection channel** — a VS Code selection lands in the prompt. - **DSH integrations** — presets, skills, MCP, goals, todos, subagents, questionnaires. - **Account sign-in** — the standard profile offers pi-ai OAuth for ChatGPT/Codex, Claude, and Grok (plus OpenAI direct and Meta Muse when available), and Host-owned DeepSeek browser sign-in as `deepseek-account` on DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+. Use `/provider` or `/auth` without another plugin. A profile-only update from a global TUI patch that already mounts `dsh-tui-auth` can still start the official loopback callback listener on demand; fixed-port SSH forwarding still requires the global package to be aligned. - **Extensions** — browser interaction, computer use and more. - **Built for long sessions** — event-driven projection, virtualization, bounded caches. Keys and commands: [Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md). Everything else: [documentation index](docs/README.md). ## Preview
## Featured & Listed Among the community plugins recommended by the **official lead of DeepSeek Harness**, dsh-TUI is the first. Featured by the **DeepSeek Harness official WeChat account**, listed in the [dshfind](https://dshfind.com/en/plugins/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI) plugin directory, and ranked **#7 on [GitHub Trending](https://trendshift.io/repositories/146168) daily** (TypeScript).

## Quick Start ### Windows one-click installer (x64) Download `dsh-tui-setup-win-x64.exe` from [Releases](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI/releases) and run it. Per-user, no administrator, fully offline, and no preinstalled Node or DSH. ### Command-line installation Prerequisites: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) and [deepseek-harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). The `deepseek-official` API-key route needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. On DSH 0.2.0-rc.1+, the standard profile can instead use `/auth login deepseek-account` and select the separate account route through `/model`. Other supported accounts can sign in through `/provider` or `/auth` after startup. The primary compatibility target is DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`. This adapter supports its Shell API, V4 session messages, declarative presets, and profile-backed settings; older supported hosts retain their compatibility paths. See [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md). On DSH rc.2, `/settings` also selects DeepSeek Search / Fetch APIs and edits their endpoint and result limits, supporting custom Loader entry IDs and a masked API key input saved through DSH's credential store. Official Flash model labels show the `1017` release marker while retaining the `deepseek-flash` model ID. `/settings` groups its sections into pages: the TUI's own settings sit under **General**, and plugins that declare a page get their own tab (`Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, or a click on the strip in fullscreen, switches pages; the strip is hidden when only one page exists). On DSH 0.1.7, `/settings` uses the TUI's actual Loader entry ID, including custom IDs. It requires matching profile dependencies with `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` 3.18.3 or newer; an incompatible schema stops TUI startup with repair guidance instead of showing an uneditable settings page. Older hosts keep their legacy settings scope. The `dsh-tui` section of `/settings` is saved in `~/.dsh-tui/settings.json`, shared by every kernel; the first launch imports it once from the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (and an older host's `~/.dsh/settings.yaml`) (see [configuration](docs/configuration.en.md#tui-configuration)). ```sh # Install the CLI and this plugin globally (ships the dsh-tui command) npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui # Start (first run auto-initializes the profile; needs pnpm) dsh-tui # Both `dsh-tui` and the short `dst` alias start the same TUI. dst ``` Manual alternative: `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-harness-tui/dsh-tui`. The repo's `sh install.sh` runs that step and checks the required commands. Afterwards `dsh-tui` and `dsh --profile dsh-tui` are equivalent. > **New-user note**: pnpm ≥11 blocks dependencies with install scripts by > default and reports `ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`. Updates skip foreign-platform > natives — the `@img/sharp-*` packages and the Claude SDK's per-platform > bundles — so only this machine's binaries are fetched. `/update` and > `dsh-tui update` write both settings automatically. An update never installs > the Claude SDK on its own: it enters a profile only when you pick that > backend in the kernel picker, which then installs the pinned SDK for the > running platform. No manual step needed. Details: > [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#pnpm-install-script-blocks-and-foreign-platform-natives). After startup the TUI checks for newer versions in the background. It never blocks the first frame. Type `/update` for a one-shot upgrade. It restarts automatically and resumes the current session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md) for the profile lifecycle, source builds, and troubleshooting, including migration from the former `dsh-cc-tui` package. ### CLI Automation: `dst -p "task"`, `dst run --json`, `dst session list --json`. The independent engine does not load the TUI or inherit its profile/preferences; it uses official DSH headless/services (validated on 0.2.0-rc.2 and 0.2.1-rc.2). `dst cli --help` lists its commands; `dst dsh ` forwards native DSH. See [Automation CLI](docs/cli.en.md) for protocol, limits, resume restrictions, and Node/Python/PowerShell integration examples. | Command | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `dsh-tui` / `dst` | Start the TUI; `dst` is a short alias for the same program | | `dsh-tui --resume [id]` · `dsh-tui update` · `dsh-tui doctor` | Resume a session · update the profile and align the launcher · pre-flight environment checks | | `dsh-tui safe` | Read-only diagnostics, plugin inventory and repair guidance; `safe --rescue` builds a clean rescue profile | | `dsh-tui version` · `dsh-tui help` | Launcher and profile versions and usage; both work even without a `dsh` install | Leading DSH options such as `--dump-config` and `--patch ` are forwarded unchanged; other arguments go to the app in `dsh --profile dsh-tui`. Use `dsh-tui -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes` to send `--resume=sid-1 ./notes` as literal prompt text, without selecting a session or workspace. When invoking DSH directly, use `dsh --profile dsh-tui -- -- --resume=sid-1 ./notes`: the first `--` belongs to DSH, the second to the app. Host options can precede a literal prompt: `dsh-tui --patch ./overlay.yml -- --resume=sid-1` applies the overlay and sends `--resume=sid-1` as prompt text without resuming that session. Safe mode: [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md). ### Importing conversations from other agents (`dsh-tui migrate`) Bring Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversation histories into the DSH session store, then browse and resume them by their original working directory via `/resume`: ```sh dsh-tui migrate # list importable counts per agent (writes nothing) dsh-tui migrate claude-code # import every Claude Code conversation (likewise codex / omp / zcode / grok-build) dsh-tui migrate codex --dry-run # preview what would land, write nothing ``` - **Read-only source**: migration only reads the foreign agent's local store; artifacts are written through the official `JsonlSessionPersistence` backend, so imported sessions are first-class (openable, continuable). - **Idempotent**: one deterministic UUID per source conversation — re-importing skips what is already present instead of stacking duplicates. - **Structure preserved**: user/assistant messages, reasoning traces, tool calls with their results, and the source's context compactions (as native compaction checkpoints) are rebuilt turn by turn; harness-injected machine text opens no turn. An imported session can pick the work straight up. In-TUI browsing: the session screen (`/resume`) shows a tab per agent that has conversations; picking one imports just that conversation and opens it. In-TUI: `/migrate` (optionally `/migrate [--dry-run]`) runs the same import in a child process and reports through the notification flow. CLI alternative: `dsh-tui migrate ...` from any shell runs the same import. Full guide: [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md). - More agents (pi, opencode, …) extend the adapter registry as adapters land; grok-build reads `GROK_HOME` when set. **VS Code**: use the integrated terminal or the `dsh-tui-vscode` extension. See [VS Code guide](docs/vscode.en.md). **Herdr**: run `dsh-tui` in a [Herdr](https://herdr.dev) pane; `idle` / `working` / `blocked` are reported through its local integration API. **Any terminal**: dsh-tui reports `idle` / `working` / `blocked` / `done` / `error` over the pty with [OSC 7501 (Program Status Protocol)](https://www.superlogical.com/rex/docs/build/program-status), so terminals and agentic inboxes that implement it can show what the session is doing; terminals that do not implement it ignore the sequence. Set `DSH_TUI_PROGRAM_STATUS=0` to turn it off. Bare `--resume` (`-c`, `--continue`) reopens the last session of the backend this launch selected. Startup recovery only ever targets that backend: a backend with no last session, or a derived target that belongs to a different backend than the one that actually booted (an unknown backend id falling back to DSH, `--backend` naming a backend that is not installed, a remembered kernel that is not the marker's source), refuses with a clear error and exit code 1 — never a silent cold start, never another backend's session, never a new session. An explicit `--resume ` passes that id to the selected backend as-is. The one exception is safe mode's "retry normal startup": it retries the kernel and session recorded in `last-run.json`, so a record whose backend is gone degrades to a warning plus a cold start — that retry is the last way back. ### Experimental: Claude backend dsh-TUI can also run its session on Claude: the same interface, driving the Claude Code CLI through the Claude Agent SDK. Your project's `CLAUDE.md`, settings, hooks, MCP servers and plugins load as the CLI loads them. ```sh # once, in the dsh-tui profile directory (the SDK is an optional dependency) cd ~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-tui && pnpm add @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk@0.3.287 dsh-tui --backend claude # or pick Claude in /kernel; that choice is remembered ``` The easiest install: open the kernel picker (the launchpad "Kernel" entry or `/kernel`) and press Enter on the dim Claude row — the wizard locates the profile directory and installs the pinned SDK for you; the command above is its manual equivalent. The confirmation shows the exact package and version. Closing the wizard, including clicking outside it on the launchpad, cancels a pending installation. - **Sign-in**: a `/channel` relay profile, your dsh-auth `anthropic` sign-in (`/login`), `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or cloud-provider variables, or an existing `claude login`, in that order. A `claude` on `PATH` is used when present, then one in the native install directory under your home (`~/.local/bin`, or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin` on Windows); every candidate has to launch and report a version, and the SDK's bundled binary is used only when none does. - **Works**: streaming, tool cards, approvals and questions, `/model`, `/effort`, Claude's permission modes (`/permission`, `Shift+Tab`), `/compact`, `/context`, `/mcp`, `/resume`, `/fork`, double-`Esc` rewind, subagents, background jobs, images, `/btw`, and the USD cost Claude reports. - **Not available**: DSH-only commands such as `/tree`, `/preset`, `/provider`, `/workspace`, `/agentview` and `/bg`. One process runs one backend; `/kernel` switches by restarting into a new session. - **Startup**: the screen appears before the session opens, with only a light profile composed (this package plus the profile's third-party plugins); see [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md#known-limitations). The DSH kernel starts from the same entry and loads DSH in the same process behind its first screen; `DSH_TUI_HOST_ENTRY=0` restores the old launch path for every kernel. Details and known limitations: [Claude backend](docs/claude-backend.en.md). ### Experimental: native Codex backend Run your own Codex through `codex app-server`, sharing its configuration, login, instructions, skills, hooks, MCP and native threads: ```sh npm install -g @openai/codex@0.160.1 dsh-tui --backend codex dsh-tui --backend codex --resume ``` Protocol baseline **0.160.1**, minimum **0.144.0**; other versions may show drift. `CODEX_EXECUTABLE` selects a binary; `/kernel` remembers the backend. `codex resume ` can open the same thread after the other writer exits. This is not `migrate codex`, which imports history into DSH. With native credentials, a writer conflict for an idle thread retained by the official background server triggers a reconnection to that server. Managed subscription credentials and `/channel` connections use private app-server processes. Streaming/tool cards, approvals, questions, steer/queue/interrupt, model and effort controls, Plan, `/review`, `/diff`, `/usage`, `/init`, skills and MCP share the existing UI. Async questions open the questionnaire while Codex continues working; answers steer the turn (or queue if unavailable), and dismissing the question leaves work running. **Shift+Tab only toggles Plan**, keeping its underlying permission preset; Full Access requires an explicit choice. Existing Codex settings are respected, not overwritten with defaults. `/login` offers ChatGPT OAuth, a device code or an API key (the last writes to Codex’s own credential store). Relay `/channel` connections take precedence; managed subscription tokens are only injected on first-party routes. dsh-TUI does not write `~/.codex/config.toml` or log out your native Codex account. A provider `env_key` from your own config (e.g. `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`) that the shell did not export is injected from the DSH credential store when the ref is stored there — the active store first, then the default `~/.dsh` one — so keep the key in the store, no per-shell export needed. When nothing can supply it, the session still starts and the reason is reported once as a start notice: Codex itself rejects every turn of that provider. TPS includes hidden reasoning time and excludes tool execution time. Live text estimates are corrected when Codex reports output token usage. Native browsing/archive, fork/conversation rewind (the first message requires Codex app-server 0.160.1+), paged history, images, subagents, polled background terminals, goals and `/btw`/`/recap` use the existing surfaces. `/logout` removes only the matching dsh-auth credential; already-loaded managed tokens require a normal restart, not native logout. The real 0.160.1 app-server passed nine credential-free offline checks and eight daemon-resume checks, with no model turn or charge; real subscription login, credentialed model calls and real-TTY interaction were not run. Only Codex identification/title changes automatically, not palette or companion. Using ChatGPT subscription tokens in third-party clients is subject to OpenAI’s terms. Full instructions and current boundaries: [Codex backend](docs/codex-backend.en.md). ### Experimental: DSH Agent Teams DSH's experimental Agent Teams lets the session's agent (the Lead) create named teammates that share the working directory, message each other and coordinate on a shared task board. It ships with dsh, is off by default, and `/plugin list` advertises it. Switch it on: ```sh /plugin enable @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile ``` The switch enables or disables the bundle in the profile, so it persists across restarts, and on a `dsh --profile` launch it applies at once — running sessions included: the model is told which tools came and went. `/team` appears in Help and `/` completion only once the team service is mounted, and only reports: `/team` (or `/team status`) shows the bundle, the service and this session's teammates. `/team on|off` was removed; typing it points at `/plugin enable|disable`. Turning the bundle off while teammates run asks first, and switching off stops them: the team service releases the teammates still running as it unloads. Inside a teammate session the other teammates' runs are not visible, so the question counts them as possibly running. The team record stays in the session and comes back when the bundle is enabled again. If the running DSH does not ship the bundle (`/plugin list` stays silent), switch DSH to one of the supported lines first (`0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-alpha.5`, `0.2.0-rc.1` or `0.2.0-rc.2`). To install it into the profile explicitly, run `dsh plugin --profile dsh-tui add @deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-agent-team-profile@`: the team packages ship in lockstep with DSH and pin their DSH peers exactly, so the version must match. While a request carries `spawn_teammate`, dsh-TUI drops `subagent` / `subagent_fork` from it, and the team's `send_message` / `list_agents` / `interrupt_agent` / `wait_agent` take the place of the legacy controls of the same names, so `spawn_teammate` is the delegation tool; with the team off the legacy tools are back. Subagents that are not team members (workflow, ralph) keep `subagent`. A teammate shows up as a subagent row, a message between members as a `✉ ` bubble in the receiving session (a teammate's received messages show on its subagent detail as agent messages), and the other team tools as one-line cards (`send_message` with its target and `sent`). The agents dashboard (Ctrl+A) and the agents side panel switch to a team view: each teammate under its member name with `running` / `idle` / `provisioning` / `failed` (a teammate whose turn ended is idle — a message wakes it — not done), the Lead line, the remaining subagents, a read-only task board (status, owner, `blocked`, write-scope warnings) and a banner when the team record was rejected. Limits: the switch covers the whole profile, not one session (a launch without the profile plugin service, or without hot reload, needs `dsh plugin` and a restart); there is no "enter teammate session" yet, and `/export` leaves team messages out. Upstream limits apply: teammates share one working directory, a team lives in one process, and a task owner is never released automatically. ## Keybindings & Mouse `Enter` send · `Tab` complete · `Ctrl+Enter` interrupt and send · `Alt+Up` recall the last message · `Esc` dismiss, double-`Esc` rewinds · `Ctrl+B` side panel · `Ctrl+O` details · `Ctrl+R` history (`↑`/`↓` and `Ctrl+R` are scoped to the current project) · `Ctrl+V` paste · `Ctrl+Shift+E` fullscreen draft editor · `?` shortcuts · `←` open the session manager (DSH backgrounds the current session first). Text, cursor position and staged image attachments on the launchpad or in chat while the backend starts are preserved when the session becomes ready. Press `Enter` after it is ready to send; an earlier `Enter` preserves the draft without queuing it. Opening a new session while startup is pending clears the previous draft and its images. The goal bar stays on one summary line: hovering truncated goal text in fullscreen or split shows the whole objective, and a bare `/goal` prints the full status — objective,

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH Knowledge Core

Persistent, evidence-backed project memory for AI coding agents.

[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-knowledge-core)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-knowledge-core) [![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-knowledge-core)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-knowledge-core)

Coding agents need project context that survives a conversation: architectural decisions, repository facts, and lessons worth keeping. DSH Knowledge Core stores that context in SQLite, with workspace/project scope, lifecycle status, and references to the evidence behind each entry.

Records can reference files, Git snapshots, or sessions. Deterministic retrieval selects relevant knowledge, while on-demand Git checks help identify evidence that has changed. Use the core as an ESM library or connect it to DeepSeek Harness through the optional adapter.

Your application decides what to store and how to use retrieved records. The core does not run an agent, call an LLM, provide semantic/vector search, or synchronize knowledge between machines. Automatic extraction and context injection are optional Harness adapter features.

[**npm package**](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-knowledge-core) · [Install](#requirements-and-installation) · [Quick start](#quick-start) · [Harness integration](#deepseek-harness-integration) · [Configuration](#configuration-and-data-storage) · [Limitations and security](#limitations-and-security)

## Key features

- **Local storage:** SQLite persistence through `better-sqlite3`, with automatic schema migrations.
- **Scoped records:** Facts, decisions, and lessons organized by workspace and optional project, with file, Git, or session evidence.
- **Explicit lifecycle:** Create, update, verify, archive, and supersede records through the repository API.
- **Deterministic retrieval:** Ranked lexical matching with score explanations and conservative duplicate suppression; literal search is also available.
- **Git provenance and freshness:** Capture clean, committed file references and compare their snapshots against the current repository.
- **Knowledge health:** Inspect one record or a batch of up to 16 records without changing stored knowledge.
- **Optional candidate extraction:** Conservative rules extract candidates from direct user messages in Harness.
- **Harness tools and context:** Seven knowledge tools and bounded retrieval before agent steps.

## Requirements and installation

- Node.js 20+ and npm, on a Node major supported by `better-sqlite3`. The locked development/test tooling requires Node.js 20.19+ or 22.12+ on a supported major version.
- ESM imports: use a `.mjs` file or a project with `"type": "module"`. JavaScript and TypeScript declarations are included; there is no CommonJS `require` export.
- `better-sqlite3` is a native dependency; installation requires a compatible prebuilt binary or a working native build toolchain.
- Git is required for source installation and Git provenance/freshness checks, but not for basic storage and retrieval.

Install the library in your Node.js project:

```sh
npm install dsh-knowledge-core
```

If a prebuilt native binary is unavailable, compilation requires Python and platform C/C++ build tools: Visual Studio's C++ workload on Windows, Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS, or `make` and a compiler on Unix. See the [node-gyp prerequisites](https://github.com/nodejs/node-gyp#installation). A separate SQLite server is not required.

Use `npm view dsh-knowledge-core version engines` to inspect the release supplied by your registry. For a source checkout, see [Development](#development). A Harness runtime is not needed to use the core entry point.

## Quick start

Save this as `quick-start.mjs` in a project where the package is installed, then run `node quick-start.mjs`:

```js
import {
  KnowledgeRepository,
  KnowledgeStore,
  retrieveRelevantKnowledge,
} from "dsh-knowledge-core";

const store = new KnowledgeStore(".dsh-knowledge/knowledge.sqlite");
const repository = new KnowledgeRepository(store);
const scope = { workspace: process.cwd(), project: "payments" };

repository.create({
  type: "decision",
  content: "Store project knowledge in SQLite.",
  scope,
  evidence: [{
    type: "file",
    source: "quick-start.mjs",
    locator: "repository.create",
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
  }],
});

const matches = retrieveRelevantKnowledge(
  repository,
  "project knowledge SQLite",
  { ...scope, limit: 4 },
);

console.log(matches.map(({ knowledge }) => knowledge.content));
store.close();
```

On a fresh database, this prints `[ 'Store project knowledge in SQLite.' ]`. The record persists in `.dsh-knowledge/knowledge.sqlite` after the store closes; each run creates another candidate. File evidence here points to the example you saved. It is caller-supplied metadata, not a file-content check or captured Git snapshot.

New records start as `candidate`. Explicit candidates, including this example, are eligible for ranked retrieval immediately; automatically extracted candidates require verification first. After reviewing a record, an application can mark it verified with `repository.update(id, { status: "verified" })`. Use `repository.archive(id)` to archive it, or `repository.supersede(id, replacementId)` to replace a verified record with another verified record in the same scope.

`repository.search(query, filters)` performs literal substring matching. `retrieveRelevantKnowledge()` returns ranked records with scores and explanations, includes workspace-wide knowledge alongside the selected project, and excludes archived/superseded records.

Pass scope filters to `repository.list()` and `repository.search()` explicitly: without filters they can return records across all workspaces, projects, and lifecycle states. For those methods, `project: null` selects workspace-wide records; omitting `project` does not filter projects. Ranked retrieval always requires a workspace and, without a project, selects only workspace-wide records.

The public core also exports `captureFileProvenance()`, `checkKnowledgeFreshness()`, `checkKnowledgeHealth()`, and `checkKnowledgeHealthBatch()`. Health and freshness checks take an explicit `workspaceDirectory`; storing file evidence alone does not capture Git provenance.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Harness["DeepSeek Harness tools and hooks"] --> Adapter["DSH adapter"]
    Adapter --> Repository["KnowledgeRepository"]
    Application["ESM application"] --> Repository
    Repository --> Store["KnowledgeStore"]
    Store --> SQLite[("Local SQLite database")]
```

| Public entry point | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `dsh-knowledge-core` | Storage, repository, ranked retrieval, extraction helpers, Git inspection, health checks, and their TypeScript types. |
| `dsh-knowledge-core/plugin` | Cordis plugin with named `name`, `inject`, `Config`, and `apply` exports, plus a default plugin object. |

The core entry point works independently of the Harness adapter. Git inspection runs locally and does not fetch missing objects or contact remotes.

## DeepSeek Harness integration

The adapter targets Harness `0.2.0-rc.2`. Its optional peer requirements are `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` at exactly `0.2.0-rc.2`, plus `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `~4.0.4` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `~3.18.4`. Use a matching DSH CLI/runtime, pnpm, and a configured profile. Compatibility with other Harness releases is not established.

The package exports the adapter at `dsh-knowledge-core/plugin`. Its `dsh.bundle.patch` points to [cordis.patch.yml](cordis.patch.yml), which retains the plugin ID `dsh-knowledge` and registration name `dsh-knowledge/plugin`. Install under the `dsh-knowledge` dependency alias so that registration resolves.

For an npm installation, replace `<profile>` with your profile name, such as `web`:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-knowledge@npm:dsh-knowledge-core
```

For a built [local checkout](#development), replace the absolute path and profile name:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add "dsh-knowledge@file:/absolute/path/to/dsh-knowledge-core"
```

Or install from the repository:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-knowledge@github:Claven07/dsh-knowledge-core
```

Git installations build through `prepare`. If pnpm blocks required build scripts, review the packages and allow the exact build entries it reports in the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml` before retrying. See pnpm's [package aliases](https://pnpm.io/aliases) documentation for the dependency-name behavior.

Add an ID-targeted override to `<resolved DSH home>/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml` (by default `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`) to select a project and opt into extraction:

```yaml
- id: dsh-knowledge
  name: dsh-knowledge/plugin
  config:
    project: payments
    automaticExtraction: true
```

An override replaces the row's configuration, so include all settings you need to retain.

| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `knowledge_add` | Create a candidate with caller evidence and current-session evidence when available. |
| `knowledge_search` | Search stored content literally with scope and lifecycle filters. |
| `knowledge_list` | List records by scope, type, status, or creation origin. |
| `knowledge_get` | Read a record; `includeHealth: true` requests a live health check. |
| `knowledge_archive` | Archive a record in the selected scope. |
| `knowledge_check_freshness` | Compare Git-backed evidence in the active workspace/configured project. |
| `knowledge_health` | Check 1–16 IDs; `includeGuidance: true` adds advisory follow-up guidance. |

Before agent steps, the adapter retrieves at most four relevant records and injects up to 1,800 characters of quoted context. `knowledge_add` attempts Git provenance capture for clean, tracked file evidence when the requested workspace matches the active session.

## Configuration and data storage

All plugin settings are optional:

| Option | Default | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `databasePath` | `<resolved DSH home>/knowledge/knowledge.sqlite` | SQLite file path; relative paths resolve against the process working directory. |
| `dshHome` | `DSH_HOME`, then `~/.dsh` | Override the Harness home used by the default database path. |
| `project` | No project label | Select the default project for tools, extraction, and pre-step retrieval. |
| `automaticExtraction` | `false` | Enable rule-based candidate extraction from direct user messages. |

With no home override, the plugin stores data in `~/.dsh/knowledge/knowledge.sqlite`. The core library requires an explicit database path; the quick start uses `.dsh-knowledge/knowledge.sqlite`. `KnowledgeStore` creates parent directories and supports `:memory:` for temporary databases. File-backed databases use SQLite WAL mode.

The adapter uses the active session's `cwd` as its workspace. Without a configured project, tools and pre-step retrieval use workspace-wide knowledge. Tools with a project parameter accept `project: null` to select workspace-wide records explicitly.

When extraction is enabled, bounded direct-user statements are processed after each turn. The detector stores the selected statement as a candidate with a compact session reference, rather than a full transcript. Extracted records have `creationOrigin: "automatic"`; inspect them with `knowledge_list`. They enter ranked retrieval only after explicit verification through the core API.

## Development

Clone the repository and install its development dependencies:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Claven07/dsh-knowledge-core.git
cd dsh-knowledge-core
npm ci
npm run build
npm run typecheck
npm test
```

`npm ci` runs the package's `prepare` script, which builds with TypeScript; `npm run build` rebuilds explicitly. The build emits ESM JavaScript and TypeScript declarations in `dist/`. `npm run typecheck` checks `src/` without emitting files; `npm test` runs `tests/**/*.test.ts` with Vitest in a Node.js environment.

To use the built checkout in another Node.js project, run this from that project, replacing the path:

```sh
npm install "/absolute/path/to/dsh-knowledge-core"
```

## Limitations and security

- Retrieval uses local lexical matching and scans active records in scope. It does not use embeddings or semantic search.
- Extraction recognizes a narrow set of explicit statements and may miss useful knowledge. Assistant assertions and tool outcomes are not treated as evidence for automatic candidates; there is no model-facing verification tool.
- Health and freshness are on-demand evidence checks, not proof that a claim is true. `current` means checkable Git-backed snapshots match; `potentially_stale` signals a changed or missing source; `unverifiable` means evidence could not be checked. These checks do not alter lifecycle status or retrieval eligibility.
- Git checks are bounded snapshot comparisons. They do not follow renames or identify every historical edit. Missing objects, unsafe paths, configured filters, and hidden index state can make evidence unverifiable.
- Workspace scope uses the supplied string without filesystem canonicalization. Use consistent workspace paths and configure project labels explicitly. Data stays in the selected SQLite database; synchronization is not provided.
- Workspace/project scope is a filtering convention, not an access-control boundary. The trusted repository API can read across scopes. Protect access to the SQLite database and its WAL/SHM files and backups; exclude private project-memory files from version control.
- The Harness ingestion tool and automatic extraction reject common secret patterns, but this filtering is not comprehensive. The trusted core repository API does not scan secrets. Do not store credentials or sensitive personal data.
- Injected knowledge is quoted and labeled as untrusted data. Review stored content before relying on it or marking it verified.
- Harness places retrieved content in the agent's model context. Local SQLite storage does not prevent that content from being sent to the configured model provider.

# dsh-task-ledger

Name reserved for an upcoming [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh) (dsh) plugin:

- a **task ledger board** UI (per-workspace todos, history by owner, reports)
- the **task-ledger** skill bundled for global agent use

First functional release in development.

# dsh-task-ledger

Monorepo for the **task ledger** project — one repo, two npm packages:

| Package | What | Who installs it | Publish trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`dsh-task-ledger`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-task-ledger) | DSH (DeepSeek Harness) plugin: task ledger board UI + the `task-ledger` skill bundled | DSH users (`dsh plugin add dsh-task-ledger`) | tag `plugin-v*` |
| [`task-ledger`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/task-ledger) | The standalone skill (SKILL.md + scripts + assets), zero-code | CodeBuddy / other agent users (`npm install task-ledger`) | tag `skill-v*` |

The skill content has a single source of truth at `packages/skill/`; the plugin bundles a copy built from it, so DSH users get the skill automatically while everyone else installs `task-ledger` directly.

## Status

- `task-ledger@1.2.2` published (2026-10-19): every edit to a worklog must now be followed by exactly one `log` call — an edit without a matching execution record counts as unfinished work.
- `dsh-task-ledger@0.0.56` published (2026-10-19): bundles the updated skill text; no host behaviour change.
- `task-ledger@1.2.1` published (2026-10-19): prompt slimmed from ~26 KB to ~9 KB (details moved to `references/`, loaded on demand); `description` rewritten as pure routing (three intent clusters + explicit-only close/release) — no commands, paths or workflow text; handover removed from the prompt (release → claim only, `set --owner` kept for a future UI); history table separator fixed to 9 columns; older worklogs without the 执行记录 section get one appended automatically.
- `dsh-task-ledger@0.0.55` published (2026-10-19): bundles the slimmed skill and its references; no host behaviour change beyond `0.0.54`.
- `task-ledger@1.2.0` published (2026-10-19): worklog gains a script-maintained **执行记录** section (`- 时间 · 类型 · @谁 · 说明`, types `new`/`claim`/`set`/`release`/`log`/`close`, append-only) and a new `log` subcommand; `progress.json` gains `updated` (last-progress time); **`blocked` state removed** — blocked/stale are now time-derived flags (7 days since start / 3 days since last update), old `blocked` rows stay readable as in-progress.
- `dsh-task-ledger@0.0.54` published (2026-10-19): board stats `blocked`/`myBlocked` replaced by time-derived `overdue`/`myOverdue` (7 days since start); stale now means 3 days without progress and feeds the `updated` field; per-row `overdue` flag ships for the UI round.
- `task-ledger@1.0.2` published (2026-10-17): `history` JSON mode now emits JSON even when a workspace has no history files (fixes a 500 that blanked the whole board).
- `task-ledger@1.1.0` published (2026-10-17): history format 8→9 columns — new **creator** column (task initiator, distinct from owner which can be claimed away). `close` writes it; `upgrade_history` migrates legacy rows by following each row's worklog link and reading the 「创建：…（@发起人）」 header (same source as `created` — **no data lost**); read-only `history --json` also back-fills it for unmigrated 8-col rows.
- `dsh-task-ledger@0.0.18` published (2026-10-17): chart semantics fixed per user — **新增（我的）now means 'created by me' (creator)**, while 完成/未结（我的）stay 'owned by me' (owner). Previously all three used owner. Smoke adds a fork-semantics integration test (creator-created + other-owned open/closed fixtures: mine.created=2, mine.done=0, mine.remaining=0) and scopes the remaining baseline invariant to `all` only (mine's three series are now different scopes — mixing them in one identity is invalid).
- `dsh-task-ledger@0.0.17` published (2026-10-17): chart hover tooltip cleaned up — top line now only shows the week-end date (e.g. '截至 2026-10-17'), with the three colored rows below carrying the numbers; when '只看我的' is checked the date line shows '(只看我的)' so the scope is obvious.
