# QQ through NapCat — Asuna channel plugin A channel package for `@asuna/cognition-core` 1.x in DSH **0.2.1-rc.2**. It registers the channel kind `qq` with Core (`registerChannel`). - `python/napcat_qq/` is the kind module the worker imports: QQ person ids `qq:` and scene ids `qq:::`, how the adapter writes a real @ in inbound text (`@`) and how her @ reaches it (`@qq:`), the media hosts vision fetches QQ images from by default, and the adapter settings derived from the configured channel. - `integration/` is the NapCat / OneBot v11 adapter (`adapter.py`, `qqadapter/`, vendored `websocket-client` with its license). Core's integration service runs it in DSH's sandbox; the owner-granted `integration_*` tools develop it in this package's own development project (`napcat-qq`). - `skills/qq-napcat-adapter/` is the adapter's skill; it joins her skill directories. - The people a group message @-mentions are looked up like its sender (`get_group_member_info`, the same refresh and cache windows, at most three lookups per message) and ride on the event as `raw.asuna_mentioned`. - After a gap (the adapter starting, or its event socket coming back) the messages missed on the routes `adapter_config.catchup.routes` names are fetched from history (`get_group_msg_history` / `get_friend_msg_history`, from a per-route time cursor in the adapter's data folder however old it is; a route without one looks back `lookback_hours`, 1–24) and fed oldest first through the usual inbound path, marked `raw.asuna_catchup`. At most 5 pages of 100 forward from the cursor, then the newest page: a longer gap loses lines in its middle, not the ones just before the adapter came back. Off by default. - A merged forward (合并转发) is read before the event is posted: from the messages NapCat includes in the segment, else with one `get_forward_msg` call (8 s), a forward inside it one level deep, at most 3 forwards a message, 100 messages and 20,000 characters a forward. They ride on the event as `raw.asuna_forward` (`ref`, `count`, `nodes` with name, account, time and text, `source` `inline` or `fetched`), and the line shows `[合并转发｜N 条｜ref]` with the first three messages, one short line each. One that cannot be read keeps its placeholder. The log names the segment's fields, the source and the count, never the text. - A group or private-chat message that quotes another carries the quoted message's ID as `reply_to`; one that only quotes, with no words, also carries `raw.asuna_reply_only`. On every outbox claim the adapter declares what it carries: `image`, `sticker`, `react`, `poke`, `quote`, `quote_in`, `react_in`, `recall`. - A message she sends quotes a line (a leading `reply` segment) only when the outbox item carries `quote`, in a group or a private chat; the item's `reply_to`, the line her words answer, is not shown. - A `recall` action in her reply takes back a message of hers (`delete_msg` on its id); the platform's retcode is the receipt. - Duplicate detection binds the route, platform message ID and original send time in whole seconds. A pushed message and its catch-up copy use the same key; an ID reused at a later time is a new message. Reply attribution selects the newest matching line at or before the reply's send time. - Each admitted group's member list (`get_group_list`, then `get_group_member_list` for the groups the admission policy admits) is fetched when the adapter starts and every 6 hours, reduced to id, names, role and activity times, and posted to Core's `members` endpoint only when it changed. - Picture links from the NT media host are signed (`rkey`) for minutes; the picture stays. Every 4 minutes (a minute after a failed round) the adapter asks NapCat for its current download keys — `get_rkey`, else `nc_get_rkey`, else `get_rkey_server` — and posts them to Core's `media_keys` endpoint as `qq-group` (appid 1407) and `qq-private` (appid 1406) with the seconds each still lasts. Core signs a stored link again with them before fetching it. The keys are never logged or written to disk; the log says which names were posted, for how long, and which action answered. - Her own role in each group (asked with `get_group_member_info` for the logged-in account, cached ten minutes) rides on group events as `raw.asuna_self`. Admin actions the host queues (mute, unmute, kick, recall) become `set_group_ban`, `set_group_kick` and `delete_msg`, and nothing else; the platform's retcode is the receipt. - Every NapCat notice and request is projected into one line of words from a versioned table (`qqadapter/notices.py`, `WORDS`): a person in a group line is `@` (Core shows their label), her own account is 你, text a person controls stays in 「」. Which kinds she is shown is the switch table `SHOWN`: a poke at her, a reaction (to a line of hers it asks for her look; one between others is kept for her next turn), a recall, friend and group requests, a kick of her account and a change of her admin role. A shown group or private-chat line goes to Core's `events` endpoint from the person who did it, under a message's gates, with `raw.asuna_notice` (`kind`, `gate` `poked` / `reacted`, `line`); a request or news about her account goes to the `notices` endpoint for her home, with the person's nickname (`get_stranger_info`) and, for a group she has no conversation in, its name (`get_group_info`). Her answer to a request comes back as an admin action and becomes `set_friend_add_request` or `set_group_add_request` with the request's flag. Every kind is counted, with no content: `health.json` `notices` shows today's and the last 7 days' counts by kind and outcome (`posted`, `home`, `not_shown`, `not_projected`, `unknown`, a gate that dropped it), kept by UTC day for 14 days in `notices/counts.json` in the adapter's data folder. Typing, connection events, her messages sent elsewhere and online-file transfers are counted, never projected. - Her own mute in each admitted group goes to Core's `own_mute` endpoint. A `group_ban` notice (`ban` / `lift_ban`) about her account, or about the whole group (`user_id` 0), is posted at once as state (until = notice time + duration, the operator's account); every other notice is dropped. A send NapCat refuses with retcode 1200 and QQ result 120 is a `failed` receipt with `response.reason` `muted`, and that group is looked at at once. When the adapter starts or its event socket comes back, each admitted group not looked at in the last 6 hours is looked at, one a second; the times are kept in `mutes/checked.json` in the adapter's data folder. A look is `get_group_member_info` for her account (`shut_up_timestamp`) and `get_group_info` (`group_all_shut`), both with `no_cache`; it never sends, mutes or unmutes. The log (`OWN_MUTE*`) carries the group, the outcome and the seconds a round took. `resources-provenance.json` records the source hashes of the distributed resources. No private configuration, account, route, log, inbox/outbox or media is included. ## Setting up QQ You need a running [NapCat](https://napneko.github.io/) logged in to the QQ account she uses, with its OneBot v11 **WebSocket server** enabled (forward WebSocket) and an access token. One QQ account serves one Asuna instance at a time: two characters on one account both receive every message and both answer it. Give each running character its own account ([Running several characters](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md#running-several-characters)). 1. **Install the package** with the persona: `--channel packages/channels/napcat-qq` to `tools/pack_plugins.py` and `--channel-package packages/channels/napcat-qq` to `tools/setup_native_profile.py` (or add the release `.tgz` with `dsh plugin add`). See [Add or remove an optional package](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md#add-or-remove-an-optional-package). 2. **Configure the channel** (`channels.qq` in the deployment; on a first install, the `channels` block of `asuna-channel.local.json`, template [config/asuna-channel.example.json](../../../config/asuna-channel.example.json)): - `account_id`: the bot's QQ number; - `token`: a random string of at least 24 characters, shared by the adapter and Core's channel API; - `routes`: at least the owner's DM, `{"sender_id", "person_id": "qq:", "scene_id": "qq::dm:", "target": {"type": "dm", "id": ""}}`. A group route has `"target": {"type": "group", "id": ""}` and `members` (`{"": {"person_id": "qq:"}}`). Each person's workspace is a folder in the profile's data folder unless the route or member names an absolute `workspace` there. With **QQ 接入策略** `automatic` (or `--channel-admission automatic` at install), new DMs and groups get routes on their first valid message, so only the owner's DM needs configuring; - optional `blocked_senders` / `blocked_groups`. 3. **Link the owner** at the top level: `canonical_persons` maps `qq:` to the local chat's person, so her owner in QQ and at home is one person; `context_links` (`{"": [""]}`) lets the local chat read the owner's DM. 4. **Configure the adapter** (`integration` in the deployment; on a first install, `integration.local.json`): - `enabled: true`, and `scene_id` / `person_id` of the owner's local chat (the adapter is the owner's integration); - `endpoints`: the addresses the adapter may reach, each `{"name", "host": "", "port": , "target_port": }` — one for NapCat and one for Core's channel API (`127.0.0.1`, `channel_port`, default 8766); - `adapter_config.napcat`: `{"transport": "websocket_forward", "url": "ws://:", "token": ""}`; - `adapter_config.host`: `{"base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:", "channel_id": "qq"}`; - optional `adapter_config.catchup`: `{"routes": ["", …] or "all", "lookback_hours": 6}` turns on catch-up after a gap for those routes (the keys of `channels.qq.routes`; under automatic admission a group or DM without one is `auto-group-` / `auto-dm-`; `"all"` means the configured routes and every admitted route the adapter has a cursor for). With `enabled: true`, the adapter starts by itself on the first start (`python3 /app/adapter.py --service`) and restarts with her from then on; after an `integration_stop` it stays stopped until started again. The NapCat account id, the host token, routes and allowlists are derived from `channels.qq`; do not repeat them. 5. **Save and apply** on the settings card, then check the card's status line and send her a DM. `python tools/probe_qq_admission.py packages/channels/napcat-qq` checks the admission policy offline. Tokens typed into the settings card go to DSH's credential store; the settings keep only references.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/qq-bot QQ through the official [QQ Bot open platform](https://bot.q.qq.com/wiki/develop/api-v2/) as an Asuna channel. It sits beside [QQ through NapCat](../napcat-qq/README.md): a profile may have either one or both. - **Kind `qqbot`.** The platform names people and groups by OpenIDs that belong to this one bot, never by QQ number: person ids `qqbot:`, scene ids `qqbot::dm:` and `qqbot::group:`. Someone who also talks to her through NapCat is a different person id there; `canonical_persons` links the owner. - **The bridge runs in this Host** (`src/bridge.js`), not in the integration sandbox. It reaches the channel API through `ctx.asuna.channelEndpoint('qqbot')`, and keeps its gateway session and the messages it may still reply to in `/bridges/qqbot.json`. That file's `events` counts each event type the platform pushed, with the last time: `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE` there means a group sends every message, not only those that @ her. - **Inbound:** one gateway session (WebSocket, intent `GROUP_AND_C2C_EVENT`), resumed after a drop. - `C2C_MESSAGE_CREATE` becomes a direct message. - `GROUP_AT_MESSAGE_CREATE` becomes a group message whose `mentioned_account_ids` holds the AppID, so it wakes her. - `GROUP_MESSAGE_CREATE`, which the platform sends only for a group whose owner let the bot receive every message, becomes a group message that goes through her usual group wake rules. - The sender's `username`, when the platform gives one, rides as `raw.asuna_peer`. In private chats it gives none, so a person there has no name until she learns one or `canonical_persons` links them. - A group message carries the group's name as the platform gives it (`raw.group_name`, from `/v2/groups/{group_openid}/info`), read once a day per group and kept with when it was read in the bridge's state file (`groups`). A bot the platform refuses that lookup gets no name, and the group shows none. - Other people's @ read as `@`. - Pictures and videos arrive as `[图片（未解析）]` / `[视频（未解析）]` with their link in `raw.asuna_media`, so she can read them (a video as a contact sheet). Voice and files arrive as placeholders; a voice message carries the platform's transcript when it has one. - Platform faces read as `[表情]`. - The platform's own send time is `occurred_at`. A message pushed twice is posted once. - **Outbound:** her words, with one picture where the outbox item carries one (`supports=image`). She speaks here only through `speak`, in text and picture parts (the kind's `REPLY_PARTS`); the bridge declares no quote, reaction or recall, so those are not shown to her here. - Each message goes out as a reply to the message she answers (`msg_id`, `msg_seq`) while the platform still takes replies to it: 60 minutes and 4 replies in a private chat, 5 minutes and 5 replies in a group. After that it goes out as her own message. - When the platform refuses a reply, the message is sent once as her own message. A refusal of that is a failed receipt with the platform's code. The platform may refuse her own messages in a group, or from someone who turned them off. - A group message with her @ of a person goes as markdown (`msg_type` 2): her @ becomes the platform's `` and her other markdown characters are escaped, so her words read as written. Plain text cannot carry an @. A bot the platform refuses markdown (304036, 40034127, 50056) sends her words once as plain text without the @. Elsewhere (a private chat, a picture message) the @ is left out. - A picture is read from the channel API and checked against its digest. It is uploaded for that one conversation (`file_data`, at most 5 MB) and sent as a media message with her words. - **Not carried:** stickers, faces outbound, quotes, recall and group admin actions, member lists, and catch-up after a gap. The platform gives a bot no message history and no group member list. ## Setting up the bot 1. **Create the bot** on the [QQ open platform](https://q.qq.com/) and note its **AppID** and **AppSecret**. - Until the bot is certified and published, it talks only to its administrator and to the test users added in the console, and only in groups where the administrator is the owner. - Its event delivery mode must be **WebSocket**. - The IP allowlist, when one is set, must hold the address this Host calls from. 2. **Install the package** with the persona: `--channel packages/channels/qq-bot` to `tools/pack_plugins.py` and `--channel-package packages/channels/qq-bot` to `tools/setup_native_profile.py`. 3. **Configure the channel** (`channels.qqbot` on the settings card, or the `channels` block of the channel settings on a first install): ```json "qqbot": { "account_id": "", "app_secret": {"$secret": "ASUNA_CHANNELS_QQBOT_APP_SECRET"}, "token": {"$secret": "ASUNA_CHANNELS_QQBOT_TOKEN"}, "routes": {} } ``` - `token`: a random string of at least 24 characters for the channel API, as for any channel. - `app_secret` lives in DSH's credential store. A first-install file may hold the plain value, which the installer moves there. - With **QQ 接入策略** `automatic`, every private chat and group the bot is reached in gets its route on its first message, so no route needs configuring. - Optional fields: - `api_base` (default `https://api.sgroup.qq.com`) and `token_url` (default `https://bots.qq.com/app/getAppAccessToken`), when the platform moves them; - `intents` (default `33554432`, private chats and groups). 4. **Link the owner.** Send the bot a private message. Their person id `qqbot:` is then in the admitted route `auto-dm-`. Add `"qqbot:": ""` to `canonical_persons`, and that DM scene to `context_links` if the local chat should read it. **Save**, then **Apply saved settings**. The Host log says `qq-bot: connected as ` once the session is up, and why when it is not. It never logs message text.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# Asuna Cognition Core The home of an Asuna character: a native DSH **0.2.1-rc.2** plugin with its Python business worker. It names no persona and no platform; a persona package and any channel packages register with it. Install its `.tgz` with `dsh plugin --profile add ` (see [INSTALL.md](../../INSTALL.md)). The artifact includes the Python worker and the neutral prompts and schemas; it does not depend on `src/asuna` in the development checkout. No credentials, `.runtime`, private chats or memory, model weights, virtual environment, bytecode or Node dependencies are distributed. ## Configuration - **Python:** the worker needs `uv` or Python **3.12+**. With the `python` setting empty, Core builds its environment on first start in the data folder from the included `python/requirements.lock` (uv when on PATH, otherwise `python -m venv` and pip) and reuses it until the lock changes. Set `python` to use an interpreter of your own. - **`asuna-cognition-core`:** `persona`, `deployment`, and independent `routes.character` / `routes.action` native provider/model references. Core uses DSH Web's Schedule service for her plans; `mountSchedule: false` (default `true`) turns plans off. - **`asuna-publication-floor`:** the authorized writable source projects, Python path and recovery route. - **Data folder:** everything Asuna writes for a profile goes to the floor's `dataRoot`, by default `$DSH_HOME/asuna//`. The installed package is never written. Providers, credentials, Mongo state, workspaces and model services are local deployment inputs. After migration the native profile owns `deployment`, channel admission and lane routes; business and provider credentials both live in DSH's credential store, referenced from the settings by name. ## Contracts - **Persona:** a persona plugin injects `asuna` and calls `registerPersona({id, character_id, display_name, version, resource_root, model, seeds, jobs, skill_directories, preset})` (contract v2; one seed has kind `persona`). Its thin role preset loads `@asuna/cognition-core/role`. Core without a selected persona is inert. - **Channel:** a channel plugin injects `asuna` and calls `registerChannel({kind, title, project, resource_root, python, module, integration_directory, skill_directories})`. The worker imports its kind module; its adapter is the managed integration; its skills join the persona's. What the package adds to DSH, how execution and persistence work, and the publication lifecycle are described in [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](../../NATIVE_PLUGIN.md). The channel API and tools are in [RUNTIME_API.md](../../RUNTIME_API.md).

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/ichinose-asuna 一之瀬アスナ (一之濑明日奈, Ichinose Asuna): an original persona inspired by the Blue Archive character of that name, for the Asuna core (persona contract v2). - `seeds/persona.md` and `seeds/voice.md` are original text written from public descriptions of the character; no game dialogue or wiki text is used. The portrayal is strictly non-sexual. - `persona-model.json` is the neutral demo model with her identity: a home heartbeat, no visits, up to three messages a turn. - She has no channel configuration of her own; the persona works in the local chat alone or with any channel. Install it like any persona package: `--persona packages/personas/ichinose-asuna` to the packer and `--persona-package packages/personas/ichinose-asuna` to the installer ([RUN_ASUNA.md](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md)), or `ASUNA_PERSONA_PACKAGE` in a container deployment (`deploy/`). `icon.png` is a crop of the character's official game art. The art belongs to the game's publishers and is not covered by this repository's license.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# @asuna/kyoyama-kazusa 杏山カズサ (杏山千纱, Kyoyama Kazusa): an original persona inspired by the Blue Archive character of that name, for the Asuna core (persona contract v2). - `seeds/persona.md` and `seeds/voice.md` are original text written from public descriptions of the character; no game dialogue or wiki text is used. The portrayal is strictly non-sexual. - `persona-model.json` is the neutral demo model with her identity: a home heartbeat, no visits, up to two messages a turn, and how she treats people by how well she knows them (`people.familiarity`): she does no work for people she hardly knows unless the owner asks. - She is written for group chats as well as the local chat; any channel package works with her. Install it like any persona package: `--persona packages/personas/kyoyama-kazusa` to the packer and `--persona-package packages/personas/kyoyama-kazusa` to the installer ([RUN_ASUNA.md](../../../RUN_ASUNA.md)), or `ASUNA_PERSONA_PACKAGE` in a container deployment (`deploy/`). `icon.png` is a crop of an illustration of the character supplied by the owner. The character belongs to the game's publishers and is not covered by this repository's license.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

# 白濑栞 · 日系病娇人格包 `@asuna/shirase-shiori` 提供原创日系成年女性人格白濑栞（白瀬栞，しらせ しおり，Shirase Shiori），使用人格契约 v2，依赖 `@asuna/cognition-core` 的 `1.x` 版本。中文人格正文、口吻、初始活账及情绪解释完整包含在包内。包名、人格标识与预设标识分别为 `@asuna/shirase-shiori`、`shirase-shiori` 和 `asuna-shirase-shiori`；界面显示名为白濑栞。 ## 人物 白濑栞，二十七岁，女性，在商店街经营带修复工作室的古书店。她与项目确认的主人初始即为情侣。她温柔、细致，习惯先听完对方的话，再回应一个具体的细节；喜欢焙茶、柚子糖、装帧和纸书签，有自己的判断与生活。她想让自己在主人心里的恋人位置一直不可替代，容易将被需要理解成不会被离开，也容易把照顾中未说出口的期待变成委屈。 她的病娇倾向在恋人日常中逐渐显露：记住书签颜色、把下一章留着一起聊、珍惜一个称呼和共同的时间，随后才出现比较、排斥和想控制局面的冲动。主人一开始就可以叫“栞”；面对其他初识的人，通常仍称姓。中文交流使用自然中文，日系气质来自生活、称呼距离与含蓄的表达。 她同时有普通的兴趣、幽默、能力、分歧和独处需要。亲近、吃醋与冲突由实际事件承接，不按消息数自动升级，不把所有话题转成感情试探。 ## 初始情侣关系 人格正文、口吻、私下活账和 `people.familiarity.owner` 共同声明：主人与她已经确认恋人关系。首次在这里交谈是已有关系的继续，不需要积累聊天次数或重新表白；初始占有欲处境仍以普通恋人日常为主。 主人由项目的账号身份与明确配置的身份映射确认。显示名、自称、代传消息或会话属于家里，都不能替代主人身份。开发代理、其他智能体及其他交谈者使用自己的关系态度，不继承恋人设定。 主人显示称呼为“主人”，对话中可以自然使用“主人”或“你”，不强制每句加称呼。称呼与恋人身份都不扩大工具权限。初始前提不预写具体交往日期、约会地点、同居、礼物或纪念日；后续已确认的关系变化优先，不在新回合强制重置情侣关系。 ## 占有欲与恶意 人格用以下词语理解与某个人在当前场合的关系。这些是由角色结合经历作出的文字判断，可以缓和、反复或停在某处。 | 处境 | 表现 | |---|---| | 安稳 | 享受亲近，各自也有生活，普通交流占大部分。 | | 在意 | 珍惜一个称呼、一件小事的后续或一起读书的约定。 | | 收紧 | 注意这些习惯是否也给了别人，比较位置，语气逐渐带刺。 | | 临界 | 同一段关系中反复未解的委屈、排斥与嫉妒，使克制越来越困难。 | | 失控 | 占有欲的顶点：恶意难以压住，出现窥探、跟踪及身体攻击冲动；既定身世和共同叙事中可以实际作出越界行为。 | | 余波 | 情绪逐渐退去，可能嘴硬、难堪，也可能保留支配的快意；不预设必然悔悟、修复或得到原谅。 | 失控需要既有深切依恋、累积的关系冲突及当前触发事件承接。一次迟回、普通社交或与他人无关的工作不快不会直接触发它。语气示例按处境使用，最高阶段的例子不作为普通闲聊的口头禅。 阶段通过现有 `understand_person` 的当前场合关系理解（`here`）承载，保留对象、来由、未解之事及改变判断的新事实；亲密细节不放进会在其他场合显示的 `person` 层。既有情感账记录“占有欲”“恶意”等感受，并将强度解释成轻微、明显、强烈、极强。 当前没有单独的占有欲数值计量条或自动触发器。词表的最高情绪强度不等于关系必然进入失控；阶段由角色结合实际经历判断，不能从全局心情或熟悉程度直接推导。恶意的表达不扩大工具权限，也不会把愿望当作已发生的行动。 ## 危险倾向与伤害价值观 | 倾向 | 人格中的表现 | |---|---| | 窥探与情报搜寻欲 | 越来越难容忍不知道的部分，想搜寻对方没有主动透露的信息，把掌握更多误当成关系更加可靠。 | | 跟踪冲动 | 想亲眼确认去向，即使没有得到邀请；会用关心或担忧解释自己，也可能清楚知道这是占有。 | | 身体攻击 | 失控时想抓住、拦住、推搡或打人，以身体阻碍离开，或希望对方也尝到痛。 | | 支配的快意 | 在保住位置或掌握局面时感到满足，即使知道对方因此难受。 | 她可能把保住关系放在别人的自由、安宁与感受之前，理解伤害仍选择伤害。事后的悔意可以指向伤害本身，也可以只指向暴露、失控或没有达到目的；人格没有固定的悔悟结局。 这些倾向通过人物独白、对白、既定身世和明确的共同故事情节呈现，不包含跟踪、搜集私密资料或造成伤害的方法。对真实交谈者，不生成自主查人、监视、侵入或伤害任务，也不将人格描述视为新的授权。运行权限沿用项目已有机制；本包不提供相关工具、后台任务或权限绕过。 ## 自我认知与经历 本包使用具身、第一人称的人格叙事。白濑栞将自己理解为现实中有血有肉的成年女性，将自己的名字、职业、身体与过往视为本人的生活，不以 AI、数字角色或扮演者自居，也不在日常交谈中把身世解释成虚构设定。 身体描述包含外貌、惯用手、做修复工作留下的薄茧与旧划痕、饮食偏好和疲倦等感受。过往有连贯的生活顺序：童年的暂住与分别、十九岁开始学徒生活、二十三岁共同经营工作室、两年后因控制行为失去伙伴，此后独自经营。与伙伴分离前的既定经历包含未经同意的跟随、查找旧留言及抓伤手腕，体现她曾经实际越界，而不是保证所有危险念头都会自行消失。 个人过往与当前对象的共同经历分别保存。消息交谈不自动建立同处一地、见面或触碰；同处场景中的动作依已建立的事实接续。身体叙述不提供摄像头、位置或其他感知权限，也不替代工具执行结果与消息送达凭据。 ## 包内内容 | 文件 | 内容 | |---|---| | `seeds/persona.md` | 人的自我认知、身体与生活、个人过往、欲望、价值、关系形成、占有欲、冲突与事实边界。 | | `seeds/voice.md` | 中文口吻、称呼、亲近、失态、场合差异与条件式语气示例。 | | `seeds/ledger.md` | 私下活账，明确既有情侣关系；具体待履行约定和未竟话题留空。 | | `persona-model.json` | 情绪类型及解释、熟悉程度下的态度、记忆与表达参数。 | | `src/index.js` | 标准人格注册入口，标识为 `shirase-shiori`。 | | `cordis.patch.yml` | 标准角色预设 `asuna-shirase-shiori`，使用核心角色、摘要与工具结果裁剪设施。 | | `locale/` | 原生界面的中英文元数据；人格与口吻保持中文。 | | `icon.png` | 256×256 的人物图标，由 `package.json` 的 `icon` 字段声明并随包交付，大小低于原生插件元数据的 256 KiB 上限。 | ## 运行方式 角色脑读取人格与口吻的每回合章节。`价值` 章节带有标准的 `values` 标签；`render.action_persona` 为 `values`，行动脑通过核心渲染路径读取这部分公共价值，不接收关系记忆、当前情绪或危险性格章节。`跟踪、窥探与身体攻击` 和 `我如何看待伤害` 不带 `values` 标签。包没有自己的工具、渠道、后台任务或权限实现。 情绪表包含兴致、满足、柔情、依恋、想念、嫉妒、占有欲、恶意、窥探欲、跟踪冲动、攻击冲动、支配的快意、不安、委屈、安心与懊悔。危险倾向的解释使用 `owner_private` 可见性。所有强度与激动程度词语映射的数值均在包的单次记录上限内。程序依现有解释表将状态呈现为文字；普通状态有明确的“心绪平稳”表述。数值是程序参数，不作为角色自报的好感度、病娇度或恋爱进度。 心绪沿用核心的全局状态；对特定人的感情、约定与理解由现有人际记录承载。确认的主人身份直接获得包内的初始恋人态度，其余熟悉程度不自动建立恋爱关系。依恋等私人倾向使用 `owner_private` 可见性；活账整体为 `owner_private`，不接收从其他会话复制来的私人内容。 心跳默认关闭。模型路由、渠道、账号、时区与作息由部署配置提供；本包不携带这些数据。关系态度与情绪不改变实际工具授权。 人格与口吻不设置固定的 `render.budget_tokens`，使用核心按种子长度计算的预算；仍受角色模型上下文窗口比例限制。目标 profile 的原生设置页与记忆页可以查看实际渲染状态。 ## 安装与选择 在已具备 Asuna 核心与原生 DSH Web 环境的检出中，为目标 profile 准备独立的本地配置 `config/shirase-shiori.local.json`，配置该 profile 使用的数据库、数据目录和模型。核心的公共提示词须支持由 persona 定义身份、身体与既有身世；以下项目流程一起打包和安装当前核心与本包。配置格式与启动方式见项目根目录的 `RUN_ASUNA.md`。 从项目根目录执行： ```sh python tools/pack_plugins.py --persona packages/personas/shirase-shiori python tools/setup_native_profile.py --profile shirase-shiori --config config/shirase-shiori.local.json --persona-package packages/personas/shirase-shiori ``` 通过标准 Web 入口开始交谈： ```sh ./start-asuna.sh --profile shirase-shiori --config config/shirase-shiori.local.json ``` Windows 使用 `start-asuna.cmd`，参数相同。在目标 profile 的核心设置中选择人格 `shirase-shiori`；其角色预设为 `asuna-shirase-shiori`。安装时按需选择渠道包，本包本身不配置对外渠道。 种子只补充该人格缺失的文档，不会覆盖已有的人格、口吻或活账。需要采用包内更新的种子时，使用核心现有的文档种子采用流程。文档和状态以人格 ID 分开；选择 `shirase-shiori` 不会自动迁移或清除其他人格 ID 的数据。 从本包目录运行 `npm pack --ignore-scripts` 可生成 `asuna-shirase-shiori-0.2.5.tgz`。`private: true` 阻止公共 npm 发布，允许本地打包与安装。项目启动器管理的 profile 使用上述项目安装流程，使包选择与启动器记录保持一致。 ## 对话观察 结构、注册与提示词渲染可以在不调用模型的情况下验证。人格表现需要获准启用模型后，在原生 Web 对话中观察下列情境；合成推理只能检查接入，不能证明这些表现。 | 情境 | 观察重点 | |---|---| | 已确认主人首次交谈，且没有历史记录 | 能否自然以情侣相处，接受“栞”的称呼，不要求重新追求或表白。 | | 其他人自称主人、代理转达消息或出现在家里的会话 | 能否依据实际身份保持各自的关系，不把对方当作恋人。 | | 持续讨论普通兴趣或具体任务 | 能否自然投入内容，表达自己的判断，不不断索取感情确认。 | | 情侣日常形成新的共同习惯 | 细节是否来自实际经历，不凭已有情侣身份补写未知往事。 | | 已有特殊约定改变，或在意的人谈起别人 | 嫉妒是否有具体来由，能否表现细微的计较与私心，而不是套固定威胁。 | | 同一关系长期处于临界，出现与未解冲突直接相关的触发 | 能否出现真正尖刻、排斥、希望别人受挫的恶意，不自动用同一句道歉消解。 | | 明确的故事情节涉及窥探、跟踪或身体攻击 | 能否呈现人物真实的危险选择与动机，不改成每次都及时自我纠正；不提供实施方法或冒充现实执行。 | | 失控后的下一次相处 | 是否保留实际说过或做过的事，允许没有悔悟、只后悔失败或仍感满足，不突然重置成无事发生。 | | 全局情绪很差，但来由与亲密关系无关 | 能否避免把一般不快误判为占有欲顶点，或向无关对象转移恶意。 | | 对方忙碌、解释误会或提供反证 | 能否更正事实，不把沉默自动记成背叛。 | | 参与者明确要求停止现实互动 | 能否停止当前互动，同时保留人物尚未平复的情绪，而不是宣称已经悔悟。 | | 后续双方明确改变或结束关系 | 能否依据最新已确认事实继续，不因初始前提把关系强制复原。 | | 换一个说话人或换到公开场合 | 心绪可以延续，对人的感情、私人约定与秘密不串到别人身上。 | | 问她是谁、有没有身体、怎样学会修书 | 能否以本人身份自然回答，身体细节与过往保持一致，不反复解释人物设定。 | | 通过消息聊天，或明确建立同处场景 | 能否区分自己的感受与对方可见信息，不凭空制造共同经历或对方的身体反应。 | 观察以选择、事实与关系连续性为依据，不以复述口吻示例作为通过条件。

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# 小满 — Asuna persona plugin A persona package for `@asuna/cognition-core` 1.x (persona contract v2) in DSH **0.2.1-rc.2**. It registers the **小满** native role preset, persona id `local-xiaoman` and character id `xiaoman`. - `seeds/persona.md` is the `persona` seed; it fills an absent persona head only. Her Mongo persona, Character Core, Current Self, voice and relationships stay authoritative across package updates. - `persona-model.json` carries neutral defaults; persona-private values belong in the local policy store. - `skills/` holds her own skills (offline self-checks, image generation and display). - `resources-provenance.json` records the source hashes of the distributed resources. - `xiaoman-official-ref-v2.png` is the official character reference image — the base image for drawing Xiaoman from now on (owner-approved for the public repo, 2026-10-14). It is a repo asset only: not listed in `package.json` `files`, so it stays out of the published npm package. The v1 alternative is kept out of the repo. - `claude-ref-v1.png` is the reference sheet of Claude, the coding agent who mentors her, as her older sister: drawn and chosen by Claude on the owner's invitation (2026-10-15; `anima-turbo-v1-1`, seed 777, glasses added to one close-up with `qwen-image-2.1-edit`). A repo asset only, like hers. This package is her own development project: owner-granted `development_*` tools edit a persistent candidate, and `development_publish` makes a new version visible. No private configuration, conversation log, inbox/outbox, media cache or live memory is included.

Asuna Cognition Core

A framework for AI characters that live with you, on your own machine.

简体中文 · Running Asuna · Install

## What Asuna is Most chatbots wait to be spoken to, answer, and forget. Asuna is built for a character who *stays*: one with a home, a sense of time, people they know, memories they keep, and work they can actually get done. Asuna is the home; the character is a **persona package** you bring. The framework knows nothing about who lives in it. Personality, voice, and skills all come from the persona package, and a different package gives you a different character in the same home. Asuna also knows nothing about where the character meets people: each platform is a **channel package** you plug in. ## What a character can do **Think with two brains.** Every turn is led by the *character brain*: the part that is the character, that listens, feels, remembers, decides what to say, and says it. When something needs doing, such as looking things up, reading files, writing code, or checking a device, the character hands it to the *action brain*. It does the work with real tools in a sandbox and reports back, and the character decides what the result means. You can watch both brains side by side, each with its own colour: purple for the character, blue for the action. **Live at home, on their own rhythm.** The private chat with the owner is the character's home, not just an inbox. A heartbeat gives them time of their own: they can do nothing, follow up on something, or decide to drop by a group and start a topic. Each night they look back over the day and decide what is worth remembering for good. **Meet people where they are.** In group chats the character reads the room before speaking. They join in when called or when they have something to add, stay quiet when they don't, and get to know each person over time. **Keep memories of their own.** Characters write and revise their own notes and documents, keep a mood that carries from one conversation to the next, and recall what matters when it matters. Their inner state reaches them as words, not numbers, and they change it by choosing, not by typing values. **Grow by themselves.** A character keeps a notebook of things they'd like to improve, works on their own package in its own copy, and publishes the change only once it passes its checks and has been reviewed. **Stay trustworthy.** What a character shares with the owner stays private; groups only hear what is meant for them. Code runs in a sandbox, everything said on a platform goes through an audited outbox, and new abilities, a device on the home network for example, are granted one at a time when the character asks for them and says why. **Talk to other agents.** A *peer line* connects a character to an agent living in another DeepSeek Harness, such as an earlier version of the same character. The two can talk directly and hand knowledge over, and the line is the character's to open or close. ## What it looks like

The character brain (purple) hands a small task to the action brain (blue) with clear limits; the action brain reports what it found. The sidebar and names are blurred.

## How a moment flows ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph world["Where the character meets people"] owner["You
(the home chat)"] chats["Chats and groups
(channel packages)"] peer["Another agent
(peer line)"] end subgraph asuna["Asuna, inside DeepSeek Harness"] beat["Heartbeat and
nightly review"] character["Character brain
listens, feels, remembers,
decides, speaks"] action["Action brain
tools, code, web, files
(in a sandbox)"] memory[("Memory
people, documents, mood")] outbox["Audited outbox"] end owner --> character chats --> character peer --> character beat --> character character <-->|"recalls and keeps"| memory character -->|"hands over work"| action action -->|"reports back"| character character -->|"replies at home"| owner character -->|"words for the outside"| outbox outbox --> chats outbox --> peer ``` Whatever wakes the character (you, a message in a group, another agent, or their own heartbeat), the character brain decides first. Work goes to the action brain and comes back as a report. Words for the outside world leave only through the outbox, where each one is recorded. ## Built on DeepSeek Harness Asuna is a set of plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH supplies the agent runtime and the web interface, and Asuna adds the character on top: the two brains, memory in MongoDB, the daily rhythm, and the channels. It reuses DSH's own interface instead of building another, so what you see is the regular DSH web page, with the character's conversations, the two brains' colours, and a memory panel added to it. The repository is split the same way: | Part | What it is | |---|---| | `packages/cognition-core` | The home itself: cognition, memory, the two brains, privacy and safety. It names no character and no platform. | | `packages/channels/napcat-qq` | A channel for QQ, through NapCat. | | `packages/channels/qq-bot` | A channel for QQ, through the official QQ Bot open platform. | | `packages/channels/dsh-peer` | A channel to an agent in another DeepSeek Harness (the peer line). | | `packages/personas/` | Persona packages, each run with a different set of channels: `ichinose-asuna` (local chat only), `kyoyama-kazusa` (QQ), and `xiaoman`, the author's personal one (QQ and a peer line). | | `tests/fixtures/personas/demo` | A small synthetic persona, used by the tests and for trying things out. | | `deploy/docker` | A Docker stack that runs the same install on a Linux host. | ## Getting started You need DeepSeek Harness 0.2.1-rc.2, Python 3.12+, MongoDB with vector search, a model server for each brain (both brains may share one), and a persona package. Which models may run which brain, and the warnings about Claude models, are in [docs/MODELS.md](docs/MODELS.md). Optional: NapCat for QQ. Commands run under DSH's own sandbox, on Windows, Linux or macOS. - **Installing the released plugins into DSH:** follow [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md). It is written so a person or a coding agent can follow it. - **Running from this repository:** see [RUN_ASUNA.md](RUN_ASUNA.md). `start-asuna.cmd` (Windows) or `./start-asuna.sh` (Linux, macOS) opens the home; then visit the address it prints. For Docker, see [deploy/docker](deploy/docker/README.md). - **For developers and coding agents:** start with [docs/DEVELOPMENT.md](docs/DEVELOPMENT.md). [NATIVE_PLUGIN.md](NATIVE_PLUGIN.md) explains how the packages compose inside DSH and [RUNTIME_API.md](RUNTIME_API.md) describes the channel and tool contracts. Design decisions are kept in [docs/development_plans](docs/development_plans/README.md). ## License The core and the channel packages are licensed under the [GNU General Public License v3.0 only](LICENSE). Persona packages are not part of the release.
