# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow — the lead bundle

The **one** spec an interactive SDLC lead installs. Its patch layer is generated
as the union of its four members' rows (`scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs` in the
source repo), because the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a profile lists and
never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`.

Contains, in a single install:

| Member | What it contributes |
|---|---|
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core) | the nine host services (tasks, scheduler, router, verifier, integration, evidence, escalation, worker-mgr, recovery) |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools) | the propose-only model tools and the `/sdlc` command surface |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets) | 26 role compositions; the lead publishes only the Lead Orchestrator as a selectable preset |
| [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui) | the SDLC right-sidebar web UI and its host routes |

## Install

```sh
# create the profile from the shipped `web` template first
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config

# then the single spec
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow

dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

No build step and no profile edits: the package ships prebuilt `lib/` plus its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it automatically.

From a source checkout the members are unpublished, so the installer links them
as ordinary module dependencies instead (see `scripts/install-local.mjs` in the
source repo) — they must **not** be added as bundles there, or every row would
compose twice.

## Update, auto-update, uninstall

```sh
# upgrade in place (also prunes members left by older releases)
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all

# report only
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json

# remove the package and its bundle selection
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

On startup the lead checks the registry at most once per 24 hours. Stable builds
install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease builds only
report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in,
`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off` disables the check). The running process keeps the old
code until it is restarted; the result is reported as `restart-required`.
Failed installs retry after a short backoff, the version on disk is verified, and
a major release requires explicit consent. Link/file/git installs are never
replaced automatically.

The lead installs exactly one own-scope package, so the GUI **Remove** action
also uninstalls everything without ghost member entries.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0` (declared as a `peerDependency`; DSH
  enforces this range at install and at load)
- Node.js ≥ 22.13 (`node:sqlite`)

## License

MIT

# dsh-sdlc-flow — DSH SDLC Flow (DeepSeek Harness plugin suite)

> **Current beta: 0.4.0-beta.29.** Install from this checkout
> (`npm run install:local`), or the registry form
> (`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install`) — see
> [Install](#install). See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for scope and known
> limitations and [PROOF_REPORT.md](PROOF_REPORT.md) for measured evidence. No
> confirmatory developer-productivity claim is supported yet.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin suite that turns a requirement into a verified,
merged change: it plans a task DAG, dispatches role-preset workers into isolated
git worktrees, verifies against risk-appropriate gates, and integrates.

**Implemented from** [`universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md`](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md).

| Document | What it is |
|---|---|
| [universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md) | the normative specification |
| [SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md](SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md) | gate results, test pyramid, defects found |
| [SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md](SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md) | deviations D0–D7, fixes, what is not implemented |
| [EVAL_PROTOCOL.md](EVAL_PROTOCOL.md) | pre-registered A/B design proving the plugin beats plain DSH |
| [IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md](IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md) | honest audit: what was fixed, measured, or deliberately left |

## Tool startup troubleshooting

The source checkout contains unreleased tool-lifecycle repairs; reinstalling
`@latest` does not fetch these changes until a new release is published. Desktop
users can install the rebuilt `packages/sdlc-orchestrator` directory through
**Plugins → Add plugin** using its absolute path, then quit Harness completely
and reopen it. Do not edit the Desktop profile by hand. Once this build is
installed, later registry releases are checked on startup: stable builds install
automatically, prerelease builds report availability (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install`
opts in; `off` disables). Restart to load the new code.

### “The panel is newer than the SDLC host code”

Host plugin code is loaded once at process start; an in-place update replaces
files on disk but not the host code already running. The panel now probes the
routes and distinguishes three cases before telling you what to do:

- **status answers, flow does not** — an older host build is loaded; fully quit
  Harness and reopen. Closing the window can leave it running in the background:
  use **Quit** from the app/tray menu, or on Linux
  `pkill -f deepseek-harness` / `flatpak kill com.deepseek.harness`.
- **no SDLC route answers** — the host plugin is not registered or enabled in
  this profile; enable it in **Plugins**, or install it for that profile.
- **the probe cannot reach the host** — a transport/connection problem, not a
  version mismatch.

For the **Desktop app**, update through **Plugins → Add plugin** and restart.
`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install` manages the
`sdlc-web` / `sdlc-worker` / `sdlc-probe` CLI profiles; it cannot modify the
app-owned `desktop` profile. The panel shows the panel/host builds and a
**Copy diagnostics** action for support.

The panel also reads the **open session's workspace**, not the Harness process
directory, so the Desktop app shows the project you are actually working in.

For an offline runtime check (no model and no second web server):

```sh
node scripts/verify-tool-runtime.mjs /path/to/unpacked/dsh-runtime
```

It mounts all 26 role compositions and checks tool visibility, real pipeline
execution/rendering, invalid arguments, and worker denial of lead capabilities.
It also asserts that the shipped lead exposes one selectable preset (the Lead
Orchestrator), not the whole role roster. OS/delegation boundaries are stubbed:
this does not test running workers or the Desktop session-creation UI. An
optional second argument points to an unpacked plugin tarball.
A `never started` diagnostic means the loader did not create a plugin fiber;
look for the **earlier loader import error** in the application log. A missing
service instead reports `waiting for tools`. If the former persists after a
clean restart/install, include that earlier error and the installed version.

## Quick start

```sh
npm run build                     # artifacts (zero dependencies, offline; incl. UI bundle)
node scripts/validate-gates.mjs   # gate:P → gate:Q  (no model, no network)
npm run test:unit                 # L2 — pure modules + property tests
```

Every `test:*` script passes explicit globs rather than a directory: Node 24
resolves a bare directory positional as a *script* and fails with
`Cannot find module '<dir>'`, while globs work on every supported engine.

The deterministic control plane needs no model at all:

```sh
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs init        # .sdlc/, integration branch, detected gates
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs status
node packages/sdlc-cli/bin/sdlc.mjs selftest --mock
```

## Flow visualizer (right sidebar)

While a session is open, the DSH right sidebar contains an **SDLC Flow** entry
(the guide's capsule, or auto-open on the first session that has an SDLC
project). It is a live, read-only view of the orchestrator:

- **DAG** — every task node with state, role, risk, routing tier/model, and
  dependency edges;
- **Subagents** — worker runs with role, model, status, pid, tokens and duration;
- **Routing** — tier, rule, provider/model and whether the decision was recorded
  or computed;
- **Gates** — pass/fail/skipped/unknown chips plus per-task detail;
- **Locks / escalations / events** — shared-resource holders, recorded and
  task-state escalations, and the latest 100 events.

It polls `/api/sdlc.flow` every 5 s; on a failed poll the last snapshot is shown
as *stale* rather than blanked. A 404 with no project is reported as such; a
bare 404 is reported as a host/client version mismatch with a restart and
reinstall hint (an in-place update does not replace loaded host code). Missing cost/tokens/duration stay `—` with a
reason, never `0`. Set `autoOpen: false` in the UI row config to stop the
automatic open. DSH's right sidebar has **no surface without a session**, so the
Start screen cannot show it — start a session first.

## Install

### One command — always the latest published version

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
```

This resolves `latest` from the npm registry itself, pins the **exact** version
in the `sdlc-web` profile, records the matching pnpm release-age exemption,
creates the profile when missing, prunes packages left by older releases,
installs, re-selects the bundle (a failed uninstall can leave the package
installed but disabled), and verifies the installed `package.json`. Re-running
it upgrades an existing install instead of requiring an uninstall first.

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all          # lead + worker + probe
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --tag beta          # newest prerelease
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --version 0.4.0-beta.29
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json      # no changes
```

It is idempotent. Prerequisites: `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13.

> **Restart after installing.** A running lead keeps the old module tree in
> memory even after the package on disk changes (deep-imported preset rows are
> not hot-replaced). Quit DeepSeek Harness completely and reopen it; otherwise a
> new session can still report the previous version's `agent-preset/invalid`.
> The installer prints this reminder.

### Beta testers — no clone, no build

Download the release artifact and run its installer. Nothing is compiled on your
machine, and you do not need the source.

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/pwoodman/dsh-sdlc/releases/latest/download/dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
tar xzf dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz && cd dsh-sdlc-*/
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin tree to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-sdlc/<version>/` (so you can
delete the download), then creates the `sdlc-web`, `sdlc-worker` and `sdlc-probe`
profiles, installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It
is idempotent — re-run it any time.

Prerequisites: `dsh` **installed as a package** (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13. A wrapper that
merely answers `dsh --version` — an `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` shim, a shell
function, a hand-written script — is not enough: the platform gate reads the
installed package's own files, and the installer now refuses that setup with
this reason instead of failing later inside `gate:M0`.

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web          # the interactive lead (web GUI)
```

### Uninstall — one click in the plugin manager

The lead installs exactly **one** package (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`; its
members are folded inside it), so removing that single entry in the plugin
manager removes everything — no ghost entries, nothing "still required". From
the CLI it is the same one spec:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web remove @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow
```

A profile installed by a pre-fold release may still list the four members as
plain dependencies; re-run the installer (or this one command) to clear them:

```sh
pnpm remove --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui
```

On Windows, close a running lead first (`sdlc.db` and the bundle files are held
open while it runs). A profile directory itself (`~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web`) is
disposable and can always be deleted outright. The `@deepseek-ai/…` bundles you
see running (for example `dsh-agent-preset-registry`) are DeepSeek Harness's
own — they ship with the profile template and are not part of this plugin.

### DeepSeek Harness Desktop — what works today

The Desktop app owns its `desktop` profile and the `dsh` CLI refuses to manage
it, so the CLI/tarball paths above do not target it. Desktop users install
through the sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin** dialog (paste a package name, a
tarball URL, or an absolute path).

Two honest limits on a Desktop-only machine:

- the lead dispatches workers by spawning `dsh --profile sdlc-worker`, so it
  needs a `dsh` CLI on `PATH` for real task execution — without one, the lead,
  the tools, the presets and the web panel all work, but dispatch does not;
- package installs into `desktop` are the app's own operation, so a plugin that
  needs the worker/probe profiles is better tested against CLI profiles.

### Registry / Add-plugin wizard — one spec for the lead

Once the packages are published under an npm scope you own, the lead is a single
spec (the same shape `dsh-context` and `dsh-proactive` use: prebuilt `lib/` + its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no profile edits, no build
and no restart):

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create once
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

Or fill `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow` into the **Add plugin** wizard on the Plugins page.

> **Fresh beta not installing?** pnpm 11 applies a 24-hour
> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a beta published in the
> last day can resolve to the *previous* beta — this is how a known-broken
> beta.19 kept installing after beta.20 was already `latest`. Prefer the
> installer above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you.
> For a manual install, pin it exactly
> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29`) and add **one list item per
> pattern** to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29'
> ```
>
> A combined value such as `pkg@a || pkg@b` is not a valid pnpm pattern (it is
> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v0.4.0-beta.29 && git push origin v0.4.0-beta.29
```

GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.

token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install

```

builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).

installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

### Uninstall

Remove the package and its bundle selection from every managed profile:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

The GUI path is unchanged: the lead profile contains exactly one own-scope
package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: config editor, task board, side-by-side review (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
demo/                    zero-dependency fullstack task-tracker proving the loop end-to-end
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

Only the interactive lead can grant authority. A headless deployment is a guest
of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

## Web UI

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Status | live project + task + spend summary from `sdlc.db` |
| Board | tasks grouped by state machine state |
| Config | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`) read the live
DB; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI uses.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

## Status

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 662 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness, 6/6 demo. `doctor` passes with 0 errors and
0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets — the 26 SDLC role presets

One `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` row per SDLC role (lead, planner, architect,
implementer, tester, verifier, reviewer, integrator, …). A preset's `plugins`
list *is* the agent composition: persona rows compose the prompt, mounted tool
rows are the allowlist by omission, and the `sdlc_report_result` row is the
propose-only result channel.

Permissions and model are deliberately absent from the presets: permission comes
from the profile's permission row, and the model from the tier overlay.

`cordis.patch.yml` is a **generated** file — its source of truth is
`src/roles.js` (`node scripts/gen-presets.mjs` in the source repo).

## Install

A member of [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow)
(lead) and of the boot-probe composition; it can also be mounted directly:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets
```

The patch also inserts the `agent-preset-registry` row first, so the presets
reach templates that ship no registry (e.g. the `headless` and `sdk`
templates).

This member bundle declares all 26 role compositions. The lead meta-bundle
(`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`) filters the generated patch down to the public
roles (currently the Lead Orchestrator), so a DSH user does not see every
internal role in the Settings page or the new-session preset picker.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Node.js ≥ 22.13

MIT

in the `sdlc-web` profile, records the matching pnpm release-age exemption,
creates the profile when missing, prunes packages left by older releases,
installs, re-selects the bundle (a failed uninstall can leave the package
installed but disabled), and verifies the installed `package.json`. Re-running
it upgrades an existing install instead of requiring an uninstall first.

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all          # lead + worker + probe
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --tag beta          # newest prerelease
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --version 0.4.0-beta.29
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json      # no changes
```

It is idempotent. Prerequisites: `dsh` and `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13.

> **Restart after installing.** A running lead keeps the old module tree in
> memory even after the package on disk changes (deep-imported preset rows are
> not hot-replaced). Quit DeepSeek Harness completely and reopen it; otherwise a
> new session can still report the previous version's `agent-preset/invalid`.
> The installer prints this reminder.

### Beta testers — no clone, no build

Download the release artifact and run its installer. Nothing is compiled on your
machine, and you do not need the source.

```sh
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/pwoodman/dsh-sdlc/releases/latest/download/dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
tar xzf dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz && cd dsh-sdlc-*/
./install.sh
```

`install.sh` copies the plugin tree to `$DSH_HOME/dsh-sdlc/<version>/` (so you can
delete the download), then creates the `sdlc-web`, `sdlc-worker` and `sdlc-probe`
profiles, installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It
is idempotent — re-run it any time.

Prerequisites: `dsh` **installed as a package** (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13. A wrapper that
merely answers `dsh --version` — an `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh` shim, a shell
function, a hand-written script — is not enough: the platform gate reads the
installed package's own files, and the installer now refuses that setup with
this reason instead of failing later inside `gate:M0`.

```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web          # the interactive lead (web GUI)
```

### Uninstall — one click in the plugin manager

The lead installs exactly **one** package (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`; its
members are folded inside it), so removing that single entry in the plugin
manager removes everything — no ghost entries, nothing "still required". From
the CLI it is the same one spec:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web remove @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow
```

A profile installed by a pre-fold release may still list the four members as
plain dependencies; re-run the installer (or this one command) to clear them:

```sh
pnpm remove --dir ~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-core @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools \
  @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-presets @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-ui
```

On Windows, close a running lead first (`sdlc.db` and the bundle files are held
open while it runs). A profile directory itself (`~/.dsh/profiles/sdlc-web`) is
disposable and can always be deleted outright. The `@deepseek-ai/…` bundles you
see running (for example `dsh-agent-preset-registry`) are DeepSeek Harness's
own — they ship with the profile template and are not part of this plugin.

it, so the CLI/tarball paths above do not target it. Desktop users install
through the sidebar **Plugins → Add plugin** dialog (paste a package name, a
tarball URL, or an absolute path).

- the lead dispatches workers by spawning `dsh --profile sdlc-worker`, so it
  needs a `dsh` CLI on `PATH` for real task execution — without one, the lead,
  the tools, the presets and the web panel all work, but dispatch does not;

  needs the worker/probe profiles is better tested against CLI profiles.

spec (the same shape `dsh-context` and `dsh-proactive` use: prebuilt `lib/` + its
own `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the loader mounts it with no profile edits, no build
and no restart):

```sh

dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a beta published in the
> last day can resolve to the *previous* beta — this is how a known-broken
> beta.19 kept installing after beta.20 was already `latest`. Prefer the
> installer above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you.

> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29`) and add **one list item per
> pattern** to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:

>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29'
> ```
>

> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

The packages ship as `@patwoodman/*`. If your npm account does not own that scope,
`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

An npm **user scope** (`@your-username`) is free and exists automatically once
you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v0.4.0-beta.29 && git push origin v0.4.0-beta.29
```

The **Release** workflow verifies the tree, builds the tarball, publishes the
GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.

token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

### From a source checkout — one command

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

Prerequisites: `dsh` installed as a package (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh

```

builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).

installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

```sh

```

package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: config editor, task board, side-by-side review (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
demo/                    zero-dependency fullstack task-tracker proving the loop end-to-end
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Status | live project + task + spend summary from `sdlc.db` |
| Board | tasks grouped by state machine state |
| Config | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`) read the live
DB; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI uses.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 662 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness, 6/6 demo. `doctor` passes with 0 errors and
0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

# @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools — model tools and the `/sdlc` command surface

The propose-only tool surface, installed in **both** the lead and worker
profiles: workers need `sdlc_report_result`, `sdlc_claim_check` and
`sdlc_request_decision` to write their outbox proposal; the lead additionally
gets the delegation and planning tools. The `/sdlc` command surface
(`run`, `status`, `stop`, `resume`, `doctor`, `config`, `verify`, `explain`,
`debug`) is registered in interactive profiles.

None of these tools may grant authority — that is the lead's human-only
privilege (spec L.1 rule 4).

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

It is also a member of [`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow),
so a lead install brings it in without a second spec.

## Requirements

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh` `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`
- Node.js ≥ 22.13

## License

MIT

# dsh-sdlc-flow — DSH SDLC Flow (DeepSeek Harness plugin suite)

> **Current beta: 0.4.0-beta.29.** Install from this checkout
> (`npm run install:local`), or the registry form
> (`npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install`) — see
> [Install](#install). See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for scope and known
> limitations and [PROOF_REPORT.md](PROOF_REPORT.md) for measured evidence. No
> confirmatory developer-productivity claim is supported yet.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin suite that turns a requirement into a verified,
merged change: it plans a task DAG, dispatches role-preset workers into isolated
git worktrees, verifies against risk-appropriate gates, and integrates.

**Implemented from** [`universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md`](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md).

| Document | What it is |
|---|---|
| [universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md](universal_sdlc_orchestrator_dsh_spec_v3.md) | the normative specification |
| [SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md](SDLC_V3_IMPLEMENTATION_VALIDATION_REPORT.md) | gate results, test pyramid, defects found |
| [SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md](SDLC_IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md) | deviations D0–D7, fixes, what is not implemented |
| [EVAL_PROTOCOL.md](EVAL_PROTOCOL.md) | pre-registered A/B design proving the plugin beats plain DSH |
| [IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md](IMPROVEMENT_AUDIT.md) | honest audit: what was fixed, measured, or deliberately left |

## Tool startup troubleshooting

The source checkout contains unreleased tool-lifecycle repairs; reinstalling
`@latest` does not fetch these changes until a new release is published. Desktop
users can install the rebuilt `packages/sdlc-orchestrator` directory through
**Plugins → Add plugin** using its absolute path, then quit Harness completely
and reopen it. Do not edit the Desktop profile by hand. Once this build is
installed, later registry releases are checked on startup: stable builds install
automatically, prerelease builds report availability (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install`
opts in; `off` disables). Restart to load the new code.

### “The panel is newer than the SDLC host code”

Host plugin code is loaded once at process start; an in-place update replaces
files on disk but not the host code already running. The panel now probes the
routes and distinguishes three cases before telling you what to do:

- **status answers, flow does not** — an older host build is loaded; fully quit
  Harness and reopen. Closing the window can leave it running in the background:
  use **Quit** from the app/tray menu, or on Linux
  `pkill -f deepseek-harness` / `flatpak kill com.deepseek.harness`.
- **no SDLC route answers** — the host plugin is not registered or enabled in
  this profile; enable it in **Plugins**, or install it for that profile.
- **the probe cannot reach the host** — a transport/connection problem, not a
  version mismatch.

**Copy diagnostics** action for support.

directory, so the Desktop app shows the project you are actually working in.

```sh

```

execution/rendering, invalid arguments, and worker denial of lead capabilities.
It also asserts that the shipped lead exposes one selectable preset (the Lead
Orchestrator), not the whole role roster. OS/delegation boundaries are stubbed:
this does not test running workers or the Desktop session-creation UI. An
optional second argument points to an unpacked plugin tarball.

look for the **earlier loader import error** in the application log. A missing
service instead reports `waiting for tools`. If the former persists after a
clean restart/install, include that earlier error and the installed version.

```sh
npm run build                     # artifacts (zero dependencies, offline; incl. UI bundle)

npm run test:unit                 # L2 — pure modules + property tests
```

resolves a bare directory positional as a *script* and fails with


```sh
dsh --profile sdlc-web --from-default-profile web --dump-config   # create once
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-web add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow              # core + tools + presets + ui
dsh --profile sdlc-web
```

Or fill `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow` into the **Add plugin** wizard on the Plugins page.

> **Fresh beta not installing?** pnpm 11 applies a 24-hour
> `minimumReleaseAge` to range and `latest` installs, so a beta published in the
> last day can resolve to the *previous* beta — this is how a known-broken
> beta.19 kept installing after beta.20 was already `latest`. Prefer the
> installer above; it pins the exact version and writes the exemption for you.
> For a manual install, pin it exactly
> (`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29`) and add **one list item per
> pattern** to the profile's `pnpm-workspace.yaml`:
>
> ```yaml
> minimumReleaseAgeExclude:
>   - '@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@0.4.0-beta.29'
> ```
>
> A combined value such as `pkg@a || pkg@b` is not a valid pnpm pattern (it is
> ignored, silently reintroducing the old resolution). The same applies to the
> worker members.

The worker profile is deliberately *unpacked*, because mounting the host services
there would start a second scheduler and a second writer against `sdlc.db`
(errata E6):

```sh
dsh plugin --profile sdlc-worker add @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-guard @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow-tools
```

`@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`'s patch layer is generated from its four members
(`node scripts/gen-bundle-patch.mjs`) — the DSH loader mounts only the bundles a
profile lists and never descends into a bundle's `dependencies`. In the lead the
members are ordinary module dependencies; adding them as bundles *as well*
composes every row twice.

#### Publishing under your own npm scope

The packages ship as `@patwoodman/*`. If your npm account does not own that scope,
`npm publish` answers **403** and nobody can resolve `@patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow`. Fix it
in one command:

```sh
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username   # rewrites packages, patches, profiles, tests, docs
node scripts/set-scope.mjs @your-npm-username --check   # CI-safe drift check
```

An npm **user scope** (`@your-username`) is free and exists automatically once
you sign in to npm — `npm login` (GitHub OAuth works) or `npm adduser`. A free npm
**org** (`@acme-team`) works too: <https://www.npmjs.com/org/create>. Then:

```sh
git tag v0.4.0-beta.29 && git push origin v0.4.0-beta.29
```

The **Release** workflow verifies the tree, builds the tarball, publishes the
GitHub Release, and — when the repo has an `NPM_TOKEN` secret *and* the
`PUBLISH_NPM` variable is `true` — publishes the packages in dependency order.
Create the token at <https://www.npmjs.com/settings/~/tokens> (an *Automation*
token, so 2FA does not block CI) and add it as a repository secret.

### From a source checkout — one command

```sh
npm run install:local     # = node scripts/install-local.mjs
node scripts/doctor.mjs   # expect PASS
```

That single command generates the patches, builds the artifacts (zero
dependencies, offline), creates the three profiles from their shipped templates,
installs the bundles, verifies the composed lead and runs `gate:M0`. It is
idempotent and safe to re-run.

Prerequisites: `dsh` installed as a package (`npm install -g
@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2`), `pnpm` on `PATH`, Node ≥ 22.13, a POSIX host with
git.

### Building a release artifact

```sh
node scripts/build-release.mjs        # → dist/dsh-sdlc-<version>.tgz + dsh-sdlc-beta.tgz
```

### Update / upgrade

Re-running the installer is the upgrade path — it resolves the newest published
version, prunes packages left by older releases, and replaces the installed
meta-bundle:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --only all
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --check --json
```

The lead also checks the registry on startup (at most once per 24 hours).
Stable builds install a newer version through DSH's plugin manager; prerelease
builds only report availability by default (`SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=install` opts in).
The running process keeps the old code until it is restarted; the update reports
`restart-required`. A failed install is retried after a short backoff, the
installed version is verified on disk, and a major release requires explicit
consent. Disable the check with `SDLC_AUTO_UPDATE=off`. Link, file, git and
source-checkout installs are never replaced automatically.

### Uninstall

Remove the package and its bundle selection from every managed profile:

```sh
npx -y @patwoodman/dsh-sdlc-flow@latest dsh-sdlc-install --uninstall --only all
```

The GUI path is unchanged: the lead profile contains exactly one own-scope
package, so **Plugins → Remove** removes everything. Profile directories are
left in place; delete them only if you also want to discard their config.

## Layout

```
packages/sdlc-core/      host services + pure domain modules (never in a worker)
packages/sdlc-guard/     worker-side policy (tools/pre-execute, fs deciders)
packages/sdlc-tools/     propose-only model tools + the /sdlc command surface
packages/sdlc-presets/   26 dsh-agent-preset rows (generated from roles.js)
packages/sdlc-cli/       the `sdlc` executable
packages/sdlc-mock-llm/  deterministic ctx.llm provider (test-only)
packages/sdlc-client-ui/ web UI: config editor, task board, side-by-side review (sdlc-web only)
profiles/                installer recipes: sdlc-web, sdlc-worker, sdlc-probe
scripts/                 gates (P, M0–M8, Q), build, installer, doctor, harness
tests/                   unit · contract · integration · fault · adversarial · e2e
demo/                    zero-dependency fullstack task-tracker proving the loop end-to-end
```

## Modes (spec C.2)

| Mode | Command | Slash commands | Approvals | Instance lock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Interactive lead | `dsh --profile sdlc-web` | yes | yes | yes |
| Headless one-shot | `dsh --profile sdlc-worker "<task>"` | no | no (fail-closed) | no |
| Deterministic CLI | `sdlc status/tasks/…` | n/a | read/ops only | briefly |
| Boot probe | `dsh --profile sdlc-probe` | no | no | briefly |

Only the interactive lead can grant authority. A headless deployment is a guest
of the state machine: it can run work but cannot unblock itself.

## Web UI

`dsh --profile sdlc-web` mounts the **SDLC** right-sidebar tab (package
`sdlc-client-ui`, `sdlc-web` only):

| Panel | What it does |
|---|---|
| Status | live project + task + spend summary from `sdlc.db` |
| Board | tasks grouped by state machine state |
| Config | validated editor for `.sdlc/config.yml` (tiers, budgets, gates — writes rejected when validation fails) |
| Review | side-by-side time/tokens/tracepaths for two runs of one task |

Host routes (`/api/sdlc.status`, `/api/sdlc.board`, `/api/sdlc.task`,
`/api/sdlc.compare`, `/api/sdlc.config`, `/api/sdlc.metrics`) read the live
DB; the one POST validates through the same `validateConfig` the CLI uses.
The browser bundle is built offline by `node scripts/build-ui.mjs` (part of
`npm run build`) with zero dependencies.

## Status

`gate:P` and `gate:M0`…`gate:M8` plus `gate:Q` pass (11/11); 662 offline tests
pass across unit/contract/integration/fault/adversarial, 9/10 e2e (1 skipped
by design), 86/86 eval harness, 6/6 demo. `doctor` passes with 0 errors and
0 warnings on a configured host. See the validation report §1 for the two
environment-dependent skips (pnpm-present vs absent, Playwright stack).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
Answer me with HTML

Super Fast  |  ASD-STE100  |  Explainer Videos  |  One File, Offline

An agent skill. Ask a hard question, get a page you can actually read instead of a wall of text.
The model writes about 1/8 of the tokens it would need to hand-write the HTML.

Website · Install · Examples · Videos · Always-on mode · Reference · 简体中文

Once installed, ask questions the way you always do: ``` > Explain the TCP three-way handshake > Map out how the modules in this repo fit together > Redis or Memcached for our cache? ``` The agent writes a short Markdown draft and hands it to the CLI that ships with the skill. About 50 ms later you have a page: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d3063a28-5dfd-4c44-a562-be901c49b249

24-second demo. Turn the sound on for the music.

## Why not just ask for HTML? You can. Models write decent HTML now. But most of what they write is not content. We counted the tokens in 9 pages the model wrote by hand, 4,893 tokens on average: | Part of the page | Share | With this skill | | :--- | ---: | :--- | | SVG diagrams: coordinates and paths | 47% | The CLI writes it | | CSS | 15% | The CLI writes it | | HTML tags | 17% | The CLI writes it | | Text | 21% | The model writes it, as Markdown | With this skill the model writes only a Markdown draft. For the same questions that was 612 tokens on average, **about 1/8 of the hand-written HTML**. Less to write means less to wait for (3 topics × 3 runs, medians, Claude Sonnet 5.5, a plain Claude Code setup): | | Ask for HTML directly | Answer me with HTML | | | :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- | | Tokens the model writes | 4,893 | **612** | **8× fewer** | | Time | 31 s | **12 s** | **2.6× faster** |

The same question, the same model, answered both ways. Both pages are usable.

The token counts are saved in [bench/corpus/tokens.json](bench/corpus/tokens.json), so `node bench/corpus.mjs` gives the same numbers every time. The pages themselves are a [download](https://github.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html/releases/download/v0.4.14/bench-corpus-2026-10-07.zip). The bill drops less than the writing, about 15% here, because every turn also reads the system prompt, your question and the conversation, with or without the skill. See [where the cost goes](bench/README.md#where-the-cost-goes). Explainer videos save even more: about 18× fewer output tokens and 12× faster in [a small test](bench/README.md#explainer-videos). ## Install You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20 or newer. There is no `npm install` step. The CLI is bundled inside the skill. No Node.js yet? With the recommended install below, your agent asks you and then installs it. ### Let your agent install it (recommended) Paste this into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode or any other agent: > Install Answer me with HTML: read https://raw.githubusercontent.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html/main/INSTALL.md and follow it. [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) is written for agents. It installs the plugin in Claude Code and the skill in other agents, keeps an existing install, asks you nothing unless Node.js is missing or older than 20, and ends with one report after checking the result with the TCP three-way handshake page. If your agent cannot open links, use `npx -y skills add QingYunA/answer-me-with-html -g -y -a ` (for Claude Code, `-a claude-code`). ### Claude Code plugin Run this inside Claude Code: ``` /plugin marketplace add QingYunA/answer-me-with-html /plugin install answer-me-with-html@answer-me-with-html ``` ### DeepSeek Harness plugin Run this in a terminal, with the profile you run in (`web` is the shipped one): ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add github:QingYunA/answer-me-with-html ``` ### One command ```bash npx skills add QingYunA/answer-me-with-html ``` It asks which agents to install into. The installer, [vercel-labs/skills](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills), supports more than 70 agents.
Manual install Copy the `skills/answer-me-with-html` folder into your agent's skill folder. For Claude Code: ```bash git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.git /tmp/answer-me-with-html cp -R /tmp/answer-me-with-html/skills/answer-me-with-html ~/.claude/skills/answer-me-with-html ``` Skill folders for other agents: Codex `~/.codex/skills/`, Cursor `~/.cursor/skills/`, OpenCode `~/.config/opencode/skill/`.
No setup is needed after install. **We recommend turning on [always-on mode](#always-on-mode-recommended)**: the agent then adds a page to every conclusion, not only the hard ones. It takes one rule in your rules file. ## What you ask, what you get | You ask | You get | | :--- | :--- | | "Explain the TCP three-way handshake" | A sequence diagram, a state diagram and a flag table | | "How are the modules in this repo organized?" | A folder tree plus a call graph | | "Redis or Memcached?" | A comparison table with ✓ and ✗, then a verdict | | "What's wrong with this paragraph?" | Each sentence annotated, with the problem words and fixes | | "How did Kubernetes come about?" | A timeline with the key moments highlighted | | "Plan the cache change" | The real code from your files, and the open decisions as options you answer on the page | | "How do I show hidden files with `ls`?" | No page. A one-line question gets a one-line answer | The agent decides when a page is worth it: related concepts, multi-step flows, multi-way comparisons. You can also just say "explain it in HTML". Pages are saved in `~/.answer-me-with-html/pages/`. The buttons in the top-right corner switch the theme and light/dark mode, collect your reply, and copy the Markdown that produced the page. ## How is this different from Archify or GenUI plugins? [Archify](https://github.com/tt-a1i/archify) makes one interactive diagram from a JSON spec. GenUI plugins such as [dsh-genui](https://github.com/omdsh-dev/dsh-genui) show components inside one chat app. This skill answers the whole question as one page: text, tables, code and diagrams, from a Markdown draft, in any agent that can run a shell command. See the [full comparison](docs/compare.md). ## Explainer videos Karpathy's ladder for understanding LLM output ends with explainer videos. Ask for one in 3Blue1Brown style: "make a 3b1b-style video on the TCP handshake".

The agent writes the same kind of draft as for a page, plus one line of narration per beat. Nothing else: ````markdown ## Both sides wait ```sequence Client -> Server: SYN Server -> Client: SYN-ACK ``` > The client sends a SYN to ask for a connection. > The [Server] answers with a SYN-ACK. ```` `am video` turns it into a player page. The diagram builds step by step with the narration, and the camera follows the node named in brackets. The voice is inside the page, so it plays offline. The player has a chapter strip to jump between scenes, a speed button, and an export button that encodes the video in the browser and downloads it (a local file or `localhost`, no ffmpeg). Add `--mp4` for an MP4 file (needs ffmpeg), or `--webm` for a WebM file the page encodes itself (no ffmpeg). The agent only makes videos when you ask. Details: [video guide](docs/video.md). ## Settings Change settings with a slash command. There are no config files to edit by hand. | Where | How | | :--- | :--- | | Claude Code (plugin install) | `/answer-me-with-html:config` asks what to change. `/answer-me-with-html:config open off` changes it directly | | Any agent | `/answer-me-with-html config open off`, or just say "stop opening the browser" | | Terminal | `am config` to view, `am config set open off` to change, `am config reset` to restore defaults | The settings are `open` (open pages in the browser), `theme`, `mode` (light or dark), `style` (writing check), `update_check`, `close_after_reply` (close the tab after the reply is copied) and `voice` (video narration). Defaults and values: [reference](docs/reference.md#settings). ## Always-on mode (recommended) With always-on mode, **every conclusion comes with a page**: whenever the agent gives a conclusion, summary, plan or comparison, even a short one, it adds a small page with 2 to 4 panels and puts the path at the end of the reply. These pages never pop open, so they don't interrupt you. Casual chat and replies with no conclusion stay as they are. Claude Code makes no pages in plan mode. It is off by default. We recommend it: you stop asking for pages, and short answers read as well as long ones. Pages pile up in `~/.answer-me-with-html/`; clear them with `am clean`. To turn it on, paste this to your agent so it writes the rule into its rules file, such as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`: > Turn on always-on mode for Answer me with HTML: add a global rule — "[answer-me-with-html always-on] Whenever a reply gives a conclusion, summary, plan, comparison, review or explanation, even a short one, also make a page with the answer-me-with-html skill (2 to 4 panels for routine answers), render it with --no-open before you write the reply, and end the reply with the page link in the format SKILL.md specifies for your host. Skip casual chat, one- or two-sentence replies with no conclusion, pure command output, and requests for plain text." To turn it off, delete that rule. Want fewer pages instead? See [less proactive](docs/reference.md#less-proactive). ## Updating and cleaning up Updates are manual. When used, the CLI checks GitHub for a new version in the background at most once a day. If one is available, it prompts the agent at most once every three days; nothing about you is sent. To update, tell your agent "update answer-me-with-html". Pages pile up in `~/.answer-me-with-html/`. Say "clean up the pages", and the agent asks before it deletes anything. Other install methods and every option: [reference](docs/reference.md#updating-and-cleaning-up). ## Background Andrej Karpathy [posted](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2105819303471976479) that as LLMs do more of the work, keeping up with their output becomes the hard part. A diagram or a web page is far easier to take in than a long block of text. I tried asking agents to answer in HTML directly. The pages were good, but slow: a decent page took a minute or two, mostly hundreds of lines of CSS that were nearly the same every time. Diagrams were worse. The model had to compute SVG coordinates by hand, and arrows often pointed at nothing. So Answer me with HTML takes that work away from the model. The model writes content. The CLI handles layout, color and drawing. ## How it works This is all the model writes: ````markdown --- title: TCP three-way handshake --- ## A Three-way handshake {span=2} ```sequence num Client -> Server: SYN, seq=x Server -> Client: SYN+ACK, seq=y, ack=x+1 Client -> Server: ACK, ack=y+1 note Client, Server: ESTABLISHED ``` ## C State changes {span=2} ```flow LR (CLOSED) -> LISTEN: passive open LISTEN -> SYN_RCVD: get SYN / send SYN+ACK SYN_RCVD -> *ESTABLISHED: get ACK ``` ```` The CLI does the rest. It picks the template, places the panels, applies the theme, lays out the flow chart with [dagre](https://github.com/dagrejs/dagre) and spaces the sequence diagram by label width. The full draft, [examples/tcp.en.md](examples/tcp.en.md), becomes this page:

## Features - **Layout by code:** Panel placement and diagram coordinates are computed, not guessed. Labels don't get cut off, and there are no gaps in the grid. - **Fixes its own mistakes:** When a draft has an error, the CLI returns the line number, the component and a correct example. The agent fixes it in one try. - **Three themes:** `blueprint` looks like an engineering drawing, `shadcn` uses clean cards, and `paper` is set for long reading. By default the CLI picks paper for long text and blueprint for diagrams. All have light and dark modes, and you can add your own or take one from the [theme catalog](https://answer-me-with-html.com/themes/). - **One file, no dependencies:** Each page is a single `.html` with no CDN links or web fonts. It opens offline and is easy to share. - **Languages:** Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), English and Japanese get their own buttons and fonts. Other languages work with English buttons. See [languages](docs/reference.md#languages). - **Writing check:** Drafts are checked against rules adapted from ASD-STE100: long sentences, wordy phrases, passive voice. It only warns unless you ask for strict mode. - **Real code, not retyped:** A code block can quote lines from your files (`src=` `lines=`), so the code on the page is the real code. Files outside the folder and files that hold keys are refused. - **Answer on the page:** Comment on any panel, and pick options in the decisions the agent asks (`ask`). The Reply button turns your answers and comments into one message to paste back to the agent. - **Keeps its source:** Every page embeds the Markdown that made it. Click "Copy source" to get it back.
Blueprint theme (examples/ste100.md) shadcn theme, dark mode
## Components The agent picks a component by the shape of the information: | Component | Good for | | :--- | :--- | | `flow` | Architecture, call chains, decision branches. Auto layout, with groups, decisions and databases | | `er` | A data model: entities with their columns (PK / FK / UK) and crow's-foot relationships | | `sequence` | Messages going back and forth between several parties over time | | `tree` | Folders, modules, taxonomies | | `timeline` | History, releases, phases | | `limits` | A value against its limit | | `chart` | Bars, lines or a pie from a table of numbers: several series, negative values, a highlighted row | | `annot` | Word-by-word notes on a sentence | | `kv` | Metadata, a drawing's title block | | `callout` | A conclusion, a tip, a warning | | `ask` | A decision you make on the page; the agent's suggestion starts selected | | Code block | Real code quoted from a file (`src=` `lines=`), or a sketch | | Table | Multi-way comparison. Write `ok` / `no` / `warn` in a cell to get ✓ ✗ ! | The draft format (frontmatter, `span`, `rows`, raw `html` / `svg` blocks) and how to call the CLI without an agent are in the [reference](docs/reference.md). Full syntax for a component: `am help `. ## The STE writing check [ASD-STE100](https://www.asd-ste100.org/) is a controlled form of English first used for aircraft maintenance manuals. Its rules are concrete: keep sentences short, give each word one meaning, write steps as commands. Karpathy noted that asking an LLM to follow these rules makes its writing much easier to read. Every render checks the parts a machine can check: sentence length, plain words, passive voice, and common Chinese typos and vague words. It only warns by default. Set `/answer-me-with-html:config style strict` to refuse drafts that fail, or `style:` in one draft. The full rule list: [reference](docs/reference.md#writing-check). ## Development ```bash git clone https://github.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html.git && cd answer-me-with-html npm install npm test # run the tests AM_E2E=1 npm test # also run end-to-end video tests (system TTS, Chrome, ffmpeg) npm run smoke:install # install for real with npx skills and validate the plugin manifests (needs network) npm run build # after changing src/, rebuild skills/answer-me-with-html/scripts/am.mjs npm run snapshot # compare rendered HTML with origin/main (refactors must not change it) ``` Maintainer conventions (generated bundle, page format, snapshot checks, reviewing PRs, releasing) are in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). There are two runtime dependencies: [marked](https://github.com/markedjs/marked) parses Markdown and [@dagrejs/dagre](https://github.com/dagrejs/dagre) lays out flow charts. Both are bundled into `am.mjs`. ## Community Ask questions, share pages you made, suggest features, or just say hi. - [Discord](https://discord.gg/sYQuRRZNzQ) - QQ group: `1127099407` - [LINUX DO](https://linux.do), a Chinese-language developer forum - [AtomGit](https://atomgit.com/weixin_43367137/answer-me-with-html) Found a bug? Please open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/QingYunA/answer-me-with-html/issues). ## Star History ## License [MIT](LICENSE). The Bangers font that a theme can embed is under the [SIL Open Font License 1.1](skills/answer-me-with-html/licenses/OFL-Bangers.txt).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-voice-mode [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/github/license/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode?style=flat-square&color=blue)](LICENSE) [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode?style=flat-square&color=brightgreen&include_prereleases)](https://github.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/releases) [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-voice-mode?style=flat-square&color=orange)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-voice-mode) [![Tests: 611 passing](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-611%20%E2%9C%93-2ea043?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/blob/main/docs/rules/STATE.md) DeepSeek Harness 语音双工对话模式：会话内一键进入 → 边说边出字的流式识别 → 停顿自动发送 → 最终答复按句流式朗读 + 实时字幕，开口即可打断（真 barge-in）。无需 API Key，识别模型在本地宿主端推理。 **中文** · [English](https://github.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/blob/HEAD/plugin/dsh-voice-mode/README.en.md) > **Full-duplex voice mode for DeepSeek Harness** — streamed ASR to an editable draft, sentence-by-sentence read-aloud with live captions, and speaking interrupts playback and the running turn. ![dsh-voice-mode 全双工语音对话](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/HEAD/assets/hero-banner.png) ![语音模式真实录制：流式转写 → 自动发送 → 按句朗读 + 实时字幕](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/HEAD/plugin/dsh-voice-mode/assets/demo-voice-flow.gif) > **运行时变更（最近：v0.7.18 ~ v0.7.24）**：① **设置面全版本打通**——dsh 0.1.7+ 上设置页与持久化修复（Settings → 语音模式 专属页、写入与重启保留）；② **国际化重做**——界面语言跟随 dsh 官方语言设置，中/英文完整一致、切换无需刷新；③ **修复 npm/pnpm 全新安装失败与 dsh ≥0.1.7 已安装形态「failed to import」**（0.7.17 及更早版本受影响，请升级到 ≥0.7.18）；④ **官方桌面端（Electron）下本地 Kokoro 修复**——需系统 PATH 上有 Node.js ≥18（或设 `DSHVM_NODE`）；⑤ **v0.7.24：恢复 Edge 云端朗读**——微软服务端自 2026-10-15 起拒绝旧版握手（v0.7.23 及更早的默认 Edge 朗读无声，本地 VITS / Kokoro 不受影响），内联的 msedge-tts 升到 2.1.0；朗读**连续失败时**会提示切换本地引擎；另有 host 加固（`/models/retry` 仅同源 POST、模型树路径校验、错误原文不下行）。兼容 dsh 至 0.2.1-rc.2（0.2.1-alpha.4/5 起设置入口移入侧栏底部「Account menu」弹出层，本插件两处入口仍有效）。 --- ## 🤝 Fork 增强（本仓库新增） 本仓库在上游 [haoku123/dsh-voice](https://github.com/haoku123/dsh-voice) 基础上加入了大量增强，核心如下（完整清单见 git 历史与 [docs/rules/STATE.md](https://github.com/qishuilalala/dsh-voice-mode/blob/main/docs/rules/STATE.md)）： - **朗读默认 Edge 云端；本地 TTS 可选（隐私优先）**：选本地则回复文本不出本机—— - 本地 VITS（`sherpa-onnx-vits-zh-ll`，纯中文，5 说话人）； - 本地 Kokoro（**中英混读**，103 音色；`int8` 默认约 109MB / 可选 `fp32` 约 311MB 音质更好），经 `sherpa-onnx-node` **原生 addon** 运行（无 WASM 内存上限，连续合成不崩）； - Edge 云端朗读保留为可选（设置 `ttsEngine: edge`）；设置面板「朗读引擎」热切换。 - **Kokoro 音色全量 103 个**（F0 实测标定性别），四个常用男声置顶带编号；音色面板用 **下拉列表 + ◀▶ 步进**切换； - **增量传输**：partial 只传新增 0.9 秒，长段按住说话松手**秒出定稿**（不再整段重传重解码）； - **交互增强**：输入框旁**模式切换按钮**（持续聆听 ⇄ 按住说话，保存到设置）；按住说模式下**按住才录、不按住不打断**； - **长段支持**：持续聆听连续多段自动拼成一条消息（内部按 30s 分块识别，跨块累积拼接），静音断句默认 1500 毫秒；按住说停顿不断句； - **朗读稳定性**：打断即终止在途合成释放 CPU；句间不再有 3-5 秒停顿；长朗读不触发空闲下线； - **安全加固**：会话存在性校验 / 回环+Origin 校验 / 全端点限流 / **ASR+TTS 全模型 SHA256 固定** / 下载域名白名单 / 重定向守卫。 > ℹ️ 顶部 `demo-voice-flow.gif` 是**当前界面的真实录制**（语音模式 → 边说边出字 → 停顿自动发送 → 按句朗读 + 实时字幕），由 `screenshots/scripts/capture-demo.mjs` 驱动真实链路产出；UI 持续演进，以实际界面为准。 --- ## ✨ 功能 - **语音模式**：输入框工具排麦克风按钮或全局快捷键 `Ctrl+Shift+V` 进入/退出；全局单活（同一时刻仅一个会话处于语音模式，切换会话自动让出） - **两种交互模式（输入框旁按钮或设置可切换，切换即持久化）**： - `toggle`（默认）持续聆听：RMS VAD 分段 → zipformer2 流式识别（边说边出字，实时字幕预览）→ 静音约 1500 毫秒断句进草稿，连续多段拼成一条消息，再静音约 1.2 秒（合计约 2.7 秒）自动发送；按住 `Ctrl` 强制立即发送 - `hold` 按住说话：短按进入/退出，**按住麦克风按钮说话、松手即发**（滑出取消、`Esc`/失焦放弃本段）；按住期间停顿不断句（上限 10 分钟）；`Ctrl` 按住即录、松开即发 - **唤醒词（可选，默认关）**：设置 `wakeWord` 后进入待机态，说出唤醒词才开始识别（如「你好小D」）。**可直接与命令连说**（「你好小D，帮我查天气」）——唤醒词会在定稿/字幕里自动剥掉、不进消息；匹配带容错（同音字替换「小莫→小墨」、首字错、前置语气词「呃/喂/我说」），建议 3-4 字；待机态状态条实时显示「说『x』开始 · 它听到的转写」，唤醒成败可自查。边界（重要）：**仅 `toggle` 模式生效**（`hold` / 手动打断下唤醒词静默失效）；**说完整一句后回到待机态需重说唤醒词**（只喊唤醒词、还没说命令时保持聆听，可停顿想好再说）；**朗读期说唤醒词不触发**（打断由 VAD 开口即触发，与唤醒词无关） - **字幕档位**：`captionFontSize` 4 档（0=12px / 1=14px / 2=18px / 3=24px）+ `captionMaxWidth` 3 档（0=50vw / 1=70vw / 2=90vw），窄屏自适应 - **让位语义**（ADR-0008）：`backchannelYield` 默认开—— 朗读期用户插话「嗯/对」自动让位 1.5s，真要说走硬打断；让 LLM 主动让出话轮（人格层让位）；关掉恢复改造前行为 - **输出链路**：只朗读最终答复的 `text-delta`（reasoning/工具调用不读），按句流式朗读（默认 Edge 云端；可切本地 VITS/Kokoro，中英混读选 Kokoro）+ 右下角实时字幕浮层；工具调用触发提示音；全文照常写入聊天记录；口语化提示词（设置 `spokenFormat`，默认开）让回复为自然短句、不带 Markdown 排版符号 - **开口打断（barge-in）**：服务端 Silero VAD 帧级检测 + 回声门控（echoGateDb）三档灵敏度 → 本地静音 + host 合成队列作废 + 正在运行的回合取消（保留半截并自然续入新消息）；朗读中自动切超灵敏档。开启唤醒词后打断**仍是开口即打断**（打断门控是 VAD，不是唤醒词；打断后回待机态） - **模型懒加载与进度**：首次使用自动下载识别/合成模型（`.part` 断点续传），状态条实时显示进度；可用 `npm run prefetch` 预下载 - **设置**：入口随 dsh 版本而不同（见下方「设置」），可调朗读引擎/音色/语速/打断灵敏度/静音停顿/空闲超时/模型镜像/自动发送/交互模式/唤醒词/口语化提示词/字幕档位/让位语义/让位窗口/打断语音抢救/LLM 纠错；**音色可试听**（按当前音色+语速即时合成预览，自定义 ShortName 亦可） - **界面语言**：跟随 dsh 的语言设置（设置 → 通用 → 语言），**切换即时生效、无需刷新**——设置页、语音状态条、字幕、音色名称/性别/口音、错误提示全部随之变化；LLM 口语化提示词也按界面语言选中/英文版。插件词典注册在 dsh 官方 locale 服务的 `voice-mode` 命名空间，社区语言包可据此补充其它语言，缺失的语言回落英文。插件名称与描述在「插件」页同样按语言显示。 - **容错与诊断**：麦克风被拒红点提示、模型下载失败可见提示、TTS 连接失败状态条提示（自动退避重试）、提交失败文字留在草稿、SSE 断线自动重连；识别/打断检测通道连续失败、状态同步断连时状态条给出提示（可自愈的瞬时失败不打扰）；SenseVoice 定稿超过 2 秒时状态条显示「识别中… Ns」递增（看得见它在工作）；「复制诊断」一键复制版本/运行状态/设置快照/阶段耗时——**不含任何转写原文**（隐私口径） - **空闲退出**：5 分钟无活动自动退出并释放麦克风（**正在朗读计为活动**，长朗读不会中途下线） --- ## 🚀 5 分钟上手（Quick Start） ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-voice-mode ``` bundle 插件安装后需重启 dsh 生效（Linux：`systemctl restart dsh`；其他平台重启 dsh 进程）。 **第一次用**： 1. 进入任一会话，按 `Ctrl+Shift+V`（或点输入区麦克风按钮）进入语音模式，状态条显示「聆听中…」； 2. 说一句完整的话（如「帮我看看今天的天气」）→ 实时字幕立即出现，停顿后自动发送； 3. AI 回复开始朗读时，**开口说话 → 朗读即刻停止，你的话被听见**（这就是 barge-in）。 --- ## ⌨️ 操作手势 | 手势 | 作用 | | --- | --- | | `Ctrl+Shift+V` | 进入 / 退出语音模式 | | 直接说话 | `toggle`：边说边出字，停顿约 1500 毫秒断句进草稿、再静音约 1.2 秒（合计约 2.7 秒）自动发送；按住 `Ctrl` 强制立即发送 | | 按住麦克风按钮 | `hold`：松手发送；短按退出；滑出 / `Esc` / 失焦放弃本段 | | 点输入框旁模式按钮 | 在「持续聆听 ⇄ 按住说」间切换（保存到设置） | | 说唤醒词 | 待机态激活识别（配置后） | | AI 朗读时开口说话 | 打断朗读并取消当前回合 | | 点状态条「退出」 | 退出语音模式 | | 点字幕浮层「跳过」 | 跳过当前句朗读 | --- ## ⚙️ 设置 **所有 dsh 版本通用入口：设置（Settings）→ 语音模式（Voice Mode）**。另有按版本不同的次要入口（卡片内容一致）： - dsh ≤ 0.1.5：设置 → Plugins → 插件配置 → 语音模式 - dsh 0.1.6-alpha 及以后（含 0.1.7、0.2.0）：左侧 **Plugins** → 已安装的 `dsh-voice-mode` → 详情页「语音模式」卡片 - dsh 0.1.7+ 起，设置保存在插件自有文件 `~/.dsh/voice-mode.settings.json`（`$DSH_HOME` 下），优先于 profile 配置里的同名键；首次运行会从旧 `settings.yaml(.imported)` 的 `voice-mode:` 段迁移一次；恢复默认请把该文件内容改成 `{}`（不要删除）。 | 键 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `ttsEngine` | `edge` | 朗读引擎：`edge` 微软云端（默认，快）/ `vits` 本地中文 / `kokoro` 本地中英；**即时生效** | | `kokoroModel` | `int8` | Kokoro 模型精度：`int8`（默认，109MB，纯 CPU/低带宽推荐）/ `fp32`（311MB，音质更好，独显/大内存推荐）；两档共用 103 音色，**即时生效** | | `voice` | 按引擎 | 音色：VITS 五说话人；Kokoro 103 个（下拉+◀▶，62 深沉/68 浑厚/75 清亮/76 磁性置顶）；Edge 进入时自动加载全量 322 个。行内「试听」可即时预览 | | `rate` | `1.1` |
