# dsh-engram

> **[English](README.md) · [中文](README.zh.md)**

[![CI](https://github.com/skepsun/dsh-engram/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/skepsun/dsh-engram/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Minimalist long-term memory for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness), distilled from the
[symbolic-index](https://github.com/skepsun/symbolic-index) and [pi-esr](https://github.com/skepsun/pi-esr) ideas —
with one goal: **save tokens**.

- **Zero-LLM intake** — auto-captures meaningful events from tool results by pure
  pattern matching (git milestones with a written `-m` commit message, edits to
  key files, repeated errors), plus an explicit `engram_store`. Nothing on the hot
  path calls a model, and pure plumbing — `git push` / `git stash` / silent
  commits — is deliberately never recorded (see *Auto-capture policy* below).
  Every write is run through a deterministic **secret redactor** first — API
  keys, JWTs, `Bearer` tokens, private keys, AWS/Stripe/Slack/GitHub tokens and
  `key=value` secret shapes are replaced with `<REDACTED:…>` markers before the
  dedup hash, the char cap, and storage, so sensitive text can never land on
  disk. Failing **test runs** are recognized by pure patterns (`npm test`,
  `node --test`, vitest/pytest/jest, failure lines) and captured as
  `tags:["error","test"]` entries with a raised signal. DSH **goal-domain
  integration**: a completed or blocked goal (`goal/change` session event)
  auto-sediments as a `handoff`/`error` memory (`tag:goal`), so the outcome of
  a goal survives its session (see the `GET /api/dsh-engram/goals` read surface).
- **User-correction / preference learning (`autoCapturePreferences`, default on,
  zero LLM)** — the lesson that "when the AI makes a mistake and gets corrected,
  that lesson should persist" ([correx](https://github.com/ozoz5/correx),
  [PAHF](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.16173), Mem0 preference extraction): a
  `session/event` listener watches `user/message` and turns deterministic
  correction/preference cues into a dedicated `preference` memory kind —
  Chinese (`不要用X`, `改用X`, `以后统一用X`…) and English (`don't use X`,
  `switch to X`, `prefer X`, `never use X`…) patterns, three directions
  (`avoid` / `switch-to` / `prefer`), with interrogative/one-shot-instruction/
  memory-tool-meta-talk filters to keep false positives out. `preference`
  memories outrank every other kind in the `[ENGRAM]` block (`[R]` prefix) so a
  standing user rule is the first line the model sees each session; per-session
  cap + recent-window dedup mirror the auto-capture discipline. Zero LLM, zero
  embeddings, deterministic and pure — extracted clauses are bounded, and every
  write still goes through the secret redactor.
- **Symbolic index + progressive disclosure** — a compact `[ENGRAM]` block (default
  budget 700 chars ≈ 175 tokens; one line per memory) is injected at prompt
  assembly and **frozen per session**, keeping the request prefix byte-stable for
  KV-cache reuse. The agent drills down with `engram_recall` / `engram_detail` instead
  of dumping raw hits into context; recall ranks the in-domain pool with an
  in-process BM25 pass (TF·IDF with label/phrase boosts plus a gentle time-decay
  factor — deterministic, zero deps), appends a compact entity-neighborhood
  table (reusing esr_link: `node --rel--> node · conf%`) for entity-anchored
  hits, re-warms the old `error` entry when a new failure is near-identical
  (repeat-failure revival: recency + hit climb toward promoteHits so the
  failure resurfaces instead of piling up), and on zero local hits falls back
  to DSH's own cross-session full-text index (`ctx.sessionQuery`, filtered by
  cwd) instead of building a parallel SQLite index; when the FTS fallback also
  comes back empty and the query contains **CJK** characters (Chinese FTS5
  tokenization), recall runs a bounded substring scan over the newest session
  logs (zstd-decompressed, LRU-cached) and appends matched past sessions —
  deterministic `# past sessions` lines, capped files and bytes.
- **Session-start auto-recall (`autoRecallOnStart`, default on)** — the pull-only
  design had a gap proven in real use: recall tools relied on model initiative,
  and in practice the model almost never calls `engram_recall` on its own (19
  real sessions, thousands of tool calls, ~5 recall calls total). So at the FIRST
  assembly of a new session the host runs one deterministic BM25 recall keyed on
  the session's first user message and injects the top ≤ `autoRecallLimit` hits
  as a `[RECALL]` block (default 700-char budget, "few and precise" — agentmemory
  candidate ①). Relevant memory is in context even without a single recall call.
  Pure rule, zero LLM, pure read (never bumps `hits`); superseded stale truth does
  not occupy an injection slot (still fetchable via `engram_detail`); frozen per
  session together with `[ENGRAM]` for prefix stability.
- **Read-path activation (D)** — a hit whose one-line preview is truncated
  (>140 chars) carries a `…` marker and the block's trailing guidance names that
  concrete id: `#<id> truncated — engram_detail <id> (full) · engram_recall <query>`.
  So the model knows the full record is one deterministic `engram_detail` call
  away instead of assuming the preview is the whole memory (proven gap in real
  use: 66 sessions, zero `engram_detail` calls — the detail path was invisible).
- **Memory-to-memory semantics** — `engram_store` accepts optional
  `supersedes` / `contradicts` memory ids (validated against the same
  workspace). A superseded ("stale truth") memory is demoted to the tail of
  recall and **excluded from the `[ENGRAM]` block**, while the superseding
  statement keeps the line; a contradicted memory stays ranked but is flagged
  `· contradicted by <id>`. Old rows are never deleted — re-fetchable, just
  honestly ranked. Opt-in `autoSupersede` config (default **off**) auto-marks
  entity-anchored replacement updates ("改用 / no longer / switched…") as
  superseding their matching older row; explicit `supersedes` always wins.
- **Failure→fix closure (zero LLM)** — error memories carry a `cmd:` signature
  tag; when that same command later succeeds, engram auto-sediments a
  `procedure` memory (`fixed: <cmd> — N earlier failing runs now succeed`),
  tags the earlier error rows `resolved` (never re-ranking them), and recall
  then surfaces the fix instead of the stale failure.
- **ESR-lite closure protocol** — `esr_task` / `esr_close` / `esr_link` give tasks
  a `draft → active → stable` lifecycle where `stable` requires real evidence
  (`artifact` / `evaluation` / `memory_ref`), surfacing closure gaps instead of
  letting the agent declare victory without proof. With `verifyArtifact` on
  (default), a non-URL artifact is resolved against the workspace (= the session
  cwd) and must exist on disk — otherwise the task stays ACTIVE with the reason;
  `force:true` (or disabling the toggle) skips the disk check, the three gates
  are still mandatory. The tool and the web forms share one gate
  (`store.evidenceGate`), so the two surfaces can never drift.
  Tasks are never isolated graph nodes: `esr_task(entity=…)` one-call wiring
  auto-creates the `ent_<slug>` node and hangs the task on it
  (`task --relates_to--> entity`, idempotent), so a task created with a domain
  anchor immediately shows a relation; and `esr_dep` writes the dependency edge
  into both the task's `deps` (blocker logic) and the shared links table, making
  every task dependency a first-class visible edge in the graph.
- **ESR trigger mechanism (pi-esr-aligned, hybrid: static protocol + frozen
  snapshot + monotonically accumulated actionables + pull)** — prefix-cache
  stability is the point. Teaching the model WHEN to use ESR is a **static
  methodology** section (byte-identical every turn); the `[ESR]` block is a
  deterministic **per-session frozen snapshot** (set at session start,
  deterministically sorted, timestamps excluded, explicitly "WILL NOT
  auto-refresh") **plus the session's monotonically accumulated actionables**:
  the `promote:` / `root-cause:` / `close:` / `stale:` / `escalate:` lines are
  APPENDED exactly once, the moment each matures, and stay frozen for the rest
  of the session (never removed) — so the prefix changes only when genuinely
  new decision-point info appears, never per-turn, while the timely nudges
  (narrow funnel / recurring failure / work done / stale / balance) stay in
  context. Live state is still **pulled** via `esr_status` (full deterministic
  view + `since_revision` short "unchanged" response + derived actionables).
  The `tools/result` recorder feeds the actionables' data sources; P4
  conversion metering stays (`#suggest-*` tags + 10-minute attribution +
  `GET /api/dsh-engram/triggerstats`). Pure rules, zero LLM.
- **Session-end todo auto-sink (draft safety net, `autoSinkTodosOnEnd` default
  on)** — during a session the native todo stays cheap, per-session working
  memory that dies with the session. But when a session closes at its teardown
  edge (`session/disposed`) while its plan still has pending todos, they are
  **auto-landed as ESR `draft` tasks** (name = the todo text, description
  marked 「源自会话计划」, deduped against existing task names, capped by
  `maxTasksPerWorkspace`), so the plan never silently evaporates. Sinking to
  **draft** — not active — keeps them out of the `[ESR]` active rows and creates
  no evidence obligation; an explicit `esr_claim` / `esr_task` step is still
  what promotes a draft to active. The "nothing auto-written during the
  session" trade-off is unchanged; only the end-of-session data-loss gap is
  closed. Disable via profile patch or the settings card.
- **Memory GC (pi-esr constraints)** — a scheduled, mechanical, archive-only
  sweep: TTL-expired memories are archived, over-cap workspaces evict the
  lowest-value entries, stable tasks past their retention window leave the
  `[ESR]` surface, and dangling link edges are dropped. The working set (active
  task refs, task memories, indexed hits) is never touched, and nothing is
  hard-deleted — every archived entry keeps its id and stays re-fetchable.
- **Context GC (auto-GC = replaces DSH's auto-compact)** — NOT the memory-panel
  GC. It takes over the host's `compaction` service and swaps DSH's lossy
  LLM-summary compression for **mechanical eviction + re-fetch pointers**:
  evicted turns are scanned for engram/ESR anchors (`#memory-id`, `tsk_*`,
  `ent_*`, `file_path`) and replaced with one line "this detail lives at
  `engram_detail` / `engram_recall` / the [ESR] block"; only un-provenanced
  turns get a scoped LLM narrative (`gcNarrative`, default on, off = fully
  mechanical). All six GC constraints hold (working-set-protected,
  pointer-salience, no-provenance-no-evict…); any error falls back to the
  default compressor — compaction is never broken.
- **Web viewer** — a memory browser with benchmark-ish stats and a config card,
  built entirely on DSH's native settings slots (no third-party UI package).

## Why another memory plugin?

Surveys of the existing DSH plugin ecosystem show the recall-bridge, approval-gate,
LLM-distillation and vector/graph niches are already crowded. dsh-engram fills the
three gaps that matter for token discipline:

1. **No model in the write path** — capture is deterministic pattern matching.
2. **No raw text in the prompt** — a bounded symbolic index is injected, plus the
   top ≤ N memories auto-recalled for the session's first message (within budget);
   deeper retrieval stays on demand ("retrieved ≠ full-text injected").
3. **Honest task closure** — STABLE cannot be declared without evidence.

DSH already provides cross-session FTS (`ctx.sessionQuery`), storage
(`ctx.storageDomain`), prompt-injection hooks and settings slots; dsh-engram is a
thin composition layer over them, not a re-implementation.

## Security model

The DSH plugin ecosystem is young and unvetted — there is no official directory,
no signature check, and the harness's read/write permission tiers do **not**
constrain what a plugin's own code can do. So the trust bar for a memory plugin
is higher than for a tool: a memory plugin sits on your prompt prefix and writes
to disk on your behalf. dsh-engram's model, stated plainly:

- **No network, ever.** The plugin has no outbound socket, no telemetry, no
  update pinger. Nothing here can leak your sessions off the machine.
- **No shell, no filesystem access beyond one storage file.** It never executes
  commands and never touches arbitrary paths. All data lives in the single
  storage-domain unit `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_engram.json` (plus the session-log
  reads it makes through DSH's own `ctx.sessionQuery`).
- **Secrets are redacted before they can land on disk.** Every write path —
  `engram_store`, auto-capture, and the import/restore route — runs text through
  the deterministic `redactText` rule engine (API keys, JWTs, `Bearer` tokens,
  private keys, `key=value` secret shapes) *before* the dedup hash, the char
  cap, and storage. Nothing sensitive is ever persisted, so nothing sensitive
  can be recalled later.
- **Doing harm requires your harness's own permissions.** The plugin only *asks*
  the host to do things via the same seams the tools you already trust use. It
  does not widen sandbox policy or escalate to `danger-full-access` — if you
  keep your profile's defaults, engram inherits exactly those bounds.
- **Read-mostly web API, loopback-fenced.** The GUI routes under
  `/api/dsh-engram` reject any non-loopback caller unless you explicitly
  whitelist a hostname via `trustedHosts`; even then the same-origin fence holds.
- **Verifiable.** `npm run dsh-engram -- doctor` (`/scripts/dsh-engram.mjs
  doctor`) reports what the plugin is configured to touch; the whole store is
  inspectable, nothing is opaque. If you ever doubt a claim in this section, the
  code to check is `lib/redact.js`, `lib/store.js` and this plugin's
  `cordis.patch.yml`.

What this deliberately does **not** claim: it is not an air-gap. If your profile
grants the agent `danger-full-access` or a shell, the agent can use those —
engram is a memory layer, not a sandbox. The point above is that *dsh-engram
itself* adds no surface of its own.

## Data contract: export / import

Memory should not be a hostage. The four tables (memories / tasks / links /
entities) can be dumped and restored through a stable, versioned, machine-readable
shape — so the corpus survives a reinstall, a machine move, or (when a thin
adapter is written) a move to another harness, MCP end-point or Claude Code
skill. The contract is plain JSON with a self-describing header:

```http
GET  /api/dsh-engram/export?workspace=/path/to/project   # one workspace
GET  /api/dsh-engram/export                              # every workspace
```

```jsonc
{
  "meta": { "format": "dsh-engram/export", "version": 1, "exportedAt": 1724…, "workspace": "/path/to/project" },
  "memories": [ /* all rows, archived included — a backup never loses provenance */ ],
  "tasks":    [ /* draft/active/stable + archived */ ],
  "links":    [ /* typed edges */ ],
  "entities": [ /* graph nodes */ ]
}
```

Restore is idempotent by default and gated when destructive:

```http
POST /api/dsh-engram/import          # body: { payload, mode, dryRun?, workspace?, confirm? }
```

- **`mode: "merge"`** (default) — writes only rows whose `id` is absent, so a
  backup can be re-applied any number of times without duplicating anything. Each
  row keeps its own `workspace`.
- **`mode: "replace"`** — wipes the target `workspace` from all four tables, then
  restores only its rows. Destructive, so it additionally requires
  `confirm: "restore"` in the body.
- **`dryRun: true`** — computes the identical plan (what would be written /
  skipped) without writing a single row.
- **Import honors the same invariants as `storeMemory`**: memory text passes the
  secret redactor before touching disk, and rows that would break the contract
  (missing id/workspace, empty text, over `maxMemoryChars`, id already present
  in merge, over the workspace memory cap) are skipped and listed in the
  response report instead of aborting the batch.

A restore round-trip for one workspace is then:

```sh
curl -s "http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-engram/export?workspace=$PWD" -o engram-backup.json
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3080/api/dsh-engram/import \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d "{\"payload\": $(cat engram-backup.json), \"mode\": \"merge\"}"
```

### Where the API family broke — `0.1.2-alpha.2`

`0.1.2-alpha.2` is the first version of the new API family and the first that
**breaks** the released plugin versions:

- `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` **removed** `settingsNamespace()` and
  `installSettingsSection()` — the exact imports every release ≤ `0.3.6` uses —
  and replaced them with `settings.installSection`. The old host half fails to
  load on `0.1.2-alpha.2+`.
- The web client half swapped its inject set: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime`
  no longer exists in the new family (replaced by `dsh-api-remotes` plus
  `dsh-client-locale` / `-conversation` / `-renderer` / `-ui-settings-plugins`),
  and the settings card used to talk through `ctx.remote.settings`.
- Supporting bumps at the same boundary: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1 → ^4.0.2`,
  `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `^3.18.1 → ^3.18.2`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh` stopped
  shipping `config/agent-presets` in the package (moved to `dsh.configTrees`).

The web config card no longer depends on any of this: since `0.3.7` it reads
and writes the `dsh-engram` settings namespace through the plugin's **own**
HTTP route (`/api/dsh-engram/settings`, same-origin fetch like the memory
viewer), so the card is generation-agnostic on both sides of the
`0.1.2-alpha.2` boundary.

**One more settings break, at `0.1.7` / `0.2.0`** — and the reason `0.4.0` was
not actually loadable on the current DSH: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-settings` **removed
`settings.installSection` again** in `0.1.7-alpha.2` (and keeps it removed in
`0.2.x`). The new settings model is **entry-keyed**: editable fields are
`.volatile()` fields of the plugin's own `Config` (validated + hot-committed by
the loader), and the settings form is keyed by the profile entry id (`engram`),
so nothing needs "mounting". `0.5.0` feature-detects the two generations in
`installEngramSettings`:

- DSH `≥0.1.7` / `0.2.x` — the 34 GUI knobs are the volatile `Config` fields
  (`lib/settings.js` `makeEngineConfigSchema`, exported as `Config` from
  `lib/index.js`); the card reads/writes entry `engram` through the same
  `/api/dsh-engram/settings` HTTP route, and the `service.settings` seam
  re-syncs `resolved` on `loader/volatile-update` so card edits land live on
  new sessions.
- DSH `≤0.1.5` — the legacy `settings.installSection` namespace (`dsh-engram`)
  is registered as before; nothing changes.

The declared range `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.3.0-0` covers both, and the HTTP wire
namespace stays `dsh-engram` on both generations (the seam's active namespace
drives mutations).

So: keep DSH on `0.1.1-rc.2` or older while running a release ≤ `0.3.6`, and
upgrade the plugin to `>=0.3.7` before moving DSH to `0.1.2-alpha.2`.

### Current release — `0.7.0`

From event records to **maintainable current truth**: sessions sediment an
episode at teardown, new sessions get a resume brief, `esr_node` becomes a
readable page, and file anchors make stale truth detectable.

- **Session episode** — zero-LLM digest at `session/disposed` (files / commands /
  failures→fixed / decisions / open loops), never indexed, newest 20 per
  workspace kept.
- **Resume brief** — the newest episode from the last 7 days is injected as a
  `[RESUME]` line (≤240 chars + drill pointer) at session start.
- **Entity pages + cards** — `truth / timeline / open loops / conflicts /
  relations`; up to 2 one-line cards in the index, full page via
  `engram_detail(entity=…)`.
- **Revalidatable anchors** — file-backed memories record `mtime/size/sha256`;
  a bounded revalidation at session start tags changed/missing sources `stale`
  (dropped from index/truth, still re-fetchable).
- **Layered TTL** — preference/procedure permanent, episode 14d, error 60d,
  others 180d.
- **Migration** — only new writes are anchored (no historical backfill);
  restart `dsh web` after upgrading; an episode appears after one session ends,
  the resume brief on the next new session. The `0.6.0` ledger / defaults / JIT
  behaviour is unchanged.

The published `0.4.0` declared `>=0.1.2-alpha.2 <0.2.0-0` — which the semver
gate **rejects on every DSH `0.2.0-0` prerelease** (`<0.2.0-0` excludes
`0.2.0-rc.x`), and its host settings half still called the `installSection`
API that `dsh-settings 0.1.7+` removed. `0.5.0` fixes **both**: the range
opens to `<0.3.0-0` (verified against DSH's own `includePrerelease` check, so
`0.2.0-rc.2` and the whole `0.2.x` line pass), and the settings card is
migrated onto the entry-id **volatile Config** model described above (with a
feature-detected legacy fallback).

## Install

```sh
# from GitHub (this repo)
dsh plugin --profile web add github:skepsun/dsh-engram

# once published to npm
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-engram

# local development (symlink — edits apply immediately)
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/path/to/dsh-engram
```

Then **restart `dsh web`**. Data persists in `~/.dsh/storages/dsh_engram.json`.

> The npm and GitHub installs below need **no manual dependency step**: pnpm
> installs `zod` and vendors the optional `@deepseek-ai/*` peers into the
> plugin's own `node_modules`, and the CLI auto-registers the plugin into the
> profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`. The `setup-links` step below is only for
> the `link:` development workflow, where pnpm deliberately does not install a
> symlinked directory's dependencies.

> A fresh session is required to see the injected `[ENGRAM]`/`[ESR]` blocks and the
> tools; both prompts and the tools registry are assembled per session.

### Dependencies for `link:` installs

A *symlinked* plugin resolves its imports from its own `node_modules`, so the
host-side dependencies must be present **next to the checkout** — they are not
tracked by git:

```sh
cd /path/to/dsh-engram
node scripts/setup-links.mjs     # one command: links the @deepseek-ai
                                 # workspace packages into node_modules AND
                                 # installs zod (reused from the harness
                                 # pnpm store, or via `npm install`)
```

The script auto-locates the harness checkout at `../deepseek-harness` (also
works when it sits next to the repo's *parent*, e.g. `E:\deepseek-harness` +
`E:\kototoro_demo\dsh-engram`); override with `DSH_HARNESS_DIR`. Without this

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# AI App Foundry

AI-powered development toolkit for iOS apps and backends, with reusable agents, skills, and workflows for planning, coding, review, testing, and releases.

## Included in 0.2.0

- **[publish-app-release](skills/publish-app-release/SKILL.md)**: prepare App Store Description and What's New in the app's requested locales; manage authorized versioning and GitHub release stages; create and verify signed archives; export IPAs; upload to App Store Connect.
- A standard-library Python CLI with signing, identity, provenance, dSYM, and duplicate-upload checks.
- Offline tests that use fake external tools and never build, sign, or upload a real app.
- Client packaging for Codex, Claude Code, and DeepSeek Harness: the DSH plugin bundle in `package.json`, `cordis.patch.yml`, and [`dsh/index.mjs`](dsh/index.mjs) serves the same `skills/` directory in DSH sessions.

The release skill supports iOS app repositories with `.xcodeproj` or `.xcworkspace` containers, explicit or unambiguous scheme selection, independent scheme/target names, and custom build configurations. It reads application identity and release conventions from the selected checkout. Backend skills are planned; none are included in this version.

## Install in Codex

Add this repository as a plugin marketplace:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add TeleginS/ai-app-foundry
```

Then open the plugin browser, find **AI App Foundry**, and install it. Adding a marketplace makes its plugin discoverable; it does not itself install or activate the plugin. Available installation controls depend on the Codex client and workspace policy.

The repository includes a portable `plugin.json`, a Codex compatibility manifest at `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, and a marketplace catalog at `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. No MCP server or service connection is bundled.

See the official [plugin packaging and installation documentation](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/build/plugins).

## Install in Claude Code

Install the plugin from this repository's marketplace (Claude Code 2.1.275 or later):

```text
/plugin install ai-app-foundry --marketplace TeleginS/ai-app-foundry
```

On older versions, add the marketplace first and then install:

```text
/plugin marketplace add TeleginS/ai-app-foundry
/plugin install ai-app-foundry@ai-app-foundry
```

The Claude Code manifests live in `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`; they share the same `skills/` directory with Codex. See the [Claude Code plugin documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins).

## Install in DeepSeek Harness

DSH installs skills through plugin bundles. This repository is also one: the root `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, and [`dsh/index.mjs`](dsh/index.mjs) registers a bundled skill provider, so every skill under `skills/` appears in the DSH session catalog. Add the repository to the profile your DSH app boots (for example `web`):

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add github:TeleginS/ai-app-foundry
```

To install from a local checkout instead, pass its absolute path to the same command, for example `dsh plugin --profile web add /absolute/path/to/ai-app-foundry`.

The bundle needs a profile that mounts the skill registry; profiles built from `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base`, including the shipped `web`, `headless`, `acp`, and `sdk` profiles, do. It contributes only a skill provider: no tools, MCP servers, network connections, credentials, or dsh peer dependencies. Installed bundles are listed on DSH's **Plugins** page and can be disabled, removed, or installed from there as well. Remove it with:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove ai-app-foundry
```

DSH also discovers local skills without a bundle: link the skill directory into `~/.agents/skills/` (shared agent configuration) or into a project's `.agents/skills/` or `.dsh/skills/`, and DSH picks it up on the next step. That is the quickest way to try the skill from a checkout before installing the bundle.

## Use

Open the application checkout and invoke the installed **Publish App Release** skill. For example, in Codex:

```text
Use $publish-app-release to prepare App Store metadata for the current version in English and Spanish.
```

```text
Use $publish-app-release to create a signed archive of the current version. Archive only.
```

In Claude Code, invoke it as `/ai-app-foundry:publish-app-release` or describe the task and Claude loads the skill automatically:

```text
/ai-app-foundry:publish-app-release prepare App Store metadata for the current version in English and Spanish
```

In DSH, describe the task and the agent loads the skill from its catalog, or invoke it explicitly by name:

```text
/publish-app-release prepare App Store metadata for the current version in English and Spanish
```

Only requested stages run. Installing this plugin does not publish a release, upload a build, change App Store metadata, or submit an app for review.

For direct CLI use, resolve `SKILL_DIR` to the installed `skills/publish-app-release` directory and pass the application checkout explicitly:

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/app_store_build.py" inspect \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/application-repo
```

For a workspace or an ambiguous checkout, pass its selection explicitly:

```bash
python3 "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/app_store_build.py" inspect \
  --repo /absolute/path/to/application-repo \
  --workspace 'Client Workspace.xcworkspace' --scheme 'Store Scheme'
```

Use the resolved bundle ID as `--bundle-id com.example.app` for `archive`, `verify-archive`, `export`, `verify-ipa`, and `upload`. These commands reject a different app identity; they never rewrite it. `--target` selects among multiple native app targets; `--configuration` and `--validation-configuration` support custom configuration names. Source provenance covers the entire Git checkout so shared code and configuration changes are included. See the [CLI contract and examples](skills/publish-app-release/references/app-store-build.md).

The CLI defaults to the current working directory when `--repo` is omitted. It never derives the app repository from the plugin cache path. Use absolute paths for installed scripts; do not assume they exist inside the application checkout.

Archive/export/upload requires macOS, Xcode, Python 3.9+, and an appropriate signing account. GitHub publication requires Git and authenticated GitHub CLI access. App Store Connect uploads require the existing app record and appropriate Apple access. Credentials and signing artifacts are not included. Codebase Memory can assist source inspection when installed; it is optional for this package.

## Develop and validate

From the repository root:

```bash
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m unittest discover \
  -s skills/publish-app-release/tests -v
```

The DSH plugin has its own offline tests; they mount the plugin with a fake skill registry and check the bundled catalog:

```bash
node --test
```

Add further skills as `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`, with supporting resources inside that skill's directory. The DSH provider discovers them automatically; no bundle edit is needed. Update the plugin version in all manifests together when publishing package changes: `plugin.json`, `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, and the DSH bundle's root `package.json`. Validate the Claude Code manifests with:

```bash
claude plugin validate .
```

## Origin

The release skill was imported from [TrafficRulesApp at e873cd6](https://github.com/TeleginS/TrafficRulesApp/tree/e873cd640058a75d29b8d9ab37fdfcf4b6787d7b/.agents/skills/publish-app-release), including its bullet-formatting rules, references, CLI, and offline tests. Version 0.2.0 generalizes app identity, project/workspace selection, source provenance, metadata locales, and release conventions for reuse across iOS apps. The original repository skill remains in place.

# dsh-compress-codex A DSH **bundle** that replaces the compaction policy behind the `ctx.compaction` seam with one whose **D1–D5 policy dimensions follow Codex** — same DSH transaction contract, different strategy. > **Provenance, stated precisely.** D1 (trigger) and D4 (summary prompt) are Codex-derived, as are > parts of D2/D5. **D3 (retention) and the anti-drift / idempotence layer (#9) are DSH-original** — > Codex has *no explicit anti-drift mechanism*, so describing the whole plugin as "Codex-style" is > wrong. See [`docs/codex-dsh-mapping.md`](docs/codex-dsh-mapping.md) §4: `lib/core/idempotence.js` > is explicitly *not* a Codex port. - Policy dimensions **D1 触发 / D2 切分 / D3 保留 / D4 摘要 / D5 注入**: [`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md) §1.3 - Codex source-level spec (every claim carries file+line evidence): [`docs/codex-notes.md`](docs/codex-notes.md) - Codex → DSH mapping, incl. what must **not** be copied: [`docs/codex-dsh-mapping.md`](docs/codex-dsh-mapping.md) - Layering, seam and transaction: [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) - What is verified vs not: [`docs/runtime-verification.md`](docs/runtime-verification.md) > **Read this first if you are wiring this into a runtime.** Four things bite people, and > they matter more than the feature list: > 1. **Host packages only resolve inside a booting dsh process** — see [§5.1](#51-host-packages-do-not-resolve-from-a-profile-directory). > 2. **Never smoke-test on the `web` template** — it already disables `compaction-basic`, so you get a false green ([§5.2](#52-the-web-template-is-a-false-green)). > 3. **`disabled: true` is load-bearing**: without it two engines provide `compaction` and the boot fails fatally ([§5.3](#53-disabling-the-official-row-is-load-bearing)). > 4. **Not everything is verified yet** — see [§6](#6-status-what-works-today). Interfaces, config and layer semantics follow the DSH plugin contract; for the plugin toolchain itself see the `dsh-plugin-construction` skill in your DSH install. --- ## 1. Why this exists The official `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic` is a solid backend, but its policy has three properties this project treats as defects ([`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md) §1.4): | # | Official behaviour | Why it hurts | |---|---|---| | 1 | Retention is a **token ratio** (`retainRatio: 0.16` of `W − O`) | It cannot tell "the last three task turns" from "50k tokens of older tool logs". Structure is not modelled. | | 2 | The summary is **free text** | There is no stable, resumable field set, so a resumed session relearns context. This plugin uses **Codex's four bullets** (progress and key decisions / context, constraints and preferences / what remains to be done / critical data and references) **plus two DSH-original fields** (`files`, `pitfalls`) that Codex does not have. | | 3 | Repeated compaction has **no drift convention** | Each round re-encodes; quality decays silently. | Codex answers all three — but only some of its answers survive DSH's contract constraints C1–C5. The mapping table marks every one of them as *copyable*, *needs adaptation* or *do not copy*. ## 2. How it plugs in It is a bundle: `package.json` declares `dsh.bundle.patch` → `cordis.patch.yml`, which performs exactly two operations on the layer `dsh-base` owns: ```yaml - id: compaction-basic name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic' disabled: true # keep exactly one implementation of ctx.compaction - insert: - id: compaction-codex name: 'dsh-compress-codex' config: {} ``` `command-compact` (`/compact`) and `tool-result-pruner` are intentionally untouched: they are backend-independent. ## 3. Install Requires a DSH with the plugin CLI (`dsh 0.2.1-rc.2` verified) and `pnpm` on `PATH`. ```sh # from a checkout dsh plugin --profile add /path/to/dsh-Compress-codex # or from a registry/tarball dsh plugin --profile add dsh-compress-codex ``` Then confirm the layer landed **without booting anything**: ```sh dsh --profile --dump-config | grep -B1 -A3 -E 'id: compaction-(basic|codex)' ``` Expected: `compaction-basic` is `disabled: true` **and** annotated `patched by dsh-compress-codex`; `compaction-codex` resolves to `dsh-compress-codex`. The annotation matters — `disabled: true` alone could come from the template ([§5.2](#52-the-web-template-is-a-false-green)). ### Peer dependencies `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic` and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` are **peer dependencies** (and dev dependencies). They must never be moved into `dependencies`: the host shares one instance, and a second copy fails module resolution. A link install keeps them unresolved in the profile's `node_modules`; that is normal and is why [§5.1](#51-host-packages-do-not-resolve-from-a-profile-directory) exists. ### Configuration Row config is a **whole replacement**, not a deep merge. All keys optional; unknown keys fail at mount time instead of silently behaving like the default. | Key | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `triggerLimitTokens` | — | Absolute trigger limit (Codex `config.limit`) | | `triggerLimitRatio` | `0.9` | `limit = min(triggerLimitTokens ?? ∞, floor(W × ratio))` | | `effectiveWindowPercent` | `0.95` | Hard-full ceiling: `full = floor(W × percent)` | | `triggerBufferTokens` | `0` | Buffer added **on the limit side** | | `turnEndPercent` | `0` | Turn-end check; `0` disables it | | `overflowRecovery` | `true` | Bypass thresholds on `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` | | `retainMode` | `'structural'` | Retention by dialogue structure, not by token ratio | | `retainRecentUnits` | `3` | Recent structural units kept verbatim | | `retainTokens` | — | **Soft** ceiling: whole units in or out, never half a tool pair | | `summaryTemplate` | `'codex-v1'` | Template version for measuring drift. **The id is ours**, not Codex's — Codex has no template-version concept | | `summaryExtraFields` | `['files','pitfalls']` | Codex's four fields + our two | Defaults and rationale: [`docs/codex-impl-checklist.md`](docs/codex-impl-checklist.md) §1.1. ## 4. Verify Three levels, cheapest first: 1. **Composition** — `dsh --profile

--dump-config` (see §3). Any stale override prints `patch: entry "" not found`. This warning appears **only** in `--dump-config`. 2. **Real boot, offline** — `node scripts/smoke-runtime.mjs` runs a throwaway `DSH_HOME`, installs this bundle into a minimal profile, and asserts composition, the negative control, **and that the real mount resolves the real base class inside a booting dsh process**. 3. **Session level** — `SMOKE_SESSION=1` drives a real two-turn session on a real model and asserts the full `compaction/start → compaction/summary → user/message → compaction/end` transaction. Verified; see §6 and §4.3 of the verification record for what it does **not** prove. ```sh node scripts/smoke-runtime.mjs # A1-A6; A7 not requested -> exit 2 (INCOMPLETE) SMOKE_SESSION=1 node scripts/smoke-runtime.mjs # + A7 on a real model (needs a credential) SMOKE_KEEP=1 node scripts/smoke-runtime.mjs # keep the temp home for debugging ``` A skip is **not** a pass, and the exit code enforces it instead of merely asking: | exit | meaning | |---|---| | `0` | every assertion ran and passed — a **complete** run | | `1` | at least one assertion **failed** | | `2` | everything that ran passed, but something was **skipped** (or a prerequisite was missing) — the run is **INCOMPLETE** | The conclusion line says so in words as well — `SMOKE RESULT: INCOMPLETE — PASS WITH 1 SKIPPED, NOT fully verified (A7)` — and `0` is never printed for a partial run. A caller that **deliberately** does not ask for an opt-in assertion declares that scope with `SMOKE_ALLOW_SKIP=1`, which maps an otherwise-clean incomplete run to `0` while printing the same line. `ci / compat-next` has no model credential, so it must pass that variable. ## 5. Four things that bite ### 5.1 Host packages do not resolve from a profile directory ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/

" && node --input-type=module -e "await import('@deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic')" # -> ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND ``` Yet inside a booting dsh process the same import **succeeds**: the loader supplies installation-scope resolution at boot. A profile's `node_modules` holds only the linked plugin. **A "resolve the host package from a bare node process" assertion is a false negative**; assert the mount from inside a boot instead (that is what `smoke-runtime.mjs` A6 does). Evidence: [`docs/runtime-verification.md`](docs/runtime-verification.md) §5.1. ### 5.2 The `web` template is a false green The `web` profile template **already disables `compaction-basic`** (that row belongs to `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`). Dump-config on `web` therefore shows `disabled: true` even with this bundle absent — the assertion is vacuous. Use `dsh plugin add` (minimal stack) and always keep a negative control profile. Evidence: [`docs/runtime-verification.md`](docs/runtime-verification.md) §1. ### 5.3 Disabling the official row is load-bearing Without `disabled: true` both engines provide `compaction` and the composition dies: ``` dsh: fatal load failure: Error: service "compaction" has been registered at at new CodexCompactionEngine (lib/engine.js) ``` So do not "clean up" that op. Evidence: [`docs/runtime-verification.md`](docs/runtime-verification.md) §5.2. ### 5.4 `--help` is not a smoke entry point `dsh --profile

--help` hangs on a plugin-add profile (observed 60s and 120s). Use the offline boot instead — no prompt, no network, no credential, ~2s: ```sh dsh --profile

--patch remove dsh-compress-codex # dependency + layer dsh --profile --dump-config | grep -B1 -A3 'id: compaction-basic' ``` `compaction-basic` must come back **enabled** and **without** the `patched by dsh-compress-codex` annotation. Nuclear option: recreate the profile with `dsh plugin --profile --from-default-profile

🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

--- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`. Install with a single command: ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. **Key Features:** - 🧠 **Persistent Memory** - Context survives across sessions - 📊 **Progressive Disclosure** - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility - 🔍 **Skill-Based Search** - Query your project history with mem-search skill - 🖥️ **Local My Work** - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **TeamBrain** - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Claude Desktop Skill** - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations - 🔒 **Privacy Control** - Use `` tags to exclude sensitive content from storage - ⚙️ **Context Configuration** - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected - 🤖 **Automatic Operation** - No manual intervention required - 🔗 **Citations** - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview)** - System components & data flow - **[Architecture Evolution](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture-evolution)** - The journey from v3 to v5 - **[Hooks Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture)** - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks - **[Hooks Reference](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/hooks)** - Every hook entry explained - **[Worker Service](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/worker-service)** - HTTP API & Bun management - **[Database](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database)** - SQLite schema & FTS5 search - **[Search Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/search-architecture)** - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database ### Configuration & Development - **[Configuration](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** - Environment variables & settings - **[Development](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** - Building, testing, contributing - **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** - Common issues & solutions --- ## How It Works **Core Components:** 1. **Lifecycle Hooks** - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, `claude-mem hook claude-code `, run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH 2. **Smart Install** - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on `claude --init` / `--maintenance`, plus `npx claude-mem install` / `repair`) 3. **Worker Service** - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun 4. **SQLite Database** - Stores sessions, observations, summaries 5. **mem-search Skill** - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure 6. **Chroma Vector Database** - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details. --- ## MCP Search Tools Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through **4 MCP tools** following a token-efficient **3-layer workflow pattern**: **The 3-Layer Workflow:** 1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result) 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result) **How It Works:** - Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory - Start with `search` to get an index of results - Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations - Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs - **~10x token savings** by filtering before fetching details **Available MCP Tools:** 1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs) **Example Usage:** ```typescript // Step 1: Search for index search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10) // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456) // Step 3: Fetch full details get_observations(ids=[123, 456]) ``` See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples. --- ## System Requirements - **Node.js**: 20.0.0 or higher - **Claude Code**: Latest version with plugin support - **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing) - **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing) - **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled) --- ### Windows Setup Notes If you see an error like: ```powershell npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet ``` Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation. Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks). --- ## Configuration Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings. To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources. See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples. ### Mode & Language Configuration Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting. This option controls both: - The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation) - The language used in generated observations #### How to Configure Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`: ```json { "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh" } ``` Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-token-budget

`dsh-token-budget` 是 [DeepSeek Harness（DSH）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的独立插件，作为社区插件 [`@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams`](https://github.com/NanmiCoder/dsh-agent-teams)（基线 `0.1.23`）的**补丁插件**：

- **不修改原插件源码**，与社区原版并存；原版升级不会覆盖本插件。
- **只作用于团队会话**（队长与成员），普通会话不受影响。
- 插件整体由 DSH 插件管理面板启停。

> 状态：**0.5.0 已完成**（2026-10-19，tag `v0.5.0`，未发 Release）：兼容 DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 与 agent-teams 0.1.25、w1 交接只发一次、普通子会话隐藏本插件工具，设计见 [`docs/design/0.5.0.md`](docs/design/0.5.0.md)。0.4.0（workspace 双层记录）见 tag `v0.4.0` 与 [`docs/design/0.4.0-workspace-notes.md`](docs/design/0.4.0-workspace-notes.md)，0.3.0（换窗交接）见 tag `v0.3.0`。权威设计见 [`docs/design/plugin-design.md`](docs/design/plugin-design.md) 与各版本设计文档。

## 它解决什么

团队成员长时间工作时上下文会被塞满，宿主压缩后成员常常丢掉进度。本插件：

1. **提前提醒**：成员上下文占用 37%、40% 各提醒一次，提示把进度写进笔记；第一次提醒说明可以调用 `context_new_window` 自己换窗。
2. **换窗不调模型**：成员到 45% 后（经下面的兜底）换到新窗口。换窗不发摘要请求，摘要位置换成一段【交接】：身份、任务与当前 `attempt_id`、笔记位置与更新状态、团队信件和上一窗口的回看指针。宿主约 80% 的自动压缩、手动 `/compact` 在团队会话里也用这段【交接】。
3. **兜底**：成员到 45% 时一律先注入一次强提示并多给 16384 token 额度（不论本窗口是否写过笔记，对齐 Codex）：把最新进展补记进笔记（尽量一次 `team_notes`），然后调用 `context_new_window`；额度用完照样换窗。【交接】里注明笔记状态：兜底开始后写的算已更新；额度用完时标「可能未写完」；只在兜底前写过标「可能未含最新进展」；没进兜底时，只有模型自己调用 `context_new_window` 换窗（成员提前换、队长主动换）才标已更新，宿主约 80% 自动压缩（含队长）即使本窗口写过也标「可能未含最新进展」；没写标「未更新」。成员看不到 `team_notes` 时不兜底，直接换窗。
4. **队长不强制**：队长只在 45%、48% 各提醒一次（不催促），不强制换窗。
5. **笔记**：每个成员一份独立笔记，团队共享一份 `workspace.md`（只有队长能写；成员任务结束时的笔记快照进入待合并清单，由队长或外接模型合并进去）。
6. **记录**：任务终态全文、成员笔记快照、`workspace.md` 每次修改前的快照都留在 `records/`，只读可查；团队代结束后自动归档。
7. **只读历史**：成员可以回看本会话先前窗口里被隐藏的原始消息，以及团队来往的信。

## 功能

| 能力 | 开关 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 换窗交接 | 无（插件本体） | 成员 37% / 40% 提醒，45% 先兜底再换窗；队长 45% / 48% 提醒。换窗经宿主压缩服务的 `compactIfNeeded`，接管 `summarize()` 返回【交接】，零模型请求。`context_new_window` 工具（无参数，随时可调；本窗口没写笔记时拒绝一次）。常驻说明只讲规则，第一个窗口注入一次精简【交接】 |
| 团队笔记 | `notes`（默认开） | `team_notes` 工具：读（可给 `start_line` / `stop_line`，大文件不给范围时返回末尾 + 总行数）、写、追加、搜索、`resolve`（队长删待合并清单条目）。成员写自己的笔记，只有队长能写 `workspace.md`；队友笔记与 `records/…` 只读。【交接】里的笔记指针与元数据 |
| 记录 | 随 `notes` | 终态任务全文（分卷 1 MB、单条 32 KB）、成员笔记快照（换窗与终态时拍，坐标 `<会话>/w<n>/e<seq>`）、`workspace.md` 修改前快照（`records/workspace-snapshots/`，编号越小越旧）。团队代结束时归档在用笔记，可选按天清理 |
| 历史工具 | `history`（默认开） | `history_list_windows` / `history_list_items` / `history_read_item` / `history_search_contents`；窗口编号 `w1`、`w2`…，只读，不落盘 |
| 团队信件回看 | `teamHistory`（默认开） | `team_history` 工具：回看团队信件，含已读和已作废的信。队长看全队（包括成员之间的信），成员看发给自己和自己发出的信。只读，不落盘 |
| 剩余上下文 | `contextTool`（默认开） | `context_remaining` 工具：返回已用比例与距离主动压缩的余量 |
| 笔记合并 | `notesMerge`（默认关） | 待合并清单非空时，用所选模型把清单条目指向的成员笔记快照合并进 `workspace.md`，成功后删掉已合并的条目；可附带近期任务全文（材料 a）与历史快照（材料 b，实验性），超出模型上下文时自动裁剪。关闭时由队长读清单、整理后 `resolve` |

所有开关和数值在设置页保存后**即时生效**，无需重启 DSH；已打开的会话在下一次请求时就会增减对应工具。

## 安装

需要 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2` 或更新版本，并已安装 `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams`。

从源码安装（当前方式）：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Todo56565/make-the-plugin.git
cd make-the-plugin
pnpm install && pnpm build          # 生成 lib/（含浏览器端 lib/client.js）
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add file:$(pwd)
dsh --profile <profile>             # 或 dsh web --profile <profile>
```

发布到 npm 后可直接 `dsh plugin --profile <profile> add dsh-token-budget`。

安装后在 DSH 插件管理面板确认 `dsh-token-budget` 已启用。更新源码后重新 `pnpm build` 并重启 DSH 即可。

## 设置

入口：插件 → `dsh-token-budget` → 组件行的「配置」（行名旁的 `>`）。模型为下拉选择（提供方 → 模型 → 推理强度）。保存后写入 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`；与默认值相同的项不会写入。

也可以直接编辑 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`：

```yaml
- id: dsh-token-budget
  config:
    remindAtRatio: 0.37
    compactAtRatio: 0.45
```

| 配置项 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `stateDir` | `.agent-teams` | 须与 agent-teams 的 `stateDir` 一致。放在 `.agent-teams` 之外时，笔记可能被质量闸门计入交付审计（启动时会告警） |
| `notes` / `history` / `teamHistory` / `contextTool` | `true` | 四个能力开关 |
| `remindAtRatio` | `0.37` | 成员开始提醒的占用比例（最低 `0.01`，须小于 `compactAtRatio`） |
| `compactAtRatio` | `0.45` | 成员换窗的占用比例；队长在此处与再后一个步长各提醒一次（最低 `0.03`） |
| `bucketStep` | `0.03` | 提醒档位步长。成员档位 = `remindAt + k × step` 且小于 `compactAt`，不整除时去掉最后一档（只剩一档时保留）：默认 37% / 40% |
| `fallbackBufferTokens` | `16384` | 成员到换窗点后补记笔记的额外额度（token） |
| `notesMerge` | `false` | 由外接模型合并待合并清单 |
| `mergeProvider` / `mergeModel` / `mergeReasoningEffort` | 空 | 合并所用模型；`notesMerge` 开启且选了模型才会合并 |
| `mergeRecentTasks` | `false` | 材料 a：附上次成功合并以来的任务全文（至多 16,000 字节，超出保留最新） |
| `mergeSnapshots` | `off` | 材料 b（实验性）：`off` / `cosine`（在历史快照上余弦取样）/ `custom`（指定编号） |
| `mergeSnapshotCount` | `5` | `cosine` 取样份数 |
| `mergeSnapshotPicks` | 空 | `custom` 时的快照编号，如 `1,5,12`；这些编号精简时额外保留 |
| `workspaceSnapshotKeep` | `0` | `workspace.md` 快照保留份数：`0` 全部保留；否则累计到 100 份时按余弦精简到该份数（最少 2） |
| `recordsCleanupDays` | `0` | 已结束团队代超过 N 天后删除其快照、搬入的笔记与待合并清单；`0` 不清理。全文记录始终保留 |
| `maxFileBytes` | `10000` | 成员 / 队长单个笔记字节上限 |
| `workspaceMaxBytes` | `20000` | `workspace.md` 字节上限 |
| `readMaxBytes` | `24000` | 读笔记 / 记录单次返回字节上限 |
| `hintMaxBytes` / `hintRecentNotes` | `4000` / `5` | 【交接】的字节上限（最低 4000）与列出的最近改动笔记数。超限先少列最近笔记，再截断过长的团队名 / 任务标题；身份、任务、自己的笔记、上一窗口永远保留 |
| `historyMaxResults` / `historyMaxReadChars` / `historyMaxListItems` | `200` / `20000` / `2000` | 历史工具单次返回上限 |

## 使用

不需要额外操作。建团队、派任务即可：

- 成员会在上下文里看到以【上下文预算】开头的提示，按提示写笔记，可以调用 `context_new_window` 自己换窗；到 45% 会看到【上下文已用尽】提示，补记笔记后调用 `context_new_window`。
- 换窗后，新窗口开头是【交接】（在摘要位置），列出身份、任务（含 `attempt_id`）、笔记和回看工具；成员用 `team_notes` 读回笔记，缺的用 `history_*` / `team_history` 查原文。
- 成员完成或失败的任务（带成员笔记快照）会进入待合并清单（虚拟文件 `workspace.pending.md`，读 `workspace.md` 时附带）。保持 `notesMerge` 关闭时，队长读清单指向的快照、整理进 `workspace.md` 后用 `resolve` 删除条目；打开 `notesMerge` 并选模型后由插件自动合并，队长只需处理剩下的条目。
- 成员笔记里「仍在处理的请求」记为 `w<n>/e<seq>`，换窗后可用 `history_*` 按坐标查原文。

成员工具策略：agent-teams 允许部署方在它的配置里声明 `toolPolicies`，再给成员挑一个策略。策略若写了 `allow`，成员就**只看得到列出的工具**（agent-teams 会自动补上它自己的 4 个协调工具，但不会补本插件的）。这时要把本插件的工具名一起列进去，否则成员看不到它们：

```yaml
toolPolicies:
  researcher:
    allow: [read, glob, grep, team_notes, team_history, context_new_window, context_remaining, history_list_windows, history_list_items, history_read_item, history_search_contents]
```

只用 `deny`、或成员没选策略时，不需要处理。成员看不到 `team_notes` 时，到换窗点不兜底，直接换窗。

运行时文件都在工作区 `.agent-teams/.context/` 下（agent-teams 默认把 `.agent-teams` 排除在交付审计之外）：`notes/`（在用笔记）、`shared/`（`workspace.md`、待合并清单、锁）、`records/`（全文、快照、已结束团队代）、`state/`（游标与序号）。物理路径按团队代分目录，模型看到的虚拟路径不变。历史工具只读会话文件，不另存数据。

## 可选：关闭会话文件压缩（实验）

DSH 会话文件默认是 zstd 压缩（不是加密）。若想降低 history 工具的解码成本，可在 profile 中把 `session-persistence-jsonl` 的 `compression` 设为 `'none'`。这是全局存储配置，本插件不会自动修改；详见设计文档 §4.4。

## 兼容性

| 组件 | 版本 |
|---|---|
| DSH | `0.2.0-rc.2` 实测；源码基线 `d7432673`（`0.2.1-alpha.2`） |
| `@nanmicoder/dsh-agent-teams` | `0.1.23` |

## 开发

```bash
pnpm test        # node --test
pnpm typecheck
pnpm build
```

## 目录规划

```
make-the-plugin/
├── README.md                    本文件：项目总览与目录规划
├── package.json                 npm 包 dsh-token-budget（files 白名单只发布 lib/、cordis.patch.yml、README）
├── cordis.patch.yml             DSH 装载补丁：把插件行挂到宿主层
├── tsconfig.json
├── src/                         插件源码（TypeScript）
│   ├── index.ts                   入口：name / inject / Config / apply()
│   ├── config.ts                  配置 schema（Schemastery）与默认值
│   ├── team/                      团队身份解析、team.json 缓存读取
│   ├── client/                    浏览器端设置页（DSH 插件管理面板 → 配置）：表单状态、模型目录下拉、中英文文案
│   ├── context/                   `.context` 目录布局（各区路径、团队代）、跨插件文件锁、原子写
│   ├── records/                   全文记录（终态任务追加到 records/full 分卷，游标缓存与重建、首次运行基线）；已结束团队代的发现、归档与按天清理
│   ├── window/                    窗口投影（history 口径）、换窗状态与决策、context_new_window 工具
│   ├── budget/                    占用计算、提醒与兜底文本、换窗压缩与 summarize() 接管
│   ├── prompt/                    常驻规则 section、【交接】模板（完整版 / w1 精简版）
│   ├── notes/                     笔记存储与虚拟路径、team_notes 工具（含行范围读）、成员笔记快照、workspace.md 修改前快照与余弦取样、待合并清单（shared/pending/nanmi/<团队>@<代>.jsonl → 虚拟 workspace.pending.md）、自动合并与合并材料裁剪
│   ├── history/                   persistence 只读读取、窗口索引、history 工具
│   └── team-history/              团队信箱只读视图与 team_history 工具
├── test/                        单元测试（node --test），目录结构与 src/ 对应
├── docs/
│   ├── design/                    设计文档
│   │   ├── plugin-design.md         权威设计规格（实现以此为准）
│   │   ├── 0.3.0-handoff.md         0.3.0 换窗交接设计（已发布）
│   │   ├── 0.4.0-workspace-notes.md 0.4.0 workspace 双层记录设计与实现拆分
│   │   ├── future-ideas.md          远期想法（共议会、客户端数据通道、快照看板等）
│   │   └── 临时记录.md              设计讨论记录（只保留当前结论）
│   ├── research/
│   │   ├── 0.3.0-poc-results.md     0.3.0 设计 PoC 实测
│   │   └── context-compare/         Codex 与 DSH 上下文机制取证、社区插件调研、探针脚本
│   └── reference/                 外部参考资料（Codex 上下文压缩文章）
├── .agent-teams/                DSH 团队运行留下的归档（由 dsh-agent-teams 写入，勿手改）
└── _src-compare/                对照源码的 gitlink（codex、dsh-agent-teams），不随仓库检出
```

放置规则：

- **插件代码**只放 `src/`，一个能力一个子目录；跨能力共用的放 `team/`、`window/`。
- **设计变更**先改 `docs/design/plugin-design.md`，再改代码；讨论过程写进 `临时记录.md`。
- **调研与取证**（报告、探针脚本、运行输出）放 `docs/research/`，按课题建子目录。
- **构建产物** `lib/` 与 `node_modules/` 不入库（见 `.gitignore`）。
- **运行时数据不入库**：插件运行时数据写在用户工作区的 `.agent-teams/.context/`，history 不落盘。

## 许可

待定。

# dsh-office-suite-for-grid（套件本体）

DSH 办公·电网绘图套件的插件本体（v0.1）：

- 工具：`suite_env`（环境探测）、`office_read`（Word/Excel 读取，COM 引擎）、`visio_draw`（Visio 流程图，COM 引擎）；
- 命令：`office-env`；
- 引擎脚本位于 `engines\`（PowerShell），随包分发、就地执行；
- P1 起加入 Client 面板、其余图类型、CAD 转 PDF 与排版功能。

安装：经插件管理选择本目录（链接安装，代码留在本地）或从市场/Release/npm 安装打包版本。

# dsh-office-suite-for-grid

DSH 办公·电网绘图套件 —— 面向电网行业的 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）插件：在 DSH Web / Desktop 中一站式完成 Office 文档与表格的阅读、编辑、排版，驱动 Visio 绘制电网专业图表，并将 CAD 图纸智能转换为 PDF（自动分割 / 合并，适配 A4 打印）。

## 功能一览

| 模块 | 能力 |
|---|---|
| Office 文档/表格 | docx/xlsx 阅读（大纲、分页、表格与公式）、结构化编辑、通用排版、公文/红头模板、批量排版、导出 PDF 与渲染预览 |
| Visio 电网绘图 | 电气主接线图、配电系统图、通信网络拓扑、二次/继保图、变电站布置、地理接线图、时间线、流程图、组织结构图、思维导图、泳道图；内置 GB/T 4728-2022 标准符号库，支持挂接单位自备模具库 |
| CAD 转 PDF | 文件夹多张 DWG 自动合并为一个 PDF；单文件合并多图框图纸自动分割为每图一页（默认横向 A4）；图号优先排序；无 CAD 机器经 PDF 级引擎兜底处理 |

## 特性

- **符合 DSH 插件标准**：标准 bundle 清单（`dsh.bundle.patch`、`engines.dsh`、locale、图标、meta），Web 与 Desktop 共用同一套 Client 插件，只使用公开扩展点，多版本自动降级。
- **本地软件版本适配**：自动探测 Word/Excel/Visio、AutoCAD/中望/浩辰、LibreOffice、Python 等软件的安装与版本，按版本选择调用路径，能力分级、优雅降级，诊断页一目了然。
- **独立部署**：全部源码与运行时（venv、日志、备份、缓存、输出）位于项目文件夹内，官方 DSH 程序目录零写入；卸载即删除目录。
- **速度优先**：COM 会话复用、Python 常驻 worker、批量并行（可配置）、探测结果缓存、面板推送不轮询。
- **开源**：MIT 协议；第三方依赖许可证清册见 `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`。

## 安装（多种方式，Web / Desktop 通用）

1. **市场索引（推荐）**：在 DSH「插件 → 市场」添加本仓库 Pages 索引地址 `https://underfacet.github.io/dsh-office-suite-for-grid/index.json`，随后在发现页一键安装与升级。
2. **GitHub Releases**：下载 `dsh-office-suite-for-grid-x.y.z.tgz`，在插件管理中选择该文件安装。
3. **npm**：`npm install` 后经插件管理按包名安装（`dsh-office-suite-for-grid`）。
4. **源码/本地目录**：克隆本仓库后运行 `tools\install.ps1`（链接安装，代码留在本目录）。

## 目录结构

```
suite\        插件本体（安装对象）
runtime\      用户机运行时（venv、日志、备份、缓存）——自动生成，不入库
output\       产物：diagrams\（.vsdx）、pdf\（合并/分割 PDF）
docs\         设计文档、用户手册、兼容矩阵、符号对照表
tests\        脱敏公开样例与冒烟脚本
tests-local\  真实样例图纸（本地保密，不入库）
tools\        环境探测、安装/升级、发布脚本
```

## 协议与维护

- 协议：MIT（见 LICENSE）
- 分支：`main`（稳定）/ `dev`（开发）/ `feature\*`；发版打 `release-x.y.z` 标签，变更记录见 CHANGELOG.md

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-notify-say

给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) Desktop 用的通知插件：**任务跑完会说话**。

> 别的通知插件"叮"一声；这个会喊你"任务完成了"。
> 而且**子代理还在跑的时候，它不会骗你说完成了**。

只支持 **Windows**。

![设置页](docs/screenshots/settings-tts.png)

> 设置页实拍（声音来源 = 系统语音合成）。语音包、提醒规则、高级区见下文。

---

## 目录

- [它解决什么问题](#它解决什么问题)
- [特性](#特性)
- [安装](#安装)
- [快速开始](#快速开始)
- [配置](#配置)
- [语音包](#语音包)
- [关于"跳回会话"](#关于跳回会话)
- [兼容性与降级](#兼容性与降级)
- [已知限制](#已知限制)
- [常见问题](#常见问题)
- [开发](#开发)
- [许可](#许可)

---

## 它解决什么问题

你让 AI 跑一个较长任务，然后切去干别的。常见两种通知插件的毛病：

1. **该响的时候不响** —— 主会话一轮结束就报"完成"，但其实它派出的子代理还在跑，你回来发现没干完。
2. **不该响的时候一直响** —— 每个子代理结束都弹一次，连环轰炸。

本插件的做法：

- **空闲门（idle gate）**：主会话这轮结束、但仍有子代理或后台任务在跑时，**先不播**；等全部结束再播**一次**。超时兜底（默认 10 分钟），防子任务卡死导致永不播报。
- **按会话去抖**：同一会话默认 60 秒内只响一次。
- **失败单独提醒**：回合出错时播**日语道歉语音**（可选）—— 比"任务完成"更该让你立刻知道。

---

## 特性

| 特性 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| **语音播报** | 播放本地 wav，**不调用云端 TTS**。发布版自带 1 个音色，另 13 个可在设置页按需下载 |
| **空闲门** | 有在飞工作时不误报"完成"，全部结束才播一次 |
| **五类事件** | 完成 / 出错 / 被拦截 / 待批准 / 要提问，各自独立开关 |
| **设置页 GUI** | 走官方 `Config` schema，在 DSH 设置页里直接改，**改完立即生效** |
| **命令行** | `tools/notify-config.ps1`，适合脚本化与排查 |
| **切回窗口时跳会话** | 通知时你不在前台 → 你切回来时自动跳到那个会话（见[下文](#关于跳回会话)） |
| **不装语音也能用** | 没有语音包 = Toast + 系统提示音，这是正常配置 |
| **许可先告知** | 下载音色前弹出条款确认，写明署名要求与官方条款链接 |
| **诊断导出** | 一键导出脱敏日志（用户名/路径已替换），方便提 Issue |
| **日志隐私分级** | 默认只记元数据，**不记台词正文**；要详细日志需手动开 debug |
| **检查更新** | 显示当前/最新版本，有新版时给出升级命令（**不自动更新**，见[下文](#有新版本了怎么办)） |

> **联网说明**：通知、播放、TTS **完全离线**。
> 会联网的只有两件事：
> 　① **下载语音包**（访问 GitHub，只有你点「下载」时才发生）
> 　② **检查更新**（访问 npm registry 与 GitHub，**每 24 小时最多一次**）
>
> 不想让它检查更新？不点「检查更新」就不会主动查；已缓存的 24 小时内也不会再查。
> 网络不可用时这两件事都会失败，但**不影响通知和语音**。

---

## 安装

### 前置

- DSH Desktop **0.1.7-rc.2 或更高**
- Windows（Toast 用 WinRT，播放用 MCI，调用 Windows PowerShell 5.1）

### 方式一：插件页（推荐，不用命令行）

1. 打开 DSH 的 **设置 → 插件**
2. 找到「**包名或地址**」输入框（不是上面那个搜索框 —— 那个只过滤已安装列表）
3. 填进去：

   ```
   dsh-notify-say
   ```

4. 点「**安装**」，装完重启 DSH

> 装的时候卡住或报网络错误？在同一个面板里把「**安装源**」切到
> 「**中国大陆镜像源**」再试 —— 官方源在国内经常拉不动。

> 填 `dsh-notify-say` 是**包名**（不是搜索词）。它也能接受 GitHub 仓库地址
> 或本机目录路径，但包名最简单。

### 方式二：npm

```
npm install dsh-notify-say
```

### 方式三：手工 link（本地开发）

把本仓库目录链接进 profile：

```
D:\Program Files (x86)\DSH\profiles\desktop\package.json
  dependencies 里加:  "dsh-notify-say": "link:<本仓库路径>"
  dsh.profile.bundles 里加:  "dsh-notify-say"
```

然后在该 profile 目录执行 `pnpm install`，重启 DSH。

---

## 快速开始

装好之后**什么都不用配就能用**：任务完成时会弹 Toast + 播自带音色。

想做更多，进 **DSH 设置 → 通知**：

| 想做的事 | 去哪 |
|---|---|
| 换音色 / 调音量 | 设置页「音色」「音量」 |
| 下载更多音色（13 个可选） | 设置页「语音包」→ 点「加载列表」→ 选一个点「下载」 |
| 只保留提示音、不要语音 | 音源改成「系统提示音」 |
| 出错时也要语音提醒 | 「出错」开关（默认已开） |
| 让子代理结束也提醒 | 「子代理」开关（默认关） |
| 少响一点 | 「同会话去抖」调大 |
| 看看有没有新版 | 高级区「版本与更新」→ 检查更新 |

---

## 配置

四种来源，**优先级由低到高**（后者覆盖前者）：

```
1. schema 默认值
2. cordis.patch.yml 的 config
3. DSH 设置页里改的值
4. tools/notify-config.ps1 写的 storages/config.json
```

> ⚠️ **注意语义**：一旦你在设置页改过某项，再改 `cordis.patch.yml` 里同一项**不再生效**。
> 这是 DSH 官方设计（用户层优先级更高），不是本插件的 bug。

### 设置页

**DSH 设置 → 通知**。包含音源选择、音色、音量、增益、TTS 参数、五个事件开关、
去抖与冷却、音源按事件覆盖、自定义音频、语音包管理、日志级别、诊断导出等。

分常规区与「高级」折叠区：日常只用常规区，排查时才展开高级区。

### 命令行

```powershell
cd <插件目录>\tools

.\notify-config.ps1 -Show              # 看当前生效值
.\notify-config.ps1 -Voice off         # 静音（Toast 仍弹）
.\notify-config.ps1 -Volume 40
.\notify-config.ps1 -VoiceMode random
.\notify-config.ps1 -VoiceName ankomon
.\notify-config.ps1 -Disable aborted -Enable subagents
.\notify-config.ps1 -Clear             # 交还控制权给设置页
```

改完**立即生效**，不需要重启 DSH。

---

## 语音包

核心包只带**一个日语音色**（ずんだもん），安装包约 3.2 MB。

另有 **13 个音色**可单独下载（每个约 1.7–3.0 MB，合计约 27 MB），
**在设置页里点几下就能装**，不需要命令行。

### 怎么装

1. **DSH 设置 → 通知 → 语音包** → 点「加载列表」
2. 列表里会显示每个音色的名称、体积、署名要求
3. 点「下载」→ **先弹出条款确认弹窗**（见下）→ 确认后开始下载
4. 装好后在「音色」下拉里就能选到

### 下载前会告知什么

点下载会弹一个居中弹窗，写明：

- **署名要求**（例如 `VOICEVOX:ずんだもん`）—— 你用这些语音做的内容需要保留这个署名
- **官方条款链接**（可点开原文）
- 提示"下载后 zip 内也带 TERMS.md；你用它做的内容（视频、直播等）仍需守上述条款"

这不是走形式：13 个音色里有 2 个因为条款**禁止再分发**被我们排除在外，
1 个因为身份存疑（同名角色有多个）暂不收录。审核依据是官方条款原文，
留档在 [`docs/audio-audit/`](docs/audio-audit/)。

> 需要说清楚：我们的审核结论是**依据官方通用条款**得出的，
> 不等于各权利人针对"独立 WAV 素材 ZIP 再分发"出具过专项授权。

### 卸载

设置页里点「卸载」即可，会删掉该音色整个目录。
**卸载不依赖网络** —— 离线时也能卸。

### 已装的音色放哪

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-notify-say\voice-lines\<音色key>\
```

每个音色一个目录，卸载 = 删这一个目录。

### 不装语音包也完全可用

通知会退回 Windows Toast + 系统提示音。

### 想自己做音色

装 [VOICEVOX](https://voicevox.hiroshiba.jp/)（本地免费 TTS），启动引擎（默认 `http://127.0.0.1:50021`），
然后按命名规则把合成好的 wav 放进对应目录：

```
sounds/voice-lines/<key>~1.wav            完成
sounds/voice-lines/question/<key>~1.wav   提问
sounds/voice-lines/approval/<key>~1.wav   审批
sounds/voice-lines/fail/<key>~1.wav       出错
```

（合成脚本不随本包发布 —— 它依赖本地 VOICEVOX 引擎与特定音色表，放进发布包只会误导。）

---

## 关于"跳回会话"：能做到什么，做不到什么

这一节把边界写清楚 —— 有些事是**宿主没给接口**，不是本插件偷懒。
结论先给：**能在你切回来时跳到「你离开期间最早完成」的那个会话；
不能做到「点哪条通知就跳哪条」。**

### ✅ 能做到：切回窗口时跳到那个会话

```
通知发出时你不在前台  →  插件记下那个会话
你切回 DSH 窗口       →  插件自动跳到它
```

所以体验是：你在别处干活 → 听到"任务完成了" → 切回 DSH → **它已经帮你跳过去了**。

相关开关（默认值偏保守）：

| 开关 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| 后台完成时跳转 | 开 | 通知时你不在前台 → 切回来时跳 |
| 前台完成时也跳 | 关 | 你正看着屏幕时也带你过去（v0.4.63 起真正生效，见下） |
| 多个会话完成时 | 跳到最早错过的 | 见下节 |

配置读不到时**两个开关都当作关**（宁可少跳一次，也不擅自动你的界面）。

### 前台完成怎么做到「立刻跳」

打开「前台完成时也跳」后，插件用**长轮询**盯着新信号：

```
窗口可见 → 客户端挂一个 GET /wait?after=<已知最新>
         → 服务端没新信号就**挂着不返回**（不占 CPU、不发新请求）
         → 一旦有完成信号，立刻返回 → 客户端立刻跳
```

所以是**信号一到就跳**，不存在「声音响了一会儿才跳过去」的延迟。
窗口一隐藏，长轮询立刻停止，改由下面的「切回来时跳」接手 —— 两者不会重复跳。

> 实现细节：为什么不用定时轮询 —— 定时轮询要么延迟明显（体验割裂），
> 要么空转（每秒几次请求）。长轮询两头都不占。

### 多个会话都完成时跳哪个

这是个真问题：你离开期间 A、B 先后完成，回来只跳一个，另一个就只能靠侧栏绿点。

默认规则是**跳到最早错过的那个**。理由是：你回来时界面通常仍停在它上面，
对它 `openSession` 等于无操作 —— 于是你正在看的会话**不被打断**，
而你最先错过的那个正好被带过去。其余的留着绿点，你一个个看。

| 选项 | 行为 |
|---|---|
| **跳到最早错过的**（默认） | 见上。多为你仍停在它上面，等于不打断 |
| 跳到最后一个 | 只在最后完成的那条落脚 |
| 都不跳 | 多个完成时不跳，侧栏绿点一个个自己点（单会话时照常跳） |

### ❌ 做不到：点哪条 Toast 就跳哪条

Windows Toast 的协议激活串是**固定值**，DSH 桌面壳层对它做精确匹配：

```js
app.on("open-url", (event, url) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  if (url === "dsh://open" || url === "dsh://open/") focusPrimaryWindow();
});
```

**只有这两个精确字符串会唤窗**，带任何参数（`dsh://open?session=xxx`）连窗口都唤不起来。
**所以点击 Toast 只能把窗口唤到前面，带不了会话 id** ——
插件**无法知道你点的是哪一条通知**。

这不是本插件能绕过的：要解决必须由 DSH 支持带参数的深链接。
已在上游反馈：[deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness#9233](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/9233)。

### ❌ 做不到：知道「你现在正看着哪个会话」

插件拿不到这个信息，四条路都堵着：

| 想用的手段 | 实际情况 |
|---|---|
| `uiWorkspace` 服务 | 只提供 `openSession` / `startSession` / `openWorkspace` —— **只写不读** |
| 会话切换事件 | 插件能订阅的是 `session/event` / `agent/status` / `approval/request`，**没有「切换/激活」** |
| URL 路由 | DSH 不用 URL 承载会话 id |
| 宿主内部状态 | 宿主**确实知道**（`SessionUpdateRouter.activeSessions` 记录着哪些会话正被订阅），但那是 client 传输层内部结构，**没有对插件开放** |

所以插件无法判断"要跳的就是你正看着的那个"。
上面那条「跳到最早错过的」规则，正是因为缺这个信息才采用的**间接办法** ——
它靠"跳到同一个会话等于没跳"来达到相近效果。

如果将来 DSH 开放"当前会话"读取，这里可以换成精确判断。

### ❌ 做不到：把绿点加回去

宿主没有"标记未读"的接口（整个 `app.asar` 里搜 `unread` 只命中一个 SVG 图标文件名）。
插件只能**观察**会话状态，不能写回。
所以"跳走之后把原来那条重新标成未读"做不到 —— 这也是默认规则选
「跳到最早错过的」的原因：从源头上避免把你从该看的会话上带走。

### ✅ 能做到：Toast 告诉你是哪个会话

既然跳不过去，至少让标题说清是谁。Toast 标题用**会话标题**（DSH 侧栏显示的那个，
通常是你第一句话的摘要），例如：

```
┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 优化 Deepseek Harness 配置与插件      │
│ ✅ 任务完成 · 回来看结果吧            │
│ 0Deepseek                          │
└────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- 标题来源三级：`sessionTitle` 服务 → `sessionProjections` 的 `title` 投影 → 会话 id 前 12 位。
  前两级都拿不到时**退回通用文案**（不会把会话 id 当标题显示）。
- 第三行是**项目名**（工作目录最后一段），只在**标题里没包含它**时才显示，
  避免单项目用户看到重复信息。

> 为什么拿不到"会话内容摘要"：插件订阅的 `turn/end` 事件只带 `{ turn, reason }`，
> 没有消息正文；投影缓存里也只有标题、没有正文预览。标题本身已是首句摘要，
> 已经是现有接口下最有信息量的选择。

## 兼容性与降级

本插件的首要目标是**稳定**，所以每个依赖外部能力的地方都有降级路径：

| 能力 | 拿不到时怎么办 |
|---|---|
| `@deepseek-ai/schemastery`（生成设置页） | 不导出 `Config` → **设置页不出现，插件照常工作** |
| `uiWorkspace.openSession`（跳会话） | 不跳转，Toast 仍能唤出窗口（**退回旧行为**） |
| 语音包目录 | 回退系统提示音 |
| 网络（下载语音包时） | 显示失败原因并可重试；**已装音色不受影响** |
| `$DSH_HOME` 未设置 | 配置走 patch 默认值；不写任何状态文件 |

**不会出现"静默失效"**：每个降级都有明确行为，并有测试锁定。

---

## 已知限制

- **仅 Windows**（Toast = WinRT，播放 = MCI，调用 Windows PowerShell 5.1）
- **跳会话依赖未文档化 API**（`uiWorkspace`），官方随时可能改；坏了会自动降级为"只唤起窗口"
- `blocked`（回合被拦截）只用系统蜂鸣，不播失败语音 —— 语义是"被拦下"而非"失败"
- **失败语音只覆盖部分音色**：选到未覆盖的音色时，会在同池内换一个音色播，不会哑掉、也不会播错语义
- **自重载是实验性功能，而且只有"点一次"**：设置页「高级设置 → 开发者选项」里有个
  「重载现在生效」按钮，点一下尝试一次；**没有开关、不会自动监听文件**。
  
  为什么改成这样：2026-10-18 实测「监听文件自动重载」会把宿主拖崩 —— 一次改 UI 期间
  触发了 40 多次失败重载，每次销毁实例都会释放宿主仍在用的会话引用，最后渲染进程崩溃。
  危险的不是"重载失败"，是"**反复**重载"
- **自重载不能替代重启**：它只能重新导入「同一路径上的」代码。用 `dsh plugin update`
  升级后，新版本装在 `.pnpm/<name>@<ver>/` 另一个路径，自重载做不到 —— 必须重启 DSH
- **13 个音色的许可结论是条件性判断**（依据官方通用条款），不代表各权利人出具过专项授权

---

## 常见问题

**装了没声音？**
按顺序查：① 设置页「音源」是不是「不发声」；② 「语音」开关是否关着；
③ 「音量」是否拉到 0；④ 播放依赖 Windows PowerShell 5.1，被安全软件拦了会静音。
设置页「诊断」区可以**导出脱敏诊断文件**，里面能看出每次播报的决策路径。

**会不会打扰我？**
默认同会话 60 秒只响一次；「子代理」默认关（子代理结束不单独提醒）。
觉得吵可以把「同会话去抖」调大，或直接关掉某类事件。

**会上传我的会话内容吗？**
不会。通知文案是插件内置的固定句子（可自定义），播放也全在本地。
默认日志只记"播了什么、成功与否"，**不记台词正文**。
会联网的只有两处：下载语音包、以及每 24 小时最多一次的检查更新。二者失败都不影响通知与语音。

**提示"未能获取可下载列表"？**
那是 GitHub 访问不通。**已装的音色照常能用**，卸载也能用（卸载不依赖网络）。
网络恢复后点「重试」即可。

**为什么只有 13 个音色？**
VOICEVOX 有几十个角色，但每个的条款都要单独读原文核对。
我们只收录**条款明确允许本插件这样分发**的，宁可少也不冒险。
被排除的例子：有 2 个明确禁止再分发，1 个身份存疑。

**有新版本了怎么办？**

设置页 → 高级 → **版本与更新** → 点「检查更新」。有新版时那里会显示版本号、
`CHANGELOG.md` 链接，以及一条升级命令（可一键复制）。

**插件不会自己更新自己。** 原因很实在：

- 装上你的机器后，插件不知道自己是通过 npm、GitHub 还是 `link:` 装的
- 正在运行的程序替换自己的文件，失败后很难恢复
- DSH 官方 CLI 已经能升级插件（`dsh plugin --profile <名字> update dsh-notify-say`）—— 重复实现没意义

所以分工是：**插件负责告诉你有新版；你执行命令；DSH 完成升级。**
更新后需要重启对应的 DSH profile。

> 如果你是从源码 `link:` 安装的（开发模式），插件会认出来并**不给命令** ——
> 那种情况请直接更新源码目录，用插件命令会覆盖你的源码。

**能加我喜欢的音色吗？**
可以提 Issue。但要走审核流程（读官方条款原文、留档），不是加个下载链接的事。

---

## 开发

### 跑测试

```powershell
npm test              # 主套件（纯 Node，不需要 DSH 宿主）
npm run test:all      # 全部（含 route 注入的两组）
npm run test:route    # 需要 --import loader 的接线测试
npm run test:audio-wire
```

**457 条测试通过。** 绝大多数是纯逻辑测试，克隆仓库后 `npm test` 即可跑。

少数用例需要真实的 DSH 宿主（用于验证 Cordis 上下文行为）。
找不到宿主时它们会**自动 skip** —— 注意 skip 不等于通过。

```powershell
$env:DSH_CORDIS_ENTRY = "<DSH 安装目录>\.runtime\node_modules\@deepseek-ai\cordis\lib\index.js"
npm test
```

### 测试分层

| 层次 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 单元 | 音源选择、空闲门、配置校验、TTS 文案、http-guard 判定 |
| 集成 | 真实 HTTP 服务器 + 真实 handler，覆盖请求/响应全链路 |
| 行为 | 构造真实输入验证行为（如真实 ZIP 字节、真实目录） |
| 实机 | 真实 Cordis 上下文（需宿主，无则 skip） |
| 发布 | 构建发布包并断言被禁音色/第三方素材未进包 |

### 为什么有这么多"防复发"测试

这个项目踩过的坑多数是同一类：**代码看着对、测试也绿，但两者一起错**。所以后来改成：

- **构造真实输入**而不是检查源码里有没有某个字符串
  （典型：ZIP 解压防护查了不存在的字段 `entry.size`，测试也在断言同一个错字段 → 一起绿）
- **状态更新全量扫描**而不是逐个手查
  （典型：组件状态漏字段已发生 4 次，现在有 C43 静态扫描锁住）
- **变异验证**：故意改坏代码，确认测试真的会红

### CI

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 在每次 push / PR 时跑：

- 单元测试（Node 20 / 22 / 24）
- PowerShell 语法与 UTF-8 BOM 检查
- 关键文件齐全 + npm 打包内容检查（含"被禁音色不得进包"）
- 版本一致性

### 发版

```powershell
.\tools\release.ps1 -Bump patch -PublishNpm
```

流程：升版本 → 跑测试 → 重建发布包 → **在发布包里再跑一次测试**
（这一步是必要的：开发目录与发布包的文件集不同，只在开发目录跑会"本地绿、线上红"）
→ 提交推送 → 可选发 npm。

`CHANGELOG.md` 由 `release-build.ps1` **自动生成**（从开发提交提取标题，
过滤掉内部资料与 hash），随包发布。**请勿手工编辑**。

---

## 许可

代码以 MIT 发布。

**语音文件不适用 MIT**，由 VOICEVOX 生成，各音色有其自身使用条款，
详见 [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md)。
每个音色包内另有该音色的 `TERMS.md`。

The plugin uses PowerShell/TTS and downloads voice packs; no downloads or playback were invoked as plugin behavior. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
