***

## What is OpenViking

OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents — one filesystem for everything an agent knows: knowledge, memory, and skills.

Most agent memory is a black box: text goes in, embeddings come out, and nobody can see what was actually stored. OpenViking organizes context as a virtual filesystem under `viking://` instead. Agents navigate it like files — `ls`, `tree`, `read`, `write`, `grep` — and you can open any directory to inspect and edit what your agent knows. Every directory carries a generated summary, so agents can scan summaries first and decide what to read.

<a href="https://studio.openviking.ai" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">
  <picture>
    <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/images/studio-filesystem-dark.png">
    <img src="docs/images/studio-filesystem.png" alt="OpenViking Studio Filesystem: browse personal memories and resources">
  </picture>
</a>

[Try OpenViking Studio](https://studio.openviking.ai) in your browser, no installation required. [Self-host Web Studio](web-studio/README.md).

## Why OpenViking

- **One filesystem for knowledge, memory, and skills.** Resources hold documents and code; memories retain user preferences and experience; skills define how to perform tasks — not just extracted facts, but the full context, each with a `viking://` URI for browsing and retrieval. → [Viking URI](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/04-viking-uri) · [Context types](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/02-context-types)
- **Search a directory, not the whole index.** Scope semantic search to a project or memory subtree instead of scanning a flat vector pool. `find` runs a query directly; `search` plans retrieval from session context. → [Retrieval](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/07-retrieval)
- **Read the summary before the source.** Generated directory abstracts (L0) and overviews (L1) let agents judge relevance before opening full content (L2). → [Context layers](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/03-context-layers)
- **Sessions become files you can read.** Committing a session archives the conversation and extracts memories as Markdown you can inspect, edit, and merge. With VikingBot enabled, `ov compile` organizes source material into a wiki, knowledge graph, or report. → [Sessions](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/08-session) · [Context compilation](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/context-compilation/01-overview)

[Architecture](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/concepts/01-architecture) · [Design rationale](https://blog.openviking.ai/post/openviking-context-database/)

```
viking://
├── resources/              # Resources: project docs, repos, web pages, etc.
│   └── my_project/
│       ├── docs/
│       │   ├── api/
│       │   └── tutorials/
│       └── src/
└── user/
    └── {user_id}/
        ├── memories/
        │   └── preferences/
        │       ├── writing_style
        │       └── coding_habits
        ├── resources/
        │   └── private_project/
        ├── skills/
        │   ├── search_code
        │   └── analyze_data
        └── peers/
            └── web-visitor-alice/
```

The three loading tiers:

- **L0 (Abstract)**: a one-sentence summary for quick relevance checks.
- **L1 (Overview)**: core information and usage scenarios for planning.
- **L2 (Details)**: the full original data, read only when needed.

Semantically processed directories carry L0/L1 summaries, so agents can judge relevance before reading full files:

```
viking://resources/my_project/
├── .abstract.md           # L0: quick relevance check
├── .overview.md           # L1: structure and key points
└── docs/
    ├── .abstract.md
    ├── .overview.md
    └── api/
        ├── auth.md         # L2: full content, loaded on demand
        └── endpoints.md
```

## Proof it works

OpenViking 0.3.22 has been evaluated on long-conversation user memory (LoCoMo) and multi-turn agent tasks (tau2-bench). Full results and setup details, including knowledge-base QA, are in the [benchmark report](https://blog.openviking.ai/post/openviking-benchmark-results/); reproduction scripts live in [./benchmark](./benchmark).

The memory evaluation used [Doubao 2.0 Pro](https://console.volcengine.com/ark/region:cn-beijing/model/detail?Id=doubao-seed-2-0-pro) as the VLM and [Doubao-embedding-vision-251215](https://console.volcengine.com/ark/region:cn-beijing/model/detail?Id=doubao-embedding-vision) as the embedding model.

<picture>
  <source media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)" srcset="docs/images/benchmark-dark.svg">
  <img alt="Benchmark results. LoCoMo accuracy: OpenClaw 24.20% native vs 82.08% with OpenViking; Hermes 33.38% vs 82.86%; Claude Code 57.21% vs 80.32%. tau2-bench task success: Retail 70.94% vs 77.81%; Airline 54.38% vs 66.25%." src="docs/images/benchmark-light.svg">
</picture>

- **User memory (LoCoMo)**: with OpenViking, all three agent integrations land at 80–83% accuracy — up from 24–57% on their native memory — while input tokens drop by 34.3–91.0% and query latency by 58.45–66.10%.
- **Agent experience (tau2-bench)**: experience memory lifts task success by +6.87pp (retail) and +11.87pp (airline) over the same LLM without memory.

## Quick start

Set up an OpenViking server first; if you already have one, skip to [Use it with your agent](#use-it-with-your-agent). Deploying your own needs uv, Python 3.10+ and a model provider with an embedding model and a VLM.

<details open>
<summary><strong>Let your agent deploy it</strong></summary>

```text
Follow this guide to install and start an OpenViking Server for me:

https://docs.openviking.ai/en/getting-started/04-setup-for-agent

Ask me for the model provider, the models, the workspace directory and whether
other machines need to reach the server; don't guess. When you ask for the model
API key, tell me how to hand it over if I'd rather not paste it into this chat,
and never repeat it back.

When it's running, tell me the server's address and whether auth is turned on.
```

Your agent will first ask which model provider to use and for its API key.

</details>

<details>
<summary><strong>Deploy it yourself</strong></summary>

Install OpenViking and run the setup wizard, which configures the models:

```bash
uv tool install openviking --upgrade && openviking-server init
```

`init` writes `~/.openviking/ov.conf` and supports Volcengine, OpenAI, Codex OAuth, Kimi, GLM and local Ollama; see the [configuration guide](https://docs.openviking.ai/en/guides/01-configuration). The server runs in the foreground, so keep this terminal open.

</details>

# 会话回收站 · Session Recycle Bin

给 DSH 补上它本来没有的「删除会话」。删除 = 移入回收站，随时可恢复；只有「彻底删除」才真正销毁。 **子会话跟随主会话**：删一个会话会把它名下的子代理会话整棵树一起带走，回收站里是**一条条目**， 恢复、彻底删除都按整棵树处理；删除前和销毁前的确认框都会先说明「其中 N 个子会话会一并移入/销毁」。 侧栏有独立入口（**右键还能一键清空**），会话菜单里还有**红色删除项**与**工作区批量归档/删除**， 回收站页里每条会话带**复选框**，可以勾选后批量恢复或批量彻底删除。 ![会话菜单里的红色删除项](docs/assets/sidebar-delete-menu.jpg) > **维护者请看** [二次开发与维护](#二次开发与维护)：改哪里、怎么重载、哪些不变量不能破坏。 > 本仓库只包含插件本体（清单 / Host 半 / Client 半 / 图标 / 截图 / 文案），以本地目录方式安装，源码即运行代码。 ## 为什么需要它 DSH 内核**没有删除会话的接口**（这是设计选择，不是遗漏）： | 层 | 包 | 事实 | | --- | --- | --- | | 持久化 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-persistence-jsonl` | README：「不删除会话文件——日志在 `root` 下累积，直到外部移除；seam 无删除接口」 | | 工作区注册表 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace` | 只有 `archiveSession` / `unarchiveSession` / `pinSession` / `unpinSession` | | 会话控制器 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-api-session-controller` | 只有 create / resume / list / follow | | 投影缓存 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session-projection-cache` | 「无淘汰或保留接口」 | 所以任何删除插件都是**绕开内核直接动磁盘**。本插件把这件危险的事做成两步：先移进回收站，再（可选）彻底删除。 > 上表结论来自对 DSH 安装包内各包的 README、类型声明（`lib/types/**/*.d.ts`）与运行行为的逐条查证： > 持久化层与投影缓存明确没有删除 / 淘汰接口，工作区注册表只提供归档与置顶，会话控制器只提供 > create / resume / list / follow。插件机制（槽位注册、Client bundle 的 Module Loader、HTTP 信任栅栏） > 见各 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-*` 与 `@deepseek-ai/cordis` 包的 README。 ## 一次删除做了什么 Host 上按顺序完成，每步都可回退： 1. **解析整棵树**：按持久化 header 里的 `origin: 'subagent'` + `parentSession` 找到该会话的 全部子代理会话（任意深度；fork 虽然也带 `parentSession` 但没有这个 origin，不会被带走）。 树从 `sessionPersistence.list()` 读，不依赖侧栏，也不依赖子会话的 Agent 是否还活着。 2. **归档准入**：调 `workspaceRegistry.archiveSession(id)`。它先问一遍 `workspace/session-activity` 瀑布（回合 / 后台 job / 子代理 / 定时提醒）， 有工作就抛错 → 插件回 409 `session-open`。父会话的准入已经把**运行中的子代理**算进 `subagent` 家族；插件还会对树里每个成员再查一次 `agent.status` / inbox，挡住竞态。 这一步同时把侧栏行藏起来，并装上归档门禁（门禁沿血缘生效，子会话的步骤同样被挡）。 3. 把根会话的日志目录 `~/.dsh/sessions///` **移动**到 `~/.dsh/session-recycle-bin/<时间戳>-/session/`； 每个子会话移到同一 bin 条目的 `children//session/`。 4. 把每棵树的投影缓存 `~/.dsh/storages/session_projcache/sessions/.json` 移到 同一 bin 条目的 `projcache.json` / `children//projcache.json`。 5. 写一份 `entry.json`（schema 2），根会话字段照旧记 `sessionId` / `cwd` / 实际找到的 `projectDir` / `title` / `createdAt` / `deletedAt` / 原工作区 / 原归档与置顶状态 / `hadDirectory` / `hadProjectionRecord`，另加 `childCount` 与 `children[]` （每个子会话的 `sessionId` / `projectDir` / `title` / 原有状态与两个 `had*`）。 6. 清掉每个成员的登记：从各 Workspace 的 `sessionIds` 摘除、从归档与置顶集合移除， 再发 `api-session/removed` 让前端列表当场掉行（根会话与每个子会话各发一次）。 7. 如果任一成员的 Agent 仍在本进程存活，把 id 记入隐藏集合，并由 `installHiddenSessionFilter()` 包住 `sessionQuery.listSessions` 过滤掉它。 `listSessions` 会把 `ctx.sessions` 里的**活会话合并到持久记录之上**，否则下一次 列表刷新时被删会话会以侧栏合成分组「未分组」的形式重新冒出来（1.1.0 的回归，1.1.1 修）。 子会话本来就不渲染侧栏行，但保持同一规则可以避免它们从别的语料读路径漏回来。 任何一步失败都会把已经移动的东西**搬回原位**、把准入时藏起来/取消置顶的会话还原， 不会丢字节（见 `trash()` 的 try/catch、`rollback()` 与 `restoreAccounting()`）。 **恢复与彻底删除都是整条处理**：`restore` 先把树里每个目标路径检查一遍，任何一条冲突就整条拒绝 （不会出现「父会话回来了、子会话还在回收站」的半棵树）；`purge` 直接删掉条目目录，子会话自然一起销毁。 **打开过但没在跑的会话可以删**：DSH 只要打开过会话就会在 Host 里保留一个空闲 Agent （session controller 的 background activation，直到 Host 退出才释放）。这不是「工作」， 不能成为拒绝理由；它的日志写句柄跟随文件对象跨 rename 有效，所以移动目录不会破坏它， 恢复后仍可继续对话。删除后这个活 Session 对象还在内存里，所以必须靠上面的列表过滤器 把它从语料列表里遮住；插件重载后 `repopulateHidden()` 会按 bin 条目重建隐藏集合（含每个子会话）。 **永远不做的事**：不碰 `~/.dsh/attachments/v1/objects`（附件按内容寻址、跨会话共享）， 不删 `~/.dsh/sessions` 下的项目目录本身，不覆盖同 ID 的既有目录（恢复冲突直接报错）。 ### 子会话为什么跟随主会话 DSH 里的子代理会话（`subagent` / fork / Agent Team 成员）是一个**有主的子会话**，不是平级会话： - header 带 `origin: 'subagent'` 与 `parentSession`，`delegationDepth` 表示层级； - 从不进 Workspace 的 `sessionIds`（`session.create` / `fork` 才 `attachSession`）， 所以**没有侧栏行**，官方 browser 的 `sessionVisible()` 对 `origin === 'subagent'` 直接返回 false； - 只能在父会话的 `subagentCatalog` 浮层/血缘条里打开。 因此把它当独立会话删是错的：父会话一旦进回收站，子会话的 `parentSession` 就指向一个不存在 （或不可达）的 id，UI 没有入口再找到它，只能在磁盘上占空间。所以本插件把「一个会话」定义成 **一棵树**：`trash` 带整棵树，bin 条目代表整棵树。只有一种例外被保留——**孤儿子会话** （父会话已经不在持久化里，例如旧版本留下的残留）仍可用 `delete_session` 按 id 单独删， 方便清理；而父会话还在时直接删子会话会被拒绝（`session-child`，HTTP 409）， 因为「删父会话」才是正确动作。 ## 入口一览 共 11 项入口：会话菜单两行、浮层四个、侧栏面板一个、回收站页及其批量操作、设置页一个、模型工具一个。 | 入口 | 位置（代码） | 说明 `POST /dsh-session-recycle-bin/api`，工具走 `ctx.tools.register`。 ### 三个对话框里的子会话提示 子会话没有侧栏行，Client 无法从自己的 store 数出来，所以对话框在**打开时**向 Host 要一个 只读的 `preview`（`{ action: 'preview', sessionIds }` → `{ sessions, childCount, missing }`）： | 对话框 | 提示文案 | 数据来源 | | --- | --- | --- | | 单条「删除会话…」确认框 | 「其中 {count} 个子会话会一并移入回收站（子会话跟随主会话，恢复时也一起回来）。」 | 打开时 `preview` 该会话 | | 批量删除确认框 | 「其中 {count} 个子会话会一并移入回收站，恢复时也一起回来。」 | 打开时 `preview` 整个选中集合 | | 「彻底删除」销毁确认框 | 「其中 {count} 个子会话的日志会一并销毁。」 | 回收站条目自带 `childCount`；侧栏右键「清空」路径由 `list` 探测补齐 | `preview` 是建议性的：真正的树由 `trash()` 自己在动任何字节前重新解析。所以预览失败只会让 对话框少一句计数（删除照常），预览过期也只会把数字说错，不会移错东西。 ### 侧栏位置是怎么定下来的 侧栏骨架由官方 `ui-sidebar` 写死：品牌行 → 新会话 → **`sidebar.panellist`（全局面板图标）** → `sidebar.workspaces` → **`sidebar.footer.action`** + 设置。第三方能追加的只有加粗的两个 list 座位。 本插件选 `sidebar.panellist`，因为它的语义正是「打开一个主区面板」，与「插件」「定时」「市场」完全同构； `main` 的 key 必须与 `sidebar.panellist` 的 id 相同（`layout.selectPanel(id)` 会校验 `main` 已注册）。 ### 批量操作为什么在会话菜单里 工作区行自己的「…」菜单（重命名 / 删除工作区）是 `ui-workspace` 里 `ProjectRowItem` 的内联数组， **不是槽位**；要往里加第三项只能整体替换 `sidebar.workspaces`（`replaceRisk: shadows-shipped-ui`）， 等于把官方侧栏浏览器复制进插件、DSH 一升级就坏。所以批量入口放在**会话行菜单**（同一个可扩展座位）， 作用域由该会话所属工作区决定 —— 交互上就是「在某个工作区的会话上点批量，作用于这个工作区」。 ### hover 为什么用 `--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-hover`（1.3.0） 1.2.x 的菜单行 hover 用的是 `--dsw-alias-bg-layer-2`。那是**表面** token（浅色下等于 `neutral-bluish-00`，纯白），拿它当 hover 底色，在侧栏上就是一块白斑；而原生的 菜单行（`ui-primitives` 的 `._item:hover`）与侧栏自己的 `PanelRow:hover` 用的都是 `--dsw-alias-interactive-bg-hover`（浅色 `#2631480f`、深色 `#ffffff14`，一层很淡的灰蓝）。 1.3.0 把它抽成 `client.js` 里的 `HOVER_FILL` 常量，四处 hover（批量项、批量面板的行、 右键菜单项、对话框右上角 ×）全部改用它；`validate-bundle.mjs` 也加了一条不许再拿表面 token 当 hover 的断言。 ### 回收站页的排版为什么改成「行首勾选 + 行尾操作」（1.3.0） 用户要求：每条会话前面加复选框、恢复与彻底删除从下侧挪到右侧。实现上就是把条目从 「竖排卡片」改成**一行三段**：`Checkbox | 身份区(flex:1，标题/时间/ID/目录) | 操作区(flex:none)`。 操作区固定宽度，所以长列表里每一行的「恢复 / 彻底删除」都能对齐。勾选之后，列表上方的 **选择栏**（全选 / 已选计数 / 恢复 / 彻底删除）才是批量入口。 ### 销毁确认为什么是「对话框 + 整页 frozen」（1.3.1） 1.3.0 的确认是页面里的**内联确认条**，只有 `busy` 会禁用控件。问题：确认条开着时 `busy` 还是 `false`，所以下层的复选框照样能点 —— 用户可以在「要删除这 1 个吗？」还开着的时候， 又勾上第 2 个。这是**真 bug**，1.3.1 修。 现在： - 确认是**独立对话框**，注册在 `shell.overlay`（`bin-confirm`），由 store `binConfirmRequest` 驱动；对话框本体 **portal 到 `document.body`**（见下一节）。**四个销毁入口共用它**： 侧栏右键的「清空回收站」、页面标题栏的「清空回收站」、选择栏的「彻底删除」、单条的「彻底删除」； - 打开期间回收站页整体 `frozen`：所有行复选框、全选、刷新、恢复、两个批量按钮全部 `disabled`， 并且 `toggle()` / 全选 handler 内部也直接 return（不只是视觉变灰）； - 请求里**捕获计数与精确的 binId 列表**（`{ kind, count, binIds }`），所以对话框问的是 「刚才那一刻的选择」，不会在背后被改掉； - 三个 kind 各有自己的标题与正文（`bin.purgeOneTitle/Body` 等），正文永远写明条数/标题。 侧栏右键那条路径拿不到条数（那里什么都没加载），所以 `{ kind: 'all' }` 不带 count， 由对话框自己先 `list` 一次补上；条数为 0 时确认按钮 disabled。 ### 对话框为什么要 portal 到 `document.body`（1.3.2） 用户报告：从「设置 → 会话回收站」点彻底删除，**确认框被设置面板盖住**。 根因是**层叠上下文**，不是 `zIndex` 写小了： ``` body └─ .AppFrame_frame position: relative └─ .AppFrame_overlayLayer position: absolute; z-index: 20 ← 层叠上下文！ └─ <我们的 session-recycle-bin.overlay /> z-index 写多大都 ≤ 20 └─ .SettingsRoot_overlay position: fixed; z-index: 1000 ← 盖住上面全部 ``` `shell.overlay` 看起来是「全框浮层」，但宿主把它塞进一个 `z-index: 20` 的绝对定位容器里， 该容器建立了**独立的层叠上下文**——子元素再大的 `z-index` 也不会超过 20。而设置面板是 `position: fixed; z-index: 1000` 的 `body` 级浮层。所以在设置页里弹出的确认框必然在下层。 修法：用 React 的 **`createPortal` 把对话框挂到 `document.body`**，跳出那个层叠上下文。 宿主自己的 `Modal` / `Menu` / `Tooltip` 原语也是这么做的（`createPortal(..., document.body)`）， 所以这是与宿主同构的做法，而不是 hack： - `react-dom` 在 Module Loader 的**静态模块表**里（`react` / `react/jsx-runtime` / `react-dom` / `react-dom/client` / `cordis` / `zod` / `tanstack/react-virtual` / `dsh-client-store` / `ui-slots` / `ui-primitives` / `ui-dockkit`），所以 `require('react-dom')` 是合法解析，不需要声明白名单； - 主题 token 不受影响：`ui-theme` 把调色板声明在 `body` 上，而 portal 的目标正是 `body`； - 层序常量 `DIALOG_Z_BASE = 1200`（> 设置面板的 1000），`Dialog` 的 `layer` 在此基础上叠加， 所以「批量面板 40 → 删除确认 50」的相对顺序不变； - 右键菜单同样 portal（`DIALOG_Z_BASE - 10`），否则在设置页里右键侧栏图标也会被盖住； - `portalize()` 在 `document.body` 或 `createPortal` 不可用时**原地渲染**，所以测试宿主 / 极端环境不会白屏。 `validate-bundle.mjs` 的模块白名单同步放宽到那张静态表（原来只许 `react`）。 ### 「已彻底删除 undefined 个条目」——HTTP 通道漏了计数（1.3.1） 这是**两个传输层形状不一致**造成的： | 通道 | 返回 | 谁算的 count | | --- | --- | --- | | 工具 `delete_session` | `{ trashedCount, archivedCount, … }` | `execute()` 里自己拼 | | HTTP → `dispatch()` | `{ purged: [...] }` / `{ restored: [...] }` | **没人算** | Client 走 HTTP，读的是 `payload.purgedCount` → `undefined`。 修法：把计数做成 **`dispatch()` 的契约**，四个批量动作统一返回 `{ : [...], Count, failed, failedCount }`，`dispatch` 因此 `export` 出去， `test-bin.mjs` 直接对着它断言 `purgedCount === purged.length`。 工具那一侧保持不变（它本来就算对了），两条通道现在同形。 Host 侧为此新增两个批量动作 `restoreMany` / `purgeMany`：**逐项走单条 `restore()` / `purge()`**， 返回 `{ restored|purged, failed[] }` 的成败拆分。这样一条恢复冲突（目标目录已被同 ID 占用） 不会把同批其它条目卡在回收站里，也不会出现「整单失败但其实动了一半」。 ### 侧栏右键菜单为什么挂在 `document` 上（1.3.0） 侧栏那行按钮由官方 `ui-sidebar` 的 `PanelRow` 渲染，**不是槽位**；插件能画的只有 `sidebar.panellist` 里的那枚图标（宽 16/18px）。要让「整行右键」都能弹出菜单，只有两条路： 替换官方侧栏（`shadows-shipped-ui`，否决），或让图标给自己打一个 `data-session-recycle-bin-nav` 标记、再在 `document` 上监听 `contextmenu`： 命中「有该标记的按钮」才 `preventDefault()` 并弹菜单。监听器的生命周期由 `React.useEffect` 管（图标不在就不监听），不碰宿主 DOM。 菜单本身注册在 `shell.overlay` 而不是侧栏里：侧栏列 `overflow: hidden` 且带 transform， `position: fixed` 的弹层在里面会被裁掉。`shell.overlay` 是全框浮层、明确 click-through， 正是这类 popup 的座位。选「清空回收站…」后弹的是**确认对话框**（先 `list` 读条数写进正文， 条数为 0 时确认按钮禁用），确认后调 `purgeAll`，再通过 `binRevision` 让所有已挂载的 回收站页重读（侧栏页与设置页可能同时挂着两份 `BinPanel`）。 复选框放在批量面板自己的列表里，而不是侧栏行首：行首唯一的槽位 `sidebar.session.row.leading` 只有 16px，且**有状态点的行（运行中/待处理/新消息）、已归档行、空白行 根本不渲染该槽位**，无法承载完整选择。 ### 批量删除确认为什么是「对话框 + 封存」而不是内嵌确认条 1.2.1 起，点「删除」不再在面板底部挤一条确认条，而是**再叠一个独立对话框** （`Dialog layer: 50`，标题「确认移入回收站」）。同时，下层的批量面板进入 **sealed** 状态： - 遮罩层 `pointerEvents: none`（下层完全不接收点击，彻底避免"确认框开着还能勾选"）； - `aria-hidden` + 去掉自身的 `aria-modal`（读屏器只读最上层的确认框）； - Esc / 点背景的关闭路径停用，右上角 × 与 `busy` 同步禁用； - 所有复选框、全选、归档/删除按钮渲染为 disabled。 实现上 `Dialog` 增加了两个 prop：`layer`（层序）与 `sealed`（被封存），`BatchPanel` 在 `confirmingDelete` 为真时把面板传 `sealed: true` 并返回 `[panel, confirmDialog]` 两棵树。 注意 `run()` 的守卫只看 `busy` 而不是 `frozen`——否则确认框自己的「移入回收站」按钮会被 它自己触发的封存挡住（这个坑踩过，`test-client.mjs` 现在有交互测试覆盖）。 ## 验证状态（2026-10-19 / 1.4.0） > # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wework Electron Host plugin This host-side DeepSeek Harness plugin bridges the DSH process to the Electron main process through two inherited private pipes. It exposes a versioned, loopback-only HTTP carrier to the first-party Wework DSH application. This plugin belongs only to the bundled Core Runtime `0.2.0-rc.2`. The Workbench Runtime `0.1.0-rc.8` does not contain it and receives no Electron Host pipe. The new Electron architecture no longer supports `0.1.0-rc.7`. The plugin provides a typed `ctx.weworkDesktop` Host service for the current Cordis generation. It exposes narrow domain-grouped capabilities rather than Electron objects, file descriptors, or authentication tokens. Retained service references reject calls as soon as their generation is disposed. The Renderer cannot read the Host Cordis service directly. Browser code keeps using the same-origin HTTP route for these capabilities and a product plugin can wrap that route with a client adapter. Window, tray, and Wework built-in browser events from the Electron main process share the `desktop.events` capability. The Renderer keeps one non-blocking 500 ms poll for all subscribers, and the Host immediately returns the current event batch so the same-origin HTTP request channel is never held open. New desktop events must reuse this stream instead of adding feature-specific 100 ms or 250 ms HTTP polling. Browser plugins in one DSH page share an origin and JavaScript trust domain. Therefore the HTTP carrier prevents cross-origin browser access but does not claim isolation between plugins installed into the same DSH composition. Untrusted plugins must not be installed into the first-party desktop profile. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | # Wework DSH Executor Runtime This plugin is the unified execution plane for Wework DSH apps. Browser code only accesses versioned same-origin endpoints and never receives Electron IPC, executor stdio, or bearer credentials. The physical transport currently uses the migration-only Electron loopback relay. The logical client, structured errors, event sequencing, bounded ring buffer, and resume contract are stable so local sockets and the cloud runtime relay can replace it without changing product apps. ## Relationship to Agents This plugin exposes Executor capabilities and projects executions into DSH Sessions, but it does not register a second global `AgentFactory`. The DSH base bundle's `agent-loop` already owns the single factory slot; registering another factory would prevent the default workbench from starting. Executor is a separate process and one Wework process can address local and remote execution targets at the same time. Codex and Claude Code are runtimes launched by Executor, not code bundled into this plugin. A selected Wegent Agent (Team) is materialized into the existing Executor `executionRequest` when the task is created, and later turns retain that task binding without changing the legacy Executor wire protocol. The Backend's canonical task builder is the only component that materializes a Team configuration. Wework no longer maintains a second conversion path for Bots, models, Skills, or collaboration modes. For a local execution target, Wework calls `/runtime-work/materialize` for an Executor V2-compatible payload and then sends that payload directly to the local Executor; the Backend does not proxy local execution. For a remote target, the existing `/runtime-work/create` path uses the same builder before Backend dispatch. The local default-assistant path is unchanged when no Team is selected. Existing V1/V2 cloud task requests retain their original semantics. Only new clients that select a Team send the V3 intent field `wegentTeamId`, while the materialized Executor payload remains V2. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and # Focus Board A product-oriented example inspired by TODO explorers, issue trackers, and personal productivity plugins. After installation and a Core DSH restart: - Open **Focus Board** from the sidebar. - Add work items and mark them complete; state survives renderer restarts. - Open the workspace bottom panel to see the compact queue. - Type `/focus` in the Composer to insert a live Markdown summary. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. # Prompt Library A focused Composer extension inspired by snippet managers and AI prompt tools. After installation and a Core DSH restart: - Open **Prompt Library** from the Wework sidebar. - Type `/review`, `/plan`, or `/explain` in the Composer. - Type `@prompt` to insert a stable prompt-library reference. The slash command receives the public `invocation.composer` API and inserts its template into the active draft. No Wework-private module is imported. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## # Sidebar browser panel This minimal Core DSH plugin adds one left-navigation item. Selecting it opens or reuses a right workspace-sidebar tab and renders the configured website through the Wework built-in browser without changing the current workspace tab. Copy this directory when the requested plugin only needs to expose a website: 1. Rename the package, Cordis bundle id, sidebar-tab id, and navigation id. 2. Replace the label, description, icon, and URL. 3. Keep the tab and navigation ids stable so repeated clicks reuse the same right-side panel. 4. Add a nested Codex plugin only if the product also needs Codex Skills, MCP servers, agents, or other Codex resources. # Test Explorer A testing showcase inspired by VS Code Test Explorer, Eclipse TestNG, Pytest, and language-specific test adapters. Its right-sidebar tree discovers real test files, lets the user select targets, starts a bounded test process, and displays run state and output. Public contracts demonstrated: - `weworkPluginRuntime` - `ctx.wework.backend` - `ctx.wework.testing.providers` - `wework.workspace.sidebar.tab` Discovery is bounded and ignores generated dependency trees; runs are limited to selected tests with a 30-second process timeout. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. # Dev Environments A development-environment showcase inspired by Dev Containers, Remote Development, and Docker tooling. A compact workspace-toolbar status control opens a three-step global setup wizard. The backend detects real project and tool signals, recommends a container image, and creates `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` only after the user presses the wizard's explicit generation action. Public contracts demonstrated: - `weworkPluginRuntime` - `ctx.wework.backend` - `ctx.wework.environments.providers` - `wework.workspace.toolbar.action` - `wework.shell.overlay` The plugin verifies actual Node.js, Python, Git, and Docker executables and preserves an existing Dev Container configuration. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ##
