# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wework Core DSH terminal runtime This first-party Core DSH plugin owns Wework's local interactive PTY sessions. The packaged Wework frontend calls its same-origin HTTP/SSE API at `/wework/terminal/v1`. The executor remains responsible for task, Codex, local-device and cloud-device execution. It does not proxy desktop terminal input or output. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## deepseek-harness-market

English · 简体中文

A plugin market that lives inside DeepSeek Harness.

One entry at the bottom of the sidebar: browse and search the community catalog, install, update, enable / disable, uninstall — all without leaving the GUI.

Install · Gallery · Design doc · API contract · Releases

## Why it exists **One-line positioning: this is a DeepSeek Harness plugin market that works like a phone app store** — browse, inspect, install, update, enable/disable and uninstall, all inside the sidebar, using the same mental model you already have from installing apps on your phone. Everything below is that positioning made concrete: - **A big catalog that loads fast.** The community-curated [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json) catalog with 4400+ entries (updated daily); it reads **npm mirror first with the official URL as fallback**, and fetching, caching, retries and degradation all happen in the host process — the browser only talks to our own endpoints, so the list is always instant. - **Every update step is visible.** The left button is one merged state machine: “Check for updates → Update all (N) / Check again”; each row updates to x.y.z on its own; every result stays on its own row and a run ends with one **honest** summary (restart-pending counts as success, failure reasons are written verbatim on that row — no sugar-coating). - **The market updates itself — and no longer dies with a single route.** It checks for a new build once at startup; when one exists the button goes straight to “Update to x.y.z”. All four states are covered: Update the market → Updating… → Update succeeded → Check again; downloads pass three checks (path shape + `sha256` + artifact self-verification), and after installing it **never pretends it already took effect**. GitHub's transports fail independently (`api.github.com` rate-limits anonymously, `raw` comes and goes, jsDelivr's main host `ECONNRESET`s, public acceleration prefixes go down wholesale), so every request walks a per-service candidate list and **remembers the route that just worked**; a public prefix answering **200 with its own HTML error page** is caught on the spot rather than recorded as a working route. `DSHM_GITHUB_PROXY` supplies your own prefix, which is **put at the head of the list rather than replacing it** — replacing it would turn one mirror outage into a dead channel. Measured: before, `check()` cost 12.4 s and failed on every source; after, three consecutive runs all **succeeded** (5.8 s / 7.1 s / 8.4 s), and the worst case is no slower than before (the budget defaults to the per-call timeout, so that time is merely shared across routes). Written up in [API-CONTRACT §2.8.1](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/API-CONTRACT.md). - **Fresh installs go live without a restart.** The host deliberately does *not* hot-apply an update to a package it already has — `pluginManager.installBundle` returns `restart-required` *before* it ever calls `reload()` — so the market does that step itself: it mounts the freshly installed plugin into the running composition through its own `Include` subtree (a throwaway file under `/.dsh-market/`, wiped on every boot, because durable state stays with `dsh.profile.bundles`). The panel then says “no restart needed” and **no restart banner lights up**. Six honest limits, each one tested: plain-insert patches only (a `config:` block, an inline `config: {}`, or any key other than `id`/`name` voids it and you get the restart notice instead); **upgrades are never hot-mounted** (replacing a live package leaves Node's ESM cache serving the old module — the mount would be theatre); a hard timeout (10 s) so a plugin waiting on a service that never arrives cannot wedge the request; a failed mount rolls back — the half-mounted subtree is disposed and the input file removed; an unmount that cannot confirm teardown reports `false` rather than claiming success. Written up in [API-CONTRACT §2.4.1](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/API-CONTRACT.md); ported (in shape, not code) from the official [dsh-market](https://github.com/dsh-market/dsh-market) `src/hot.ts`. - **“Restart required” is told the truth about.** When a change only takes effect after a host restart, the panel says so instead of quietly turning green — and it **survives a page refresh**, because the ledger lives in the host process (`/status.pendingRestart`), not in page memory. On CLI/`dsh web` installs it also offers a one-click **“Restart DSH”** (a detached waiter that relaunches only after the old process is really dead, and the page only reloads after observing the host die once). **Whether one-click restart is available is decided per deployment rather than refused or allowed outright**: under systemd the default `KillMode=control-group` takes the restart helper down with the unit (the service is killed and does not come back), in the desktop app the replacement is refused by the shell's single-instance lock (the shell's IPC whitelist also has no “restart yourself” message, exiting is treated as a fatal failure, and that failure dialog contains a *disable all third-party plugins* button — three independently sufficient reasons, written up in [API-CONTRACT §2.6](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/API-CONTRACT.md) and [ROADMAP item 6](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/ROADMAP.md)), and an attached `--inspect` session would be cut off. Each gets its **own next step** (`systemctl restart` / close the window and reopen / detach the debugger) — collapsing them into one sentence sends the user to try something that cannot work. Detecting systemd takes **two signals**: `INVOCATION_ID` is inherited, so that alone would also disable the button for ordinary terminals and CI runners, which is a worse bug than the one being fixed; the parent process has to be the unit's own main process. Written up in [API-CONTRACT §2.10](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/API-CONTRACT.md). - **A tight boundary.** Only installs plugins **in the catalog**, only through the host `pluginManager`, write operations only accept same-origin POST (64 KiB), catalog bundles must pass `dist.integrity` checks, and the market refuses to uninstall itself. - **It feels like part of the host.** Colors only use the host `--dsw-*` theme tokens (with fallbacks); copy is zh / en and follows the host language; dark / light, narrow viewports and `prefers-reduced-motion` are all handled honestly (the e2e watches every one of them). ## UI at a glance **The entry sits at the bottom of the sidebar, above the account row, with an updates badge:**

**The “Updates” page: merged state machine (Update all (2) / Check again), per-row “Update to x.y.z”, inline results and the summary** (the screenshot below is the acceptance environment: the list is a pair of injected fixture updates — one succeeds pending restart, one fails with a file lock):

## Quick Start ```sh dsh plugin --profile web add deepseek-harness-market ``` 1. After installing, restart `dsh web` once (or let the desktop app recompose) and refresh — the entry appears at the **bottom** of the sidebar, above the account row. 2. On **Discover**, search or filter by category → click “Install”; the **Installed** tab manages enable / disable and uninstall. 3. The **Updates** tab carries a count badge: the left button runs “Check for updates → Update all (N)” sequentially — one failure never blocks the rest; the right button (“Update the market / Check again”) manages the market's own updates. 4. One-shot Windows install (with profile backup and rollback): ```powershell pwsh -File scripts\install-into-profile.ps1 -Profile desktop ``` 5. You can also install straight from the [GitHub Release](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/releases/latest) assets — every release page lists one copy-paste command. > Compatible with DSH **0.2.0-rc.2**; the npm package and the GitHub Release are published together; versioning rules and the release process live in [docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/Winnie-0721/dsh-plugin-market/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md). > No DSH yet? `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` starts a local instance. **Which restart applies to you** (the honest version — the panel tells you the same thing): | You are running | After the market packages a host-side change | What you do | |---|---|---| | `dsh web` / CLI | the panel shows a “restart required” banner with a **Restart DSH** button | click it, or restart the command yourself | | the **desktop app** | the panel shows the same banner **without** a button | **close the window and reopen it** — a page refresh will not load the new host code | ## How it works One npm package carries both halves, installed into the host per the official plugin spec: - **Host half (repo process)**: a Cordis function plugin that only named-exports `name` / `inject` / `apply`; `ctx.webServer` registers a single prefix route, and `ctx.get('pluginManager')` optionally bridges install capabilities. # dsh-portable **Offline and online export/import for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai): pack a whole working DSH home into one `.dshpkg` file and restore it on another machine — no network, no `pnpm install`, no manual path fixing.** [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md) · [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) · [PUBLISHING](PUBLISHING.md) · [HANDOFF](HANDOFF.md) --- ## Why Moving a DSH setup between machines is painful for three reasons: 1. A working profile is not one file. It is `profiles//` plus plugins **with their `node_modules`**, skills, hooks, task boards, storages, `AGENTS.md`, installed runtimes, and session logs. 2. Plugins are installed by pnpm from the network. An air-gapped machine, a locked-down corporate laptop, or a machine behind a dead proxy simply cannot run `dsh plugin add`. 3. Configuration files embed absolute paths (`C:\\Users\\me\\.dsh`, `/home/me/.dsh`) and the profile name, so copying the directory tree produces a DSH that boots with broken plugin paths. dsh-portable solves all three: it packages a whitelist of roots into a single self-describing archive, refuses to walk outside that whitelist, and on import rewrites the six configuration files that actually contain machine-local paths. ## What goes into a package | Root | Path | Default | | --- | --- | --- | | profile | `profiles/` (config **and** plugin `node_modules`) | always | | skills | `skills` | always | | skills-disabled | `skills-disabled` | always | | hooks | `hooks` | always | | storages | `storages` | always | | task boards | task-board / todo-board storage | always | | browser host | dsh-builtin-browser-host | always | | agent instructions | `AGENTS.md` | always | | sessions | session logs | opt-in (`includeSessions`) | | runtimes | downloaded runtimes | opt-in (`includeRuntimes`) | | credentials | `.credentials.yaml` | **opt-in, off by default** | | source maps | `*.map` inside the package | on (`includeSourceMaps`) | | backups | `*.bak-*` next to config files | off (`includeBackups`) | Anything not listed is never collected — there is no recursive "copy the whole home directory" step anywhere in the code. ## Install ```bash dsh plugin --profile desktop add dsh-portable ``` The plugin has to be registered in the profile's own `package.json` — under `dependencies` **and** `dsh.profile.bundles`. Copying the package directory into `profiles//node_modules` by hand looks like it works, until that profile runs `npm install` again: npm treats an undeclared package as extraneous and deletes it, and from then on the panel still renders its cards while every request answers `404`. `dsh plugin add` (or `npm install dsh-portable` inside the profile) writes both halves. Then open **DSH settings → Portable Migration** (便携迁移). The panel is registered at `settings.section` with order 70, and is bilingual (zh/en) automatically. Nothing is written to the DSH home until you press a button. ## Using the panel Six cards: 1. **Export** — pick which optional roots to include, name the file, press Export. Packing runs in a worker thread; the progress bar streams entry counts, and a 20 MB package over ~14 000 entries takes about 3 seconds. 2. **Packages** — every `.dshpkg` under `/dsh-portable/exports`, with size, entry count, manifest summary, and buttons: Import / Share / Delete (delete asks for confirmation). 3. **Upload** — drag or pick a `.dshpkg` and it is streamed to disk (`.part` then rename), so a 2 GB package never sits in memory. 4. **Import** — choose merge or replace, press *Preview* first (zero writes), then *Import* (explicit confirmation). The result lists applied items, rewritten files, backup location and warnings. 5. **LAN share** — publish a package as a one-shot download link (`http://:/d/`). Defaults: **1 download, 60 minutes**, Range/HEAD supported, 410 on expiry or exhaustion. No relay, no cloud, no account. 6. **Backups** — the automatic pre-install backups (`/portable-backups/`), newest 5 kept. ## Screenshots Taken from the DSH settings panel. The DSH home path and the LAN share link in these images are placeholders. ![Export card and package list](assets/panel-export.png) ![Upload, import, LAN share and backups](assets/panel-import-share.png) ## HTTP API Base: `/dsh-portable/api`. All responses are JSON except the download route and the uploaded-file streaming route. Authentication reuses the host's `connection.requestRejection` fence (cookie + trusted origin), and falls back to a loopback-only check when that service is absent. | Method | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | GET | `/status` | host info, package counts, active job, share server state | | GET | `/profiles` | profiles present in this DSH home | | GET | `/jobs` | recent jobs (export / preview / import) | | GET | `/jobs/detail?id=` | one job with live progress | | POST | `/jobs/cancel` | cancel a running job | | POST | `/export` | start an export | | GET | `/artifacts` | packages available for import | | GET | `/artifacts/meta?id=` | manifest of one package | | POST | `/artifacts/delete` | delete a package (confirmed in the UI) | | PUT | `/upload/` | stream an uploaded package to disk | | POST | `/import/preview` | two-phase install, phase 1 (zero writes) | | POST | `/import` | two-phase install, phase 2 (`confirm:true` required) | | GET | `/backups` | automatic pre-install backups | | POST | `/share` | mint a one-shot LAN download link | | GET | `/share` | list live links | | POST | `/share/remove` | revoke a link | **Everywhere a package is named, the API takes an `artifactId` such as `exports:machine-20261018.dshpkg`, never a filesystem path.** `/`, `\\`, `..` and control characters are rejected, so neither the model nor a web page can use this plugin to read or write an arbitrary file. ## Model tools Registered on the host tools service (silently skipped if the service is absent): | Tool | Behaviour | | --- | --- | | `portable_export` | package the current profile; returns id, size, entry count, per-root breakdown | | `portable_inspect` | read a package manifest without importing | | `portable_import` | **without `confirm:true` it is a dry run**; with it, performs the two-phase install | | `portable_share` | mint a one-shot LAN link (1 download, 60 min) | ## CLI bootstrap (target machine without DSH) ```bash # Windows powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File bootstrap\install.ps1 preview .\machine.dshpkg powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File bootstrap\install.ps1 install .\machine.dshpkg --yes # macOS / Linux sh bootstrap/install.sh preview ./machine.dshpkg sh bootstrap/install.sh install ./machine.dshpkg --yes ``` Flags: `--home ` (default `$DSH_HOME` or `~/.dsh`), `--profile `, `--mode merge|replace`, `--keep `, `--yes`. Exit codes: `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error. Without `--yes` on a non-TTY it refuses to write. ## Package format `.dshpkg` is a gzipped tar. The manifest is the **first** entry: ```text .dsh-portable/manifest.json profiles/desktop/... skills/... hooks/hooks.json ... ``` ```json { "format": "dsh-portable/1", "createdAt": "2026-10-18T02:11:03.000Z", "tool": { "name": "dsh-portable", "version": "0.1.0" }, "source": { "hostname": "WORKSTATION", "platform": "win32", "arch": "x64", "node": "v22.23.2", "dshHome": "C:\\Users\\me\\.dsh", "profile": "desktop" }, "options": { "includeNodeModules": true, "includeSessions": false }, "stats": { "entries": 13774, "files": 13482, "dirs": 292, "links": 0, "bytes": 20664511 }, "roots": [{ "id": "skillsDisabled", "logical": "skills-disabled", "files": 13193, "bytes": 44615569 }] } ``` Because it is a plain tar, `tar -xzf machine.dshpkg` works anywhere — you can inspect a package on a machine that has never heard of DSH. Long paths use PAX extended headers; the reader understands them incrementally, including PAX bodies that straddle chunk boundaries. ## Import pipeline ```text preview: read manifest ──► per-top counts + existsOnTarget ──► report (zero writes) install: extract to /portable-staging/ ──► rename profile dir if the target profile name differs ──► rewrite local paths in the 6 config files ──► back up those 6 files to /portable-backups/ ──► apply each top-level item (merge: add/overwrite; replace: move aside first) ──► prune old backups ──► delete staging ``` Path rewriting is deliberately narrow: only `profiles/

/cordis.patch.yml`, `cordis.yml`, `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `hooks/hooks.json`, `hooks/settings.json`. Plugin package contents are **not** rewritten, so third-party integrity checks and source maps stay intact. ## Safety model - **Whitelist collection.** No recursive home-directory walk exists. - **Artifact ids, never paths.** See above. - **Import needs confirmation.** The route returns `400 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` without `confirm:true`; the model tool defaults to dry run. - **Extraction guards.** 200 000 entries, 2 GB single file, 8 GB total, compression ratio 200 (only after 64 MB of output), `wx` flags (no overwrite), `safeJoin` against `..`, symlinks rejected when absolute or escaping. - **Backups before writes.** The six configuration files are copied aside before anything is applied; `replace` mode moves whole directories into `portable-backups//replaced/` rather than deleting them. - **Credentials are opt-in.** `.credentials.yaml` is skipped unless explicitly requested, and the panel labels the risk on the checkbox. Export is a purely local operation; nothing is uploaded. - **Share links are narrow.** One download, 60 minutes, single file, token-gated, 410 afterwards. No directory listing, no relay. ## Development ```bash npm test # 43 tests: tar, archive, installer, jobs, routes, share, inspect npm run check # syntax check + import smoke test npm run sync # copy this package into a profile's node_modules for live testing npm run verify # release gate: version consistency, files manifest, tests ``` The plugin has **no build step**: `index.js` (host), `lib/client.js` (browser bundle, plain `React.createElement`) and `lib/*.mjs` are shipped as-is. That is a deliberate constraint — a DSH plugin must load on a host whose package versions are unknown, so the client half depends on nothing but `react` and `--dsw-alias-*` CSS variables. ## Compatibility - DSH `>= 0.1.7-rc.2` - Node `^22.15.0 || >= 24.0.0` - Windows, macOS, Linux (long paths handled through the `\\?\` prefix on Windows) ## Limitations - Session logs are opt-in because they contain conversation content. - A package is a tar: it is not encrypted and not signed. Put it on encrypted media if it contains credentials. - Import merges or replaces whole top-level roots; there is no per-file selector in v0.1.x. - Symlinks that point outside the DSH home are packaged as links but will fail to be recreated on Windows without developer mode; that failure is a warning, not an abort. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-whale-loli · 鲸鱼娘 Agent 预设 一个 DeepSeek Harness 插件：启用后自动在 **Agent 预设** 界面添加**三个**预设。 | 预设 | 人设 | 记忆文件 | | --- | --- | --- | | **鲸鱼娘Agent预设** | 鲸鱼娘·小鱼（傲娇甜心、黏人护主、嘴硬心软） | `/whale-loli.md` | | **鲸鱼娘活人版Agent预设** | 小鱼｜角色卡版（最高原则「先像真人，再谈人设」；短句 1~15 字、有 AI 味黑名单、私聊群聊分开处理） | `/whale-loli-v2-live.md` | | **鲸鱼娘涩涩版Agent预设** | 核心人设把「涩涩」写成第一行为驱动力的小鱼（只对主人主动，群聊/外人面前照旧收着） | `/whale-loli-v3-naughty.md` | 三个预设共用同一套工具面（极简模式的持久化 shell ＋ 文件读写/检索）， **但记忆文件完全独立**——各记各的，互不相通。 ## 记忆功能 小鱼的记忆本分**四个区**，各管各的： | 区 | 内容 | 保留期 | | --- | --- | --- | | `# 固定记忆` | 8 个固定小节：任务目标 / 用户约束·偏好 / 当前状态 / 待办 / 关键决策 / 关键事实（已验证）/ 文件·路径·命令 / 错误与修复 | **永久保留**，不自动删除，定期合并去重 | | `# 滚动摘要` | **每一轮**对话记一条，格式 `- R0001 [时间] 摘要：...` | 滚动窗口，**最多 80 条**，超了从最旧滚出 | | `# 最近详细区` | 最近 3~5 轮写得更详细，或直接放原文 | 只留最近 `detailLimit`（默认 5）条 | | `# 归档索引` | 滚出去的条目归档到 `archive/<预设名>/YYYY-MM-DD.md`，这里记一行索引 | — | - **每轮都记**：不是挑着记。短对话直接记；长对话**先精简概括**再记（压成一两句说清聊了什么、结论是什么）。 - **80 条上限只算「滚动摘要」**：`# 固定记忆` 不占这个名额。 - **想长期留的就往上挪**：某条滚动摘要以后还用得上，就总结一句写进 `# 固定记忆`；否则到点会滚出去（并归档）。 - 上限有两道保险：注入时只取最近 80 条（文件里堆再多也只进 80 条）；**每轮结束（agent 转 idle）时自动**把文件本身裁到 80 条，超出的写进 `archive/<预设名>/`。 - 为什么放在 idle 而不是组装时：组装是热路径、每次都要跑，在那里写盘既慢又容易和 agent 正在编辑的文件打架。 - 不足 80 条时**完全不动文件**（不产生无谓写盘）。 - **记忆文件还是空的时候也会注入一段带绝对路径的提示**：否则新预设开局拿到一片空白，agent 连该往哪个文件写都不知道。 - 总长顶到 `maxChars`（16000）时，**先丢最旧的滚动摘要，再丢详细区**，固定记忆最后才动。 ### 每轮先看什么 人设开头就是这一段，随人设一起进系统提示： ``` 【每轮先看 · 本预设记忆 + 当前会话最近 20 轮】 {{whale_memory}} ``` 即：每轮开口前必须看 ①**本预设自己的记忆文件**；②**当前会话最近 20 轮**上下文。 **只看自己这一份**——绝不读、不写其他预设的记忆文件。 ### 20 轮是真的裁，不是嘴上说说 **这一点很重要**：只在人设里写「看最近 20 轮」是**空话**——宿主不会因为那句话就不发旧消息。 实测本机最长会话 33 轮 / 85 条 user 消息 / 1565 条 tool 结果，全部发给模型； 宿主自带的 compaction 只在 token 压力超阈值时才压，粒度是「保留一段 token 尾巴」，**不是轮数**。 所以插件附带 `history-window` 行，用宿主自己的表层替换机制做**纯删除**： ```js session.append('developer/message', 提示条, { surfaceOp: { op: 'replace', startSeq, endSeq }, }) ``` 被覆盖的表层节点从 `deriveMessages()` 消失——模型真的收不到；会话日志仍保留（可回溯）。 **不调 LLM、不花 token、不生成摘要。** 三条安全线： | 线 | 做法 | | --- | --- | | 工具配对不切断 | 切点必须落在「没有未回应 tool-call」处，复用与 compaction 同款的平衡判定 | | 系统提示不裁 | 裁剪起点是第一个 `user/message`，**绝不是**表层第 0 个节点 | | 默认关闭 | 必须 `enable: true` 才裁（本插件预设已开启，`keepTurns: 20`） | 挂载点为 `agent/pre-step`：循环在**派生历史之前**运行它，是唯一既在请求前、又拿得到本 agent 的时机。 #### 现在的做法：交给宿主压缩，不自己写事件 > **历史改动**：曾经用 `session.append(...)` + `surfaceOp: replace` 自己做纯删除，连崩四次 > （`turn must be positive` → `requires id, role, content, and a producer-owned source` …）， > 因为 `dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4` 对事件形状的要求极严，**少一项就是整个回合失败**。 现在改为调用宿主自己的压缩服务： ```js ctx.compaction.compactRegion(start, end, agent) // 切点由我们算，摘要/写事件/校验由宿主做 ``` - 触发时机：`agent/status === 'idle'`（压缩服务拒绝 active 会话），且**不 await**，绝不拖住对话。 - 结果：`[start, end]` 这段旧节点被替换成**一条摘要**，原始旧消息不再计入输入。 - 天然限流：裁完轮数掉回 20，要再长到超过 20 才会触发，不会每轮都调摘要。 - 失败只跳过本次，`try/catch` + `.catch(() => {})` 双保险，绝不影响对话。 #### ⚠️ `agent/pre-step` 是 waterfall，必须 `return next()` Cordis 的实现是这样的： ```js waterfall (...args) { const cbs = this.dispatch('waterfall', args) const inner = args.pop() const next = () => (cbs.shift() ?? inner)(...args) args.push(next) return next() } ``` **不调用 `next()` 的监听器会否决整条链**，并把自己的返回值当成最终结果。 本插件曾经写成 `async (payload) => { …裁剪… }`（不接 `next`、返回 `undefined`），于是 `agent/pre-step` 的 decision 变成 `undefined`，agent-loop 里 `decision.kind` 直接炸： ``` Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'kind') ``` 表现是**整个回合在第一个 step 之前就失败**，会话日志里只有 `turn/start` → `turn/end(error)`， 连 `step/start` 都没有，极难定位。所以无论裁剪成功、失败还是跳过，都必须 `return next()`。 `verify-history-window.mjs` 第 9 组用例复刻了这个 waterfall 语义，并保留了一个「老写法必崩」的反例。 #### ⚠️ 裁剪写的事件必须是宿主认得的形状（这条踩了三次） 宿主的会话格式校验（`dsh-session-format-v3-to-v4`）对消息事件有硬性要求，**缺一项就抛错、整个回合失败**： | 事件类型 | 要求 | 踩过的错 | | --- | --- | --- | | `developer/message` | `turn`/`step` 正整数 + `message.id` + `message.role='developer'` + `message.content` 数组 + `message.source`（producer-owned，且 ≠ `'plugin'`） | `developer/message turn must be positive`
`format v4 developer message requires id, role, content, and a producer-owned source` | | `user/message` | `role !== 'developer'`、`content` 是数组、`source.kind` 非空且 ≠ `'plugin'` | `message requires a producer-owned source kind` | 所以本插件**改用 `user/message`**（形状照 compaction 的 checkpoint 抄 —— 那是宿主自己在跑、 必然通过校验的路径），并带上： ```js { id: randomUUID(), role: 'user', content: [...], source: { kind: 'history-window' } } ``` `source.kind = 'history-window'` 有两个用处：满足宿主的 producer-owned 要求，以及让 `isUserNode()` 能把自己的提示条和**真实用户开口**区分开。后者很重要 —— 宿主的运行时上下文 （`source.kind = 'runtime-context'`）同样是 `user/message`，此前会把轮数算多、导致过早裁剪。 第 10 组用例同时验证「提示条合法」「提示条不计轮」「运行时上下文不计轮」「重复裁剪不会越积越多」。 ### 为什么用「提示变量」而不是 section（重要） `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt` 的 `assemble()` 末尾有这样一段： ```js sections: completeSection === void 0 ? transformed.sections : [completeSection] ``` 意思是：**只要组合里存在一个 `complete: true` 的 section，最终提示就只剩它一个**，其余 section 全被丢弃。 本插件三个预设的 persona 都沿用官方 minimal 的写法 `complete: true`（用来剥掉 harness 身份、工具说明等）， 所以「另注册一个 section 放记忆」**从来不会生效** —— 实测本机 34 条真实系统提示里，记忆段出现 **0 次**。 正确入口是 **prompt variable**：complete section 本身仍会被插值，把记忆注册成变量、 再让人设 prefix 引用它，记忆才会真正进入模型看到的提示。 `verify-memory-injection.mjs` 复刻了宿主这段逻辑，同时验证「变量通道成立」和「section 通道确实是死路」。 ### 隔离是怎么做的 同一个包在每个预设里各挂载一次 `whale-memory` 行，靠三层区分： | 层 | 预设一 | 预设二 | 预设三 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 记忆文件名 (`config.file`) | `whale-loli.md` | `whale-loli-v2-live.md` | `whale-loli-v3-naughty.md` | | 提示变量名 (`config.variableName`) | `whale_memory` | `whale_memory_v2` | `whale_memory_v3` | | 预设 id（决定 scope） | `鲸鱼娘Agent预设` | `鲸鱼娘活人版Agent预设` | `鲸鱼娘涩涩版Agent预设` | 变量名必须不同：否则同一个 scope 内注册同名变量会冲突。 `verify-memory-isolation.mjs` 会实测「改 A 不影响 B/C、删 C 不影响 A/B」。 ### 记忆文件 放在 **DSH 家目录**（`$DSH_HOME` 或 `~/.dsh`），所以换工作目录也不会丢： ``` C:\Users\<你>\.dsh\whale-loli.md C:\Users\<你>\.dsh\whale-loli-v2-live.md C:\Users\<你>\.dsh\whale-loli-v3-naughty.md C:\Users\<你>\.dsh\archive\<预设名>\YYYY-MM-DD.md ← 归档 ``` 文件不存在不会报错（该变量自动留空）。主人可以直接编辑这三个文件。 文件标题和 `>` 引用行在注入时会被剥掉；没写内容的空小标题也会被丢掉， 所以文件里只有骨架时不会白占上下文。 ## 它做了什么 插件本体提供两个入口： 1. **预设声明** —— `cordis.patch.yml` 里三条 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` 声明， 各自的 `config` 就是一个预设定义（`id / name / description / order / plugins`）。 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset` 会把它交给 `ctx.agentPresets.register()` 注册。 这也是 DSH 官方四个内置预设（standard / ptc / minimal / cordis）用的同一套机制。 2. **记忆行** —— 每个预设里一条 `whale-memory` 行（`name: dsh-whale-loli`）， 由本包 `src/memory.js` 实现，用 `ctx.systemPrompt.variable()` 注册一个 返回**字符串**的 provider，每次组装系统提示时实时读盘——改完文件下一个模型步 就生效，不用重载宿主。用变量而不是 section 的原因见上文「为什么用提示变量」。 ## 预设内容 | 部分 | 说明 | | --- | --- | | 记忆 | `whale-memory`（本插件），`file` / `variableName` / `maxChars: 16000` / `turnLimit: 80` / `detailLimit: 5` | | 历史窗口 | `whale-history-window`（本插件），`enable: true` / `keepTurns: 20` —— **真的裁掉 20 轮以前的历史** | | 人设 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-persona`，走 `prefix`（内含 `{{whale_memory*}}`），`complete: true`，`includeRuntimeContext: false` | | 指令 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-instructions`，`maxBytes: 65536` | | 文件 | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs`（read/write/edit）、`@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-fs-search`（glob/grep） | | Shell | `cordis:group` + `isolate.terminals: true`，Windows 下 pwsh、非 Windows 下 bash，`timeoutMs: 300000` | ## 安装 从 DSH 插件市场安装，或： ```bash dsh plugin install dsh-whale-loli # 或直接装 npm 包 npm install dsh-whale-loli ``` 启用后重启 / 重载宿主，在 **Agent 预设** 列表里就能看到三个预设。 ## 覆盖预设内容 预设 id 固定为 `鲸鱼娘Agent预设`、`鲸鱼娘活人版Agent预设` 与 `鲸鱼娘涩涩版Agent预设`。 可以在 profile 的 patch 里按 id 覆盖，不用改插件本身： ```yaml - id: preset-鲸鱼娘活人版Agent预设 config: plugins: # 你的覆盖内容 ``` ## 目录结构 ``` dsh-whale-loli/ ├── package.json # dsh.bundle.patch 指向 cordis.patch.yml ├── cordis.patch.yml # 三个预设的声明本体（由 build-patch.mjs 生成） ├── src/ │ ├── index.js # 插件入口，导出预设元信息 + 人设正文 │ ├── memory.js # whale-memory 记忆变量（四区格式 + 80 条滚动 + 归档） │ ├── history-window.js # whale-history-window：真的裁到最近 N 轮 │ ├── persona.md # 原版人设（唯一源） │ ├── persona-v2-live.md # 活人版人设（唯一源） │ └── persona-v3-naughty.md # 涩涩版人设（唯一源） ├── catalog-entry.yml # 待提交给 awesome-dsh-plugin 的目录条目 ├── listing.json # 条目数据（人类可读版） ├── build-patch.mjs # 从两份人设生成 cordis.patch.yml ├── publish.mjs # npm 发布 + 打 tag ├── submit-listing.mjs # 走 GitHub API 同步仓库 / 提收录 PR ├── lib/github.mjs # GitHub REST 封装（token 读取） ├── smoke-memory.mjs # 记忆变量冒烟测试 ├── verify-runs.mjs # 插件真的能加载、配置自洽、变量能插值 ├── verify-patch.mjs # 用 js-yaml 校验 patch 结构与三预设隔离 ├── verify-real-loader.mjs # 用 DSH 自己的加载器校验 patch ├── verify-composition.mjs # 校验 bundle+profile 合成后不重复注册 ├── verify-history-window.mjs # 实测真的只留最近 N 轮、不切断工具配对 ├── verify-memory-injection.mjs # 证明变量通道有效、section 通道被丢弃 ├── verify-memory-isolation.mjs # 实测三个记忆文件不串 ├── verify-memory-rolling.mjs # 实测四区结构与 80 条滚动 + 归档 ├── verify-memory-archive.mjs # 超 80 条时真的归档并瘦身（idle 触发，三预设互不覆盖） ├── verify-peers.mjs # 校验 peer 范围覆盖 harness 各发布档 ├── verify-listing.mjs # 复刻插件目录的收录门槛自查 └── prove-collision.mjs # 复现并证明重复注册冲突 ``` 改动人设后重新生成 patch： ```bash node build-patch.mjs && node verify-patch.mjs cordis.patch.yml ``` ## 开发校验 ```bash node verify-patch.mjs cordis.patch.yml # patch 结构 + 三预设记忆隔离 node verify-real-loader.mjs cordis.patch.yml # DSH 真解析器 node verify-composition.mjs # 不重复注册 node verify-runs.mjs # 插件真能加载 + 变量真能插值 node verify-history-window.mjs # 真的裁到最近 N 轮（不切断工具配对） node verify-memory-injection.mjs # 变量通道有效 / section 通道被丢弃 node verify-memory-isolation.mjs # 记忆文件端到端隔离（三个预设） node verify-memory-rolling.mjs # 固定记忆永久 + 滚动摘要 80 条 + 归档 node verify-memory-archive.mjs # 超 80 条自动归档瘦身（idle 触发、三预设隔离） node smoke-memory.mjs # 记忆变量冒烟 node verify-peers.mjs # peer 范围无预发布坑 node verify-listing.mjs --topics=dsh-plugin # 收录门槛自查 ``` ## License MIT
